pages.title: Set / change password
pages.user_md:
## Set or change your password

You land here automatically on first login (or after an admin reset) — the app requires you to choose your own password before continuing. You can also open it anytime to change your password.

The rules shown live under the input (length, uppercase, number, special character…) are your company's password policy — the Save button won't pass until they're all met and both fields match. After saving you're taken to your home page.

**When to ticket:** you keep getting "Could not update password" even though the on-screen rules are satisfied.
pages.support_md:
## How it works

The page is a client echo of the tenant password policy (fetched via auth context); the SERVER is authoritative — the save goes through `POST /api/v1/core/me/set-password`, which validates against the tenant policy, sets the password via the Supabase admin API, and clears `must_reset_password`. It deliberately does NOT call `supabase.auth.updateUser` client-side, so the policy cannot be bypassed.

- Forced mode (`must_reset_password` true): login page redirects here and the title reads "Set your password".
- Policy is per tenant (edited at /admin/security). Hard cap: 128 chars regardless of policy.
- Signed-out visitors are bounced to /login.

## Symptom → diagnosis → fix

- "Password must be at least/at most N characters" mismatch with what user expects → tenant policy differs from their old company's — show them the live rule list.
- Save fails with a server error while rules pass client-side → client policy echo may be stale (admin just changed policy) — refresh the page; if it persists, check /failures for a Reference id and escalate.
- User stuck in a redirect loop between /login and /account/password → must_reset flag not clearing — escalate to platform operator with the user's email.

common_issues.symptom: New employee says their temp password/access code doesn't let them in
common_issues.diagnosis: Code expired, was retyped wrong, or a newer code was issued (newest-wins on resend).
common_issues.fix: Admin uses /admin/roles → Resend (re-emails a fresh code) or Reveal code to read the current one; hand it over securely.
common_issues.escalate_when: Resend repeatedly fails to email (delivery infrastructure) — platform operator.

common_issues.symptom: Password accepted client-side but rejected on save
common_issues.diagnosis: Server-side tenant policy is authoritative and may have changed since page load.
common_issues.fix: Refresh the page to reload the policy, retry with a compliant password.
common_issues.escalate_when: Compliant passwords still rejected — escalate with the exact error + Reference id from /failures.

pages.permissions_needed: Any signed-in user (self-service). No role needed — this page must work before provisioning issues are resolved.
related_settings: must_reset_password flag (set by invites and admin resets)

pages.title: Account Module (hub)
pages.user_md:
## Account Module

The home of your books. MetricsPro builds a **Profit & Loss** and a **Balance Sheet** from the data already in the system (sales, MI/ATU residual, distributor/VIP charges, commissions, payroll, store expenses, inventory) plus any manual journal entries you add. Statements are produced **per company, per store, and consolidated (all companies)** for the period selected in the top-of-section period switcher.

### What you can do here
- **Compute statements** — the big button rebuilds the chart of accounts and every P&L / Balance Sheet snapshot for the current period. Run it after new data lands or after you change a setting.
- **Consolidated tile row** — Revenue, Gross Profit, Net Income, Total Assets, and a balance check for all companies combined.
- **By Company / By Store tables** — drill into any scope's P&L or Balance Sheet.
- **Accounting settings card** — set this tenant's **Accessory COGS %** (default 20%). This is money-touching: after saving you must recompute for it to show on the statements.
- **Export** — the overview (Summary + By Company + By Store) exports to Excel/PDF and can be emailed/WhatsApp'd.

### When to open a ticket
- Statements say **"No statements computed"** and clicking Compute does nothing or errors.
- The consolidated numbers look wrong vs a statement you trust (a known-good month).
- The **"Claude narrative engine is not configured"** banner shows but you were told narratives are on.
- A company or store is missing from the By Company / By Store tables.
pages.support_md:
### Data sources & construction
- Router: `/api/v1/account/*` (the account router carries its own `/account` prefix; it is mounted at `/api/v1`). Backend: `backend/app/modules/account/**`.
- The hub calls `GET /account/overview/{period}` (per-scope tiles) + `GET /account/health` (narrative engine flag).
- **Compute** = `POST /account/compute/{period}` → `engine.compute_and_store` → `coa.build_inputs`. It writes one row per (statement_type, scope_key) into `commcalc.account_statements`. Statements are **stored snapshots**, not live — nothing on the P&L/BS changes until a recompute.
- Scopes: `consolidated`, `company:<id>` (from `store_companies`), `store:<canonical address>`. Stores roll up store -> company -> consolidated.
- **Multi-company + deterministic.** Numbers never originate from Claude; the AI only writes the narrative over already-computed figures.

### MUST-KNOW finance facts (apply across every accounts page)
- **Store canonicalization.** Every raw store key is canonicalized by `coa.store_resolver` -> `store_mapping.store_address` (address -> aliases -> code -> leading-number). This is what fixed "the same store appears twice." If a store shows up twice, or as a raw/ugly key, the cause is almost always a **missing alias in `store_mapping`**, NOT a bug in the engine — check aliases first.
- **Period-spelling duality.** Uploads store the period as either `"2026-06"` or `"June 2026"`. Filtering on only one spelling once zeroed the retail P&L. `coa`/`recon`/`residual` query **both** via `_period.period_keys`. A brand-new $0 line for a period that clearly has data smells like a spelling mismatch (data saved under a third spelling like `07/2026`).
- **PayGo is company-wide.** `vip_paygo_payments.dealer` is the VIP **dealer account** (one entity), NOT a store. It is booked company-wide (appears in Consolidated only). Treating it as a store once produced a phantom -$236k store scope. Do not re-scope it.
- **Accessory COGS default 20%, now per-org config.** `coa._account_config` resolves `accessory_cogs_pct` from `commcalc.account_config` (mig 611); 0.20 is the code default so a tenant with no row is byte-identical. The **Accounting settings card** here is the front-end for it (`GET/PUT /account/config`).
- **Residual = MI + ATU.** For Boost it reads `raw_mi`. For MA-report tenants (Total / luxelink) with NO `raw_mi` for the period, `coa`/`residual` fall through to `raw_ma_commission` + `raw_ma_daily_tx` (booked company-wide, MA rows carry no store). Source is chosen by which data EXISTS, never by tenant name.
- **AI narrative** needs `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` on the backend (set per owner 2026-07-14). Unset -> deterministic summary only; the numbers are unaffected.

### symptom -> diagnosis -> fix
- "No statements computed" -> the period was never computed (new tenant, or a fresh upload with no recompute) -> click **Compute statements**; if it errors, capture the message and escalate.
- A company/store missing -> stores unassigned or unmapped -> assign on **Companies**; if a store is genuinely missing it usually needs a `store_mapping` alias.
- Numbers look stale right after an upload -> snapshots are stored; the auto-recompute cron (`account-run-due`, every 15 min) or the Recompute button refreshes them.

### Escalation
Support staff resolve via **guidance + the config UIs** (Companies, Accounting settings, Journal, Inventory overrides). Anything needing **SQL** (store_mapping aliases, migrations), a **deploy**, or **approving a money-touching recompute** (COGS/booking-rule change) -> **escalate to the platform operator**.

common_issues.symptom: Hub shows "No statements computed for {period} yet."
common_issues.diagnosis: The period's snapshots were never built for this tenant (new org, or data arrived and nothing recomputed).
common_issues.fix: Confirm stores are assigned on Companies, then click Compute statements. Verify the correct period is selected in the section period switcher.
common_issues.escalate_when: Compute returns an error (500 / "compute failed"), or it succeeds but the tenant still reads computed:false.

common_issues.symptom: Yellow banner: "Claude narrative engine is not configured."
common_issues.diagnosis: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is not visible to the backend. Numbers are still exact and deterministic; only the written analysis is missing.
common_issues.fix: Reassure the user the statements are correct. Narrative is optional.
common_issues.escalate_when: The owner expects narratives on (key was confirmed set 2026-07-14) but the banner persists — the backend env/key needs an operator check.

common_issues.symptom: A store appears twice in By Store, or under an unfamiliar raw key.
common_issues.diagnosis: store_resolver could not canonicalize that raw store key to a single store_mapping.store_address — a missing alias, not an engine bug.
common_issues.fix: Identify the raw key vs the canonical address; add the alias to store_mapping so both fold together, then recompute.
common_issues.escalate_when: Adding aliases requires SQL / store_mapping edits the support role can't make — escalate to the platform operator.

pages.permissions_needed: Accounts/Finance module access (module key exposed via the plan's assigned modules). Compute + config saves are finance-owner actions; money-touching config (accessory COGS) changes are propose-first per the finance guardrails.

pages.title: Balance Sheet
pages.user_md:
## Balance Sheet

A point-in-time statement of **Assets = Liabilities + Equity** for the selected period and scope. Assets include Cash/bank (manual), on-hand Inventory value, inter-store receivables, and fixtures. Liabilities include Owed to Distributor (device financing), unpaid Distributor invoices, chargeback reserve. Equity includes owner capital and **Retained earnings** (accumulated net income).

### Reading it
- **Balanced badge / warning.** If Assets != Liabilities + Equity, a red card shows the imbalance and links to the Journal to enter Cash / opening balances.
- **Scope dropdown** + **Store/Market filter** work like the P&L. Note: a single store rarely balances on its own because cash and opening balances are company-wide.
- **Edit inventory** button jumps to the Inventory Values page.
- **Export** = multi-sheet (Statement Info + Balance Sheet + per-store Inventory detail), filter-aware.

### When to open a ticket
- The imbalance won't clear even after entering Cash and opening balances.
- The Inventory asset line looks wrong or is missing for stores.
- Retained earnings looks off across months.
pages.support_md:
### Data sources & construction
- `GET /account/balance-sheet/{period}?scope=&stores=&markets=` — stored snapshot, or the summed per-store aggregate when filtered.
- Line specs: `coa.BS_SPEC`. Assets: `cash` (manual), `inventory` (auto, store — effective per-store value from Inventory Values), `inter_store_recv`, `fixtures` (manual). Liabilities: `owed_vip` (Owed to Distributor), `vip_ap`, `inter_store_pay`, `chargeback_res`. Equity: `owner_capital` (manual), `retained` (computed = prior accumulated NI + this period's NI, via `engine._prior_accum_ni`).
- **Inventory line** uses the per-store **effective** value: manual override if set, else swept b2bsoft value, else asset-ledger on-hand fallback (see Inventory Values page).
- Balance check: `imbalance = assets - (liabilities + equity)`. Cash and opening balances are manual (Journal) — that's usually what an imbalance is waiting on.

### MUST-KNOW finance facts
- Multi-company: consolidated / per-company / per-store, same scope model as the P&L.
- **A store subset rarely balances** — cash/opening balances are company-wide; the page notes this under an active store/market filter.
- Store canonicalization via `store_resolver`; duplicate/odd store rows = missing store_mapping alias.
- **owed_vip (Owed to Distributor) is a real standalone liability** (~PayGo-pending owed) — do not zero it (it was wrongly zeroed once, restored 2026-06-25).
- Statements are **stored snapshots** — after editing inventory / journal / companies, **Recompute**.

### symptom -> diagnosis -> fix
- Imbalance persists -> Cash / owner capital / opening retained earnings not entered, or entered then not recomputed -> add them on Journal, then Recompute.
- Inventory line $0 for stores -> no swept value + no manual override + no asset-ledger fallback -> enter manual values on Inventory Values, or unblock the b2bsoft sweep (creds + mig 026), then recompute.
- Store-scoped BS won't balance -> expected (company-wide cash/opening) -> use Consolidated to judge balance.

### Escalation
Support: guide the user to Journal (cash/opening balances) + Inventory Values (manual overrides). b2bsoft credentials, mig 026, and store_mapping aliases -> platform operator. Recompute approval for a money-touching change -> operator.

common_issues.symptom: "Assets != Liabilities + Equity" warning won't clear.
common_issues.diagnosis: Opening balances (Cash, owner capital, opening retained earnings) not entered, or entered but the statement wasn't recomputed.
common_issues.fix: Enter the missing opening balances on the Journal page, then click Recompute on the hub/statement.
common_issues.escalate_when: The imbalance remains after correct opening balances + recompute — a booking-rule investigation (escalate).

common_issues.symptom: Inventory asset line is $0 or looks wrong.
common_issues.diagnosis: No swept b2bsoft value, no manual override, and no asset-ledger fallback for those stores.
common_issues.fix: Enter manual inventory values per store on the Inventory Values page and recompute.
common_issues.escalate_when: The b2bsoft auto-sweep is wanted (needs creds + mig 026) — escalate to the platform operator.

common_issues.symptom: A single-store Balance Sheet doesn't balance.
common_issues.diagnosis: Cash and opening balances are booked company-wide, so a store subset is expected to be imbalanced.
common_issues.fix: Judge balance on the Consolidated scope; the on-page note explains the subset caveat.
common_issues.escalate_when: Consolidated itself is imbalanced after opening balances are entered and recomputed.

pages.permissions_needed: Accounts/Finance module access. Journal + inventory edits and recompute are finance actions.
related_settings: Journal — Cash / bank, Owner capital, Opening retained earnings
Inventory Values — manual override / b2bsoft sweep (mig 026)

pages.title: Companies
pages.user_md:
## Companies

Define your legal entities and assign each store to a company. The P&L and Balance Sheet roll up **store -> company -> consolidated**, so this mapping decides how the multi-company statements group.

### What you can do
- **Add / edit companies** — name, legal name, EIN (inline).
- **Assign stores** three ways: per-row dropdown, **bulk apply** (set every filtered store to one company), or **assign multiple at once** (multi-select stores -> a company).
- **Filter** the store list by market or a store-name search.
- **Save assignments** persists the mapping. Stores you don't assign belong to the Default Company.

### Important
After saving assignments you must **re-compute statements** (hub) for the new grouping to appear.

### When to open a ticket
- A store you expect isn't in the list at all.
- Saved assignments don't change the By-Company statements even after recompute.
pages.support_md:
### Data sources & construction
- `GET /account/stores` returns companies + the store list; `GET /account/companies` returns full company records (legal_name/EIN). Assignments POST to `/account/companies/assign`; company CRUD via `POST/PATCH /account/companies`.
- **Store list source** = `store_mapping` UNION the tenant's sales data (raw_sales / daily_sales_feed), canonicalized through `coa.store_resolver`. This is why a tenant whose store_mapping was never populated (luxelink) still gets assignable stores from its sales — a mapped store is never duplicated.
- Mapping is stored in `commcalc.store_companies` (store_address -> company_id). No company assigned -> Default Company.
- Store selection is **pick-don't-type** (RULE THREE) — stores come from the existing canonical list, never a free-text box.

### MUST-KNOW finance facts
- Assignments only take effect on the statements after **Recompute** (stored snapshots).
- Store keys are canonical (`store_resolver` -> `store_mapping.store_address`). A store showing as an unfamiliar raw key means it has no alias yet — add the alias so the sales-derived key and the mapping fold to one row.

### symptom -> diagnosis -> fix
- Store missing from the list -> it has no store_mapping row AND no sales rows for the tenant -> confirm the store has sales data; otherwise it needs a store_mapping entry.
- Assignment saved but By-Company statements unchanged -> not recomputed -> Recompute the period.
- Same store appears twice in the assignment list -> canonicalization gap (missing alias) -> add the alias in store_mapping.

### Escalation
Support can add/edit companies and assign stores in-UI. Adding store_mapping rows/aliases (SQL) and the recompute approval -> platform operator.

common_issues.symptom: A store isn't in the assignment list.
common_issues.diagnosis: The store has no store_mapping row and no sales rows (raw_sales/daily feed) for this tenant, so nothing surfaces it.
common_issues.fix: Confirm the store actually has sales for the tenant; if it does and still doesn't appear, it needs a store_mapping entry/alias.
common_issues.escalate_when: Adding the store_mapping row/alias requires SQL — escalate to the platform operator.

common_issues.symptom: Store assignments were saved but the By-Company P&L/BS didn't change.
common_issues.diagnosis: Statements are stored snapshots; the new grouping isn't applied until a recompute.
common_issues.fix: Go to the Account hub and click Compute statements for the period.
common_issues.escalate_when: Recompute is blocked or a money-touching approval is required — escalate to the operator.

common_issues.symptom: The same store shows up twice with slightly different names.
common_issues.diagnosis: A raw sales store key and the mapped address didn't canonicalize together — a missing alias, not a bug.
common_issues.fix: Add the alias in store_mapping so both fold to one store_address, then reload/recompute.
common_issues.escalate_when: store_mapping edits need SQL — escalate to the operator.

pages.permissions_needed: Accounts/Finance module access with company-management rights.

pages.title: Inventory Values
pages.user_md:
## Inventory Values

The on-hand inventory value per store that feeds the **Balance Sheet inventory asset line**. Each store shows a **Swept** value (from the b2bsoft Inventory Aging portal), an optional **Manual override**, and the **Effective** value actually used (manual override wins; else swept; else the asset-ledger on-hand fallback).

### What you can do
- **b2bsoft connection** — enter the portal username/password, pick a frequency, enable auto-fetch, or **Fetch inventory now**. The password is stored backend-only and never shown.
- **Manual override** — type a value per store (and a note) to force the Balance Sheet figure.
- **Save overrides**, then re-compute statements so the Balance Sheet picks them up.
- **Export** the table to Excel/PDF/email/WhatsApp.

### When to open a ticket
- The b2bsoft fetch shows **error** / never runs.
- Swept values are stale or blank across all stores.
- Saved overrides don't reach the Balance Sheet.
pages.support_md:
### Data sources & construction
- `GET /account/inventory-values` returns rows {store, swept_value, manual_value, effective, effective_source, as_of_date, note} + total. `PUT /account/inventory-values` saves manual overrides.
- b2bsoft connection uses the commcalc sweep config: `GET/PUT /commcalc/b2b/sweep/config` and `POST /commcalc/b2b/sweep/run-now`. Credentials live in `b2b_sweep_config` (backend-only).
- **Effective** = manual override if set, else swept b2bsoft value, else asset-ledger on-hand fallback. This is the value the Balance Sheet inventory line reads per store.

### MUST-KNOW finance facts
- Editable b2bsoft inventory on the Balance Sheet is blocked on **b2bsoft creds + migration 026**. Mig 026 is RUN (manual values work now); only the auto-sweep needs creds, and the portal has an IP-block/2FA issue for headless login.
- After saving overrides you must **Recompute** for the Balance Sheet to update (stored snapshots).

### symptom -> diagnosis -> fix
- Fetch shows error / never runs -> no creds saved, or the b2bsoft portal IP-block/2FA blocks headless login -> manual overrides are the reliable path; the sweep needs valid creds + a trusted egress.
- Swept blank but manual works -> the sweep hasn't succeeded; effective falls back to manual/asset-ledger -> enter manual values.
- Overrides saved but BS unchanged -> not recomputed -> Recompute the period.

### Escalation
Support: help the user enter manual overrides and save the b2bsoft connection. Providing/validating b2bsoft credentials, the portal IP-block/2FA issue, mig 026, and recompute approval -> platform operator.

common_issues.symptom: "Fetch inventory now" errors or the sweep never populates Swept values.
common_issues.diagnosis: b2bsoft credentials aren't set/valid, or the portal blocks headless login from the datacenter IP (2FA / IP-block).
common_issues.fix: Save valid b2bsoft credentials; if the portal still blocks, use manual overrides which always win on the Balance Sheet.
common_issues.escalate_when: Credential/egress/2FA problems that support can't resolve — escalate to the platform operator.

common_issues.symptom: Manual overrides saved but the Balance Sheet inventory line didn't change.
common_issues.diagnosis: The Balance Sheet is a stored snapshot; overrides apply only after a recompute.
common_issues.fix: Click Compute statements on the hub for the period.
common_issues.escalate_when: Recompute blocked or a money-touching approval required — escalate.

pages.permissions_needed: Accounts/Finance module access. Saving b2bsoft credentials is a connector/config action (backend-stored secret).

pages.title: Manual Journal Entries
pages.user_md:
## Manual Journal Entries

The lines the engine can't derive from the data — Cash/bank, Fixtures, Owner capital, Opening retained earnings, income taxes, interest — entered per period. This is where you **balance the Balance Sheet** by entering cash and opening balances.

### What you can do
- **Quick add** common lines, or add a blank row.
- Each row: choose **P&L or Balance Sheet**, a **type** (revenue/cogs/opex/other or asset/liability/equity), an **account line** label, an **amount**, an optional **store**, and a memo.
- **Match a label to a statement line** (e.g. "Cash / bank") to fill that line; other labels appear as their own line in the chosen section.
- **Save entries**, then re-compute statements.
- **Filter** by store/market to focus the view (filtering never drops entries — Save preserves every row, including hidden ones).

### When to open a ticket
- A saved entry doesn't show on the statement.
- The Balance Sheet still won't balance after entering Cash + opening balances.
pages.support_md:
### Data sources & construction
- `GET/PUT /account/journal/{period}` reads/writes `commcalc.journal_entries` (org-scoped, per period). Only rows with a non-blank account_line AND a non-zero amount are saved.
- The engine maps a journal entry to a statement line by matching the account_line label to a line key (e.g. "Cash / bank" -> BS `cash`); unmatched labels render as their own line in the chosen section.
- A store-scoped entry (store_address set) attributes to that store's scope; blank store = all stores.
- The store/market filter is **display+export only** — `rows` stays the full save source of truth (index-preserving hide), so hidden entries are never lost on Save.

### MUST-KNOW finance facts
- **Period-spelling**: entries are keyed to the selected period; the engine reads both spellings — but enter under the period the section switcher shows.
- Statements are stored snapshots — **Recompute after saving** or entries won't appear.
- To balance the BS: enter **Cash** and **Owner capital / Opening retained earnings**. Retained earnings then rolls forward automatically (computed line).

### symptom -> diagnosis -> fix
- Saved entry not on the statement -> either the label didn't match a line (it appears as its own line in that section) or not recomputed -> check the section for a same-label line; Recompute.
- Entry saved to the wrong period -> section period switcher was on another month -> re-enter under the correct period.
- Entry seems to "disappear" when a filter is on -> it's an unattributed/other-store row hidden by the filter -> clear the filter; it's still saved.

### Escalation
Support can guide entry + balancing entirely in-UI. Only recompute approval (money-touching) or a booking-rule question escalates to the operator.

common_issues.symptom: A manual entry was saved but doesn't appear on the P&L/Balance Sheet.
common_issues.diagnosis: Statements are snapshots — no recompute yet; or the label didn't match a known line and rendered as its own line.
common_issues.fix: Recompute the period; look for a line with the same label in the chosen section.
common_issues.escalate_when: The entry is present in the section but the totals are wrong — a booking-rule issue to escalate.

common_issues.symptom: Balance Sheet still imbalanced after entering values.
common_issues.diagnosis: Cash and/or opening balances (owner capital, opening retained earnings) missing or entered under the wrong period, or not recomputed.
common_issues.fix: Add Cash + owner capital + opening retained earnings for the correct period, then Recompute.
common_issues.escalate_when: Imbalance persists with correct opening balances + recompute — escalate.

pages.permissions_needed: Accounts/Finance module access with journal-edit rights. Journal entries directly affect the statements (money-touching) so recompute is propose-first.

pages.title: Profit & Loss
pages.user_md:
## Profit & Loss

The cash-basis income statement for the selected **period** and **scope** (Consolidated, a company, or a single store). Revenue -> Cost of Goods Sold -> **Gross Profit** -> Operating Expenses -> Net Operating Income -> Other -> **Net Income**. Each line expands to its per-store detail where available.

### Reading it
- **Scope dropdown** (top right) switches between Consolidated / per-company / per-store.
- **Store / Market filter bar** re-attributes the statement to just the selected stores (it sums the per-store snapshots). With no filter you see the stored snapshot for the chosen scope, unchanged.
- **Manual / auto\*** tags mark lines that come from journal entries or a not-yet-fully-derived source.
- **Staleness banner** warns when your data is newer than the last compute — click Recompute.
- **Export** = multi-sheet (Statement Info cover + P&L + a By-Scope breakdown), honoring the active filter.

### When to open a ticket
- A whole revenue line (e.g. Device sales, Accessory sales, MI residual) reads **$0** for a month you know had activity.
- Gross Profit looks wrong after a COGS or classification change.
- A store filter returns $0 everywhere but the residual/MI lines.
pages.support_md:
### Data sources & construction
- `GET /account/pl/{period}?scope=&stores=&markets=` returns the stored snapshot; when stores/markets are passed it re-attributes via `statement_filter.aggregate` (sum of per-store snapshots — no recompute).
- P&L line specs live in `coa.PL_SPEC`. Revenue: `carrier_comm` (raw_comp_report, company), `mi_income` + `atu_income` (residual, company), `accessory_rev` / `device_rev` (sales, store), `vip_reimb`. COGS: `vip_device_pay` (PayGo paid), `accessory_cost`, `device_cost`, `vip_fees`. Opex: `rep_comm`, `wages` (StoreOps shifts x rate, or the exact `payroll_gross` line when present), `payroll_expenses`, `chargebacks`, `store_opex`.
- **Sales source** = `_sales_union_rows` = `raw_sales` UNION `daily_sales_feed`, deduped by trans_id (raw_sales wins). This makes GP correct whether or not the daily feed was promoted into raw_sales.
- **Device vs accessory classification** is config-driven: `commcalc.accessory_config` (mig 208) + `commcalc.gp_category_map` (mig 069). An empty config reproduces the historical Boost taxonomy (`DEVICE_DEPTS` / dept `Ondigo`) byte-identically. A non-Boost tenant whose POS departments differ and has NO map -> its device/accessory buckets fall to $0.

### MUST-KNOW finance facts
- **Period-spelling duality** (`2026-06` vs `June 2026`) is queried both ways. A sudden $0 line for a period with data usually means the data is stored under a third spelling or the store didn't canonicalize.
- **Store canonicalization** via `coa.store_resolver` -> `store_mapping`; an unmapped store is kept under its RAW name (never dropped), so it still shows — just not folded with its mapped twin. Duplicate store rows = missing alias, check before calling it a bug.
- **Company-wide lines read $0 under a store/market filter.** MI/ATU residual and carrier comp carry no store, so a store-filtered P&L shows them as $0 (there is an on-page note). See Consolidated for them.
- **PayGo (vip_device_pay COGS)** books company-wide — don't expect it on a single-store P&L.
- **Residual = MI + ATU**; MA-report tenants (Total/luxelink) fall through to `raw_ma_*` when `raw_mi` is empty for the period.
- **Accessory COGS** = accessory_rev x accessory_cogs_pct (default 0.20, per-org via Accounting settings).
- **Recompute after any config change.** The statement is a stored snapshot — a COGS %, a classification map edit, or a company reassignment shows only after `POST /account/compute/{period}` (Recompute button).

### symptom -> diagnosis -> fix
- Device/accessory revenue $0 for a non-Boost tenant with sales present -> POS departments unmapped in gp_category_map/accessory_config -> seed the tenant's department map, then recompute.
- Whole retail P&L $0 for a real month -> period-spelling mismatch or store canonicalization gap -> verify the upload's period string + store aliases; both spellings should be queried (they are).
- Store filter -> everything $0 except nothing shows -> the selected store's canonical address doesn't match a store: scope key -> confirm the store was computed as its own scope.
- Numbers unchanged after editing COGS/companies -> snapshot is stale -> Recompute.

### Escalation
Support fixes = guidance + config UI (companies, accessory COGS). Seeding `gp_category_map` / `accessory_config`, adding store_mapping aliases (SQL), and approving a money-touching recompute -> escalate to the platform operator. Do NOT unilaterally change the shared accessory classifier — it moves P&L/GP across ~8 surfaces; coordinate with mod-commission.

common_issues.symptom: Device sales / Accessory sales revenue reads $0 for a month with real sales (often a non-Boost tenant).
common_issues.diagnosis: The device/accessory classifier found no matching departments/categories — the tenant's POS departments aren't in gp_category_map/accessory_config, so lines don't classify.
common_issues.fix: Confirm sales rows exist for the period, then have the tenant's POS departments seeded into the category map; recompute the period.
common_issues.escalate_when: Seeding the category map (SQL) or the recompute approval is beyond the support role — escalate to the platform operator and coordinate with mod-commission.

common_issues.symptom: Entire retail P&L is $0 for a period that clearly had uploads.
common_issues.diagnosis: Period-spelling mismatch (data saved as e.g. 07/2026) or store keys not canonicalizing — the classic $0-retail-P&L pattern.
common_issues.fix: Check the period string on the source upload (should be 2026-07 or July 2026) and the store aliases; re-save/re-upload under a canonical spelling, then recompute.
common_issues.escalate_when: The period string is a third spelling needing a data fix, or aliases need SQL — escalate to the platform operator.

common_issues.symptom: A store-filtered P&L shows $0 for MI residual / carrier commission.
common_issues.diagnosis: Working as intended — those are company-wide lines with no store, so they are $0 in every per-store view.
common_issues.fix: Point the user to the Consolidated scope for company-wide income; the on-page note explains this.
common_issues.escalate_when: Only if the company-wide total itself is wrong in Consolidated.

pages.permissions_needed: Accounts/Finance module access. Recompute triggered from this page (or the hub) is a finance action; money-touching recomputes are propose-first.

pages.title: Distributor Credit-Memo Reconciliation
pages.user_md:
## Distributor Credit-Memo Reconciliation

Checks that the Distributor's weekly **"Weekly Incentive Credit"** memos equal the **MI + ATU** residual you actually earned for the period (Xfinity is a separate report, excluded). The authoritative check is company-wide; a best-effort per-store breakdown attributes MI/ATU to stores by rep name.

### What you can do
- **Company-wide tile row** — credit-memo total vs MI+ATU earned vs the difference, with a matches / underpaid / over status.
- **Tolerance** — set the $ threshold for flagging.
- **Scrape credit memos** — pull the latest memos using the stored Distributor portal credentials.
- **Analyze short days** (needs the AI narrative key) — buckets MI/ATU by day vs the memo range for flagged stores.
- **Write flags** — push discrepancies to Flags & Compliance (underpaid = critical, over = warning).
- **Export** the recon to Excel/PDF/email/WhatsApp.

### When to open a ticket
- "No Distributor credit memos loaded" and Scrape fails.
- Per-store attribution % is low and reps aren't matching.
pages.support_md:
### Data sources & construction
- `GET /account/recon/{period}?tolerance=&analyze=` (`recon.py`) compares `vip_credit_memos` (non-Xfinity GrandTotal) against `raw_mi` (actual_mi_payout + actual_atu_payout), company-wide.
- **Per-store attribution**: raw_mi has no native store column, so MI/ATU is attributed to a store via the rep name -> rep_commissions (rep -> store), canonicalized through the shared name_map/rep_aliases so the store lands in the same store_address space as the memo side. Labeled best-effort.
- `POST /account/credit-memos/sweep` scrapes memos using `vip_sweep_config` creds (backend-only). `POST /account/recon/{period}/sync-flags` writes to `commcalc.flags`.
- **Analyze short days** = one Claude call over flagged stores; degrades to nothing without ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.

### MUST-KNOW finance facts
- **Residual = MI + ATU** (recurring). The credit memos are weekly incentive credits reconciled against that residual — this is NOT the Comprehensive Comp / Total Compensation report.
- **Period-spelling**: recon queries both `2026-06` and `June 2026` via `_period.period_keys`.
- **Correct isolation for non-VIP tenants**: a tenant with no VIP data (luxelink) returns `has_memos:false` and the empty state — that's expected, not broken. A VidaPay/MA-equivalent recon is a future feature.
- Unattributed MI+ATU $ is still counted company-wide (the authoritative number stays complete); per-store attribution % just reflects how much matched a rep -> store.

### symptom -> diagnosis -> fix
- "No credit memos loaded" -> memos not scraped for the period, or no VIP data for this tenant -> click Scrape credit memos (needs Distributor creds); for a non-VIP tenant this is correct isolation.
- Scrape fails "credentials not set" -> `vip_sweep_config` has no portal_user/portal_pass -> set them on the Distributor sweep page.
- Low per-store attribution % -> reps in raw_mi not resolving to a store -> add the unmatched reps as aliases on the Rep Map (the page links to it); company-wide total is unaffected.
- "Analyze short days" does nothing -> ANTHROPIC_API_KEY unset -> narrative/analysis is optional.

### Escalation
Support: guide scraping, tolerance, rep-alias fixes (Rep Map is mod-commission's surface — coordinate). Distributor credentials and any flag/booking question -> platform operator.

common_issues.symptom: "No Distributor credit memos loaded for {period}."
common_issues.diagnosis: Memos not scraped yet, or this tenant has no VIP/Distributor data (correct isolation).
common_issues.fix: Click Scrape credit memos (needs stored Distributor portal creds). For a non-VIP tenant, confirm this is expected — the empty state is correct.
common_issues.escalate_when: Scrape fails because credentials aren't set/valid — escalate for credential setup.

common_issues.symptom: Per-store attribution % is low; MI/ATU shows as unattributed.
common_issues.diagnosis: raw_mi rep names don't resolve to a store via rep_commissions — missing rep aliases.
common_issues.fix: Add the unmatched reps as aliases on the Rep Map (linked from the page). The company-wide reconciliation is unaffected.
common_issues.escalate_when: Rep Map changes are outside the support role or need mod-commission coordination.

pages.permissions_needed: Accounts/Finance module access. Scraping uses backend-stored Distributor credentials; writing flags affects the compliance surface.

pages.title: Residual per Subscriber
pages.user_md:
## Residual per Subscriber

Shows **residual (MI + ATU) per paid subscriber**, per store, month over month, with a **commission overlay** — built to see the effect of lower commissions on the residual payout over time. A subscriber is a distinct phone number paid MI+ATU that month.

### What you can do
- **Range** (3/6/12/24 months) and **Metric** (residual per sub / total residual / subscribers).
- **Commission overlay** toggle plots commission paid on the right axis.
- **Market / store filters** re-aggregate the chart + matrix; **Break out by store** draws one line per selected store.
- **Export** the matrix (with the chart image) to Excel/PDF/email/WhatsApp.

### When to open a ticket
- The page is empty ("No residual data yet") for a tenant that has residual.
- A store's residual is landing in "(Unassigned)".
pages.support_md:
### Data sources & construction
- `GET /account/residual-per-sub?months=` (`residual_subs.py`). Residual = actual_mi_payout + actual_atu_payout per raw_mi row; subscriber = distinct phone number paid residual that month; residual/sub = Sum residual / distinct paid phones per store per month.
- **Store join**: raw_mi.salesforce_id -> store_mapping.salesforce_id (the clean join gp_report uses). Rows whose salesforce_id doesn't resolve go to an **(Unassigned)** bucket so the company total stays complete.
- Commission overlay = Sum rep_commissions.total_payout per month (per-store matched by street number).
- Aggregation runs in Postgres via `commcalc.residual_per_sub_by_store`; falls back to a bounded Python aggregation if migration 101 isn't present (page still works, just slower over full history).

### MUST-KNOW finance facts
- **Residual = MI + ATU.** For MA-report tenants (Total / luxelink) with no `raw_mi`, the residual aggregate falls through to the VidaPay MA tables (`raw_ma_commission` + `raw_ma_daily_tx`) — source chosen by which data exists, never by tenant name.
- This report is residual, NOT the Comprehensive Comp / Total Compensation report (that is ~76% promo + 20% bounty, $0 residual).
- Period spelling handled via `parse_period` (both spellings sort correctly).

### symptom -> diagnosis -> fix
- Empty for a tenant with residual -> no raw_mi AND no MA rows for the range, or salesforce_id join empty -> confirm residual data ingested for the tenant; for an MA tenant confirm raw_ma_* is populated.
- Residual in "(Unassigned)" -> raw_mi.salesforce_id doesn't resolve in store_mapping -> add the salesforce_id mapping so it attributes to a store (company total is already complete).
- Slow over long ranges -> migration 101 RPC not present -> Python fallback in use (works, just slow).

### Escalation
Support: explain the metric + point out (Unassigned). salesforce_id mapping, migration 101, and MA ingestion -> platform operator / mod-commission.

common_issues.symptom: Store residual shows under "(Unassigned)".
common_issues.diagnosis: raw_mi.salesforce_id didn't resolve to a store_mapping.salesforce_id, so it can't attribute to a store; the company total still includes it.
common_issues.fix: Add/correct the store's salesforce_id in store_mapping so the residual attributes to it.
common_issues.escalate_when: store_mapping edits need SQL — escalate to the platform operator.

common_issues.symptom: Page is empty for a tenant that should have residual.
common_issues.diagnosis: No raw_mi for the range and, for an MA tenant, raw_ma_* not yet populated.
common_issues.fix: Confirm residual data is ingested (raw_mi for Boost; raw_ma_commission/raw_ma_daily_tx for Total/luxelink).
common_issues.escalate_when: MA ingestion / data pull is required — escalate to mod-commission / the operator.

pages.title: Trends
pages.user_md:
## Trends

One place to see month-over-month charts across **residual per subscriber (vs commission), total expenses, commissions paid, and net profit (vs revenue)** — with shared range + market/store filters so you can compare the same subset everywhere.

### What you can do
- **Range** (3/6/12/24 months).
- **Market / store filters** re-aggregate every chart to the selected subset (default = company total).
- **Export** a combined trends summary (with chart images) to Excel/PDF/email/WhatsApp.

### When to open a ticket
- "No trend data yet" when you expect several months.
- The Net Profit chart says months are "computing" and never resolves.
pages.support_md:
### Data sources & construction
- Pulls four endpoints: `/account/residual-per-sub`, `/commcalc/expenses-trend`, `/commcalc/commission-trend`, `/commcalc/gp-trend`. Each returns company + per-store series; the page sums the visible stores when filtered.
- Net profit / revenue comes from the GP-trend, which reads the computed statements — a month with no computed statement shows as pending ("computing").

### MUST-KNOW finance facts
- Net-profit months depend on **computed statements** — an uncomputed/stale month won't chart until recomputed (auto-recompute cron or the Compute button).
- Residual line = MI + ATU per sub (same definition as the Residual per Subscriber page; MA-tenant fallback applies).
- Store/market filtering is client-side over org-scoped rosters — an empty subset is correct isolation, not a bug.

### symptom -> diagnosis -> fix
- "No trend data yet" -> fewer than a couple of computed months -> upload/compute a couple of months first.
- Net Profit months stuck "computing" -> those periods' statements aren't computed -> recompute the missing periods (Compute button / auto-recompute).
- A commcalc trend endpoint returns nothing -> that module's data/permission gap -> handled by mod-commission (expenses/commission/gp trends are commcalc endpoints).

### Escalation
Support: guide range/filters + recompute. Missing computed months (recompute approval) or a commcalc trend data gap -> operator / mod-commission.

common_issues.symptom: Net Profit chart shows N month(s) "computing" and never fills in.
common_issues.diagnosis: Those periods' account statements aren't computed, so the GP-trend has nothing to read.
common_issues.fix: Recompute the missing periods on the Account hub (or let the auto-recompute cron catch up).
common_issues.escalate_when: Recompute is blocked / needs a money-touching approval — escalate.

common_issues.symptom: "No trend data yet."
common_issues.diagnosis: Not enough computed history for the tenant.
common_issues.fix: Upload and compute a couple of months, then reload.
common_issues.escalate_when: Data is present and computed but still not charting — escalate.

pages.permissions_needed: Accounts/Finance module access (read-only report). GP/expense/commission trends also require the commcalc module.
related_settings: Computed statements (net-profit trend depends on them)

pages.title: Billing (Tenants)
pages.user_md:
## Billing (Tenants) — super-admin only

The SaaS side: price each **company/tenant** on MetricsPro by a **basis** (flat / per store / per entity / per user / per module / per carrier) x **cycle** (monthly/annual), see the live quantity drivers, generate invoices, and track MRR/ARR. It also tracks the **operator's own platform costs** (Anthropic, Railway, Supabase, Vercel, Bluehost...) to compute a **break-even per tenant**.

### What you can do
- **Set / edit a plan** per tenant: basis, unit price, cycle, currency, and which **modules** the tenant gets (all checked = full access; uncheck to restrict).
- **Generate invoices** for a period; mark them **sent / paid / void** (payments recorded manually; payment gateway is a later phase).
- **Platform costs** — add each platform's cost (live where a cost API exists, else a flat monthly figure). Total / active tenants = break-even per tenant.

### When to open a ticket
- The page says only super-admins can use it (you're not a super-admin).
- A yellow banner about migration `064_billing.sql` or `090_platform_billing.sql` not applied.
- A tenant's module restriction didn't take effect for their users.
pages.support_md:
### Data sources & construction
- Router: `/api/v1/billing/*` (own `/billing` prefix). **Every endpoint is gated by `_require_super_admin`** — this is cross-tenant by design (it bills every tenant).
- Plans/invoices live in `storeops.*` (migration **064**); platform connectors/costs in migration **090**. Live quantity drivers count real stores/users/entities/modules/carriers per org.
- **Module restriction**: the plan's `modules` array feeds the entitlement engine. The engine is **all-access by default** and `billing_plan` **restricts** — an empty/all-checked list = full access; unchecking a module hides it for that tenant on save.
- Platform costs: `platform_costs.py` pulls live cost where a provider has an API (Anthropic first); others use a flat monthly figure. Credentials are stored server-side, never logged.

### MUST-KNOW multi-tenant facts
- Billing reads the **target org from the request**; platform-cost figures use the house constant for the operator's OWN infra spend (correct — that's the operator's cost, not a tenant's).
- **New modules reach every tenant** via `seed_tenant_defaults()` + a **SEED_VERSION bump**. If a new default module was added but existing tenants don't see it, the likely cause is a **missed SEED_VERSION bump**, not billing.
- Never bill one tenant's figures against another — statements/quantities are per-org.

### symptom -> diagnosis -> fix
- "This page is for super-admins only" -> the user isn't a super_admin -> manage super-admins at /admin/tenants (not SQL); this is intentional.
- Banner: migration 064 / 090 not applied -> the billing/platform-cost tables don't exist yet -> the migration must be run (operator).
- Module unchecked but tenant still sees it -> entitlement not refreshed, or the module is a default not yet seeded -> confirm the plan saved; new default modules need a SEED_VERSION bump.
- Live platform cost shows 'error'/'not synced' -> provider credential missing/invalid or no cost API -> set a flat monthly cost as a fallback.

### Escalation
Support: only super-admins operate this page. Running migration 064/090, provider credential setup, and SEED_VERSION/entitlement issues -> platform operator (mod-platform-core owns the entitlement engine).

common_issues.symptom: "This page is for super-admins only."
common_issues.diagnosis: Billing is super-admin-gated by design (it prices/bills every tenant).
common_issues.fix: Grant super-admin at /admin/tenants if appropriate; otherwise this is expected.
common_issues.escalate_when: A legitimate operator needs super-admin and can't be granted in-UI — escalate.

common_issues.symptom: Yellow banner: migration 064_billing.sql / 090_platform_billing.sql not applied.
common_issues.diagnosis: The billing (064) or platform-cost (090) tables don't exist yet, so plans/invoices/costs can't be saved.
common_issues.fix: The migration must be run in the Supabase SQL editor.
common_issues.escalate_when: Always — running SQL is operator-only; escalate to the platform operator.

common_issues.symptom: A module was unchecked for a tenant but their users still see it (or a new module never appears).
common_issues.diagnosis: Entitlement not refreshed after save, or a new default module was added without a SEED_VERSION bump so existing tenants never got it.
common_issues.fix: Confirm the plan saved; for a brand-new default module, a SEED_VERSION bump + seed_tenant_defaults() is required.
common_issues.escalate_when: SEED_VERSION / entitlement-engine changes — escalate to the platform operator (mod-platform-core).

common_issues.symptom: Tenant billed for the wrong quantity
common_issues.diagnosis: Basis driver counts live objects (e.g. per_user counts logins) — the tenant's data changed.
common_issues.fix: Confirm the driver number on the plans row; adjust basis/unit price if the model is wrong.
common_issues.escalate_when: Driver number contradicts the tenant's actual data.

pages.permissions_needed: Super-admin (user.super_admin). Every /billing endpoint enforces _require_super_admin. Managed at /admin/tenants.

pages.title: Display Labels & Capabilities
pages.user_md:
## Display Labels

Rename any sidebar group or page for YOUR company ("Distributors"→"Suppliers") without touching code or data. Blank = revert to the built-in name. Display-only: never changes a route, table, or data path. Edits show on the next sidebar load.

Items that are carrier-gated also get a visibility dropdown: **Auto** (follow the tenant's carrier), **Always show**, or **Always hide** — the admin override for carrier-hidden pages.

**When to ticket:** saves fail with a migration message.
pages.support_md:
## How it works

Backed by `commcalc.ui_label_override` (migration 068). Reads `GET /commcalc/nav-config` (labels + capabilities), writes `POST /commcalc/nav-labels` (scope nav|group|cap). Capability overrides are stored as `carrier:<href>` keys. Renames apply on the next sidebar load; they do NOT affect permissions — a renamed item still needs its module key on the role.

## Symptom → diagnosis → fix

- Save fails mentioning migration 068 → `ui_label_override` table missing in this environment → platform operator runs the migration SQL.
- Renamed label not showing → sidebar not reloaded → refresh the page.
- Page hidden for a carrier tenant → Auto capability follows the carrier → set Always show here if the tenant needs it.
- User confuses rename with access: renaming/hiding here is tenant-wide display; per-ROLE visibility lives at /admin/roles.

common_issues.symptom: Item hidden via 'Always hide' but a user still needs it
common_issues.diagnosis: Capability override is tenant-wide.
common_issues.fix: Set the item back to Auto or Always show; use role permissions for per-person control.
common_issues.escalate_when: Override saved but nav unchanged after refresh.

pages.title: Menu Layout (sidebar designer)
pages.user_md:
## Menu Layout

Rearrange the sidebar for the whole company: MOVE any item to a different group, show a DUPLICATE copy in extra groups, HIDE items, create brand-new groups, and toggle whether the categorized "Reports ·" directory shows at all. Items you don't touch keep their default place, and newly shipped items still appear automatically.

A duplicate is a second link to the SAME page — it carries the identical permission gate (never a second permission surface). Picking a different group for an item asks explicitly: Move or Duplicate.

**When to ticket:** saved layout doesn't survive a reload.
pages.support_md:
## How it works

Saved per-org to `commcalc.ui_label_override` (scope='layout', key='__nav__', JSON `{items, groups, hideReportsDirectory}`) via `POST /commcalc/nav-layout`; applied on top of the built-in menu in (platform)/layout.tsx via `applyNavLayout`. Hiding here is tenant-wide DISPLAY — role permissions still decide who could see the item; hidden ≠ revoked. The hide-Reports-directory flag suppresses the whole categorized report shortcut section (owner directive 2026-07-18); default = shown.

## Symptom → diagnosis → fix

- "I hid a page but a user can still open it by URL" → expected: hiding is display-only; revoke via /admin/roles for real access control.
- Layout doesn't persist → save error (check the on-page message) or the backend stripped the payload → refresh, retry; if the Reports-directory toggle specifically won't stick, escalate to the platform operator (backend passthrough/deploy).
- Custom group disappeared → groups with no items persist only via the saved groups list — re-add and Save.

common_issues.symptom: Item appears twice in one group
common_issues.diagnosis: A duplicate ('also') entry targeting the primary group — the UI normally prevents this.
common_issues.fix: Remove the duplicate chip for that group and Save.
common_issues.escalate_when: Cannot be removed via the UI.

pages.title: Org Structure
pages.user_md:
## Org Structure

A configurable tree of org units (Company → Region → District → Store — levels are user-defined). Assign a manager to any node and they see every store + rep in that node's subtree; stores attach to a node and reps follow their home store.

- **Build standard org:** one click builds Company → departments → Sales → Region → District → Store from your markets/stores. WARNING: this REPLACES the current structure (levels, units, manager assignments).
- **Seed from stores:** lighter — rebuilds Company → Market → Stores, keeping manual placements.
- Per unit ("⋯"): add child, rename, delete (children too; its stores become Unassigned), move under another unit, set level, add/remove managers.
- **Manage levels:** add/rename/re-rank levels (Region, District…).
- **Unassigned stores** at the bottom: place each into a unit so subtree views work.

**When to ticket:** a manager placed on a node still can't see their team's data after re-login.
pages.support_md:
## How it works

Data via storeops org endpoints: `/storeops/org/tree`, `/org/seed`, `/org/build-standard`, `/org/units` CRUD, `/org/levels` CRUD, `/org/units/{id}/managers`, `/org/stores/{code}/unit`. Shipped with migs 050–052 (org hierarchy + manager team views + span enforcement).

**Support facts:**
- Org-tree placement is the CORRECT way to give a manager a multi-market or company-wide span — placing them at the root (or a high node) beats faking it with a market string. An "All Markets" market label on the user matches zero stores.
- A manager's visibility = the subtree of every node they manage. If they see nothing: confirm they're attached as manager to a node, the stores are attached under that node (not Unassigned), and they re-logged in.
- Deleting a unit orphans its stores to Unassigned — recheck that list after restructures.
- "Build standard org" is destructive to the structure (not to stores/employees). Prefer "Seed from stores" when placements must survive.

## Symptom → diagnosis → fix

- Manager sees no stores → node has no stores in its subtree, or the manager isn't on the node → attach stores/manager, re-login.
- Store missing from every view → it's in Unassigned → move it to a unit.
- Level dropdown empty → no levels defined → Manage levels → add, or run a seed.

common_issues.symptom: Manager can't see their district's data
common_issues.diagnosis: Manager not assigned to the unit, stores unassigned/misplaced in the tree, or stale session.
common_issues.fix: Assign them as manager on the right node, place the stores under it, have them sign out/in.
common_issues.escalate_when: Structure is correct and views stay empty — module owner investigates span enforcement.

common_issues.symptom: Someone ran Build standard org and lost the custom tree
common_issues.diagnosis: Build standard REPLACES levels/units/manager assignments by design (confirmed dialog).
common_issues.fix: Rebuild the custom parts manually; stores/employees themselves are unaffected.
common_issues.escalate_when: Never restorable by support — advise rebuilding; escalate only if data beyond structure seems lost.

pages.permissions_needed: Admin module. Underlying endpoints live in storeops (org units are shared with StoreOps).

pages.title: Employee Org Chart
pages.user_md:
## Employee Org Chart

The PEOPLE view of the org tree, drawn as a top-down graphic chart: each unit is a box (level, name, manager, people + sub-unit counts). Click a unit or person for a detail card; collapse/expand subtrees; the chart scrolls horizontally inside its own frame; Print/PDF exports just the chart.

Use it to place employees: anyone in the "unplaced" list can be assigned to a unit right here (managers are managed on /admin/org). Toggle to include inactive employees.

**When to ticket:** an employee refuses to stay placed after assignment.
pages.support_md:
## How it works

Reads `/storeops/org/tree` + `/storeops/org/employees` (optional `include_inactive`); assignment = `PUT /storeops/org/employees/{row_id}/unit`. An employee's effective unit is `resolved_unit_id` — explicit placement wins, otherwise they follow their home store's unit (`placed_by` says which). Pure HTML/CSS chart, no external libs; org-scoped by the tenant middleware (no explicit org in the calls).

## Symptom → diagnosis → fix

- Employee shows in the wrong box → they're following their home store's unit → either fix the home store (Roles/StoreOps admin) or place them explicitly here.
- Employee in "unplaced" → no explicit unit AND home store not attached to a unit → attach the store on /admin/org or place them here.
- Direct-report counts look wrong → counts derive from units the person manages (manager set on /admin/org), not the chart.

common_issues.symptom: Person keeps appearing under an old store's unit
common_issues.diagnosis: No explicit placement; they inherit their home store's unit.
common_issues.fix: Explicitly assign them to a unit here, or update the home store.
common_issues.escalate_when: Explicit placement doesn't persist across reloads.

pages.title: Roles & Access
pages.user_md:
## Roles & Access

The one page for who can see what: define roles, assign a role to every employee, and create their logins.

**Master switch — Login enforcement.** ON = everyone must sign in (users without a role + login are locked out). OFF = the app is open to anyone with the URL. Before turning it ON, make sure every active user has a role and a login.

**Assign people tab:**
- Every employee row: email, role, market, store(s) (floaters can hold several). An email is REQUIRED before a role can be assigned — the role assignment IS the login record.
- **Create login** issues an access code (emailed automatically when possible; shown on screen as fallback). **Resend** issues a fresh code (newest wins). **Reveal code** shows the currently-active code for troubleshooting (this action is audited).
- **Provision all** creates logins in bulk for everyone with an email + role and no login yet.
- Add a single person, or bulk-upload from the Excel template (Download template → fill → upload; optionally create logins in the same pass).
- Per-person dashboard **widgets** editor: override which Employee Dashboard widgets this person sees (inherits the role default otherwise).
- **Edit/remove:** Deactivate (reversible — marks inactive + revokes login) or Delete (permanent — removes employee, role, and login everywhere; history stays).

**Role permissions tab:** per role — module toggles, report access, sensitive-data grants, data scope (whole company / their market(s) / their store / self), home page, employee-dashboard widget defaults, and which Settings areas the role may edit. Quick-add templates exist for District Manager and HR. Save each role card after editing.

**When to ticket:** someone has a role but still can't sign in; a page you granted still doesn't appear after re-login.
pages.support_md:
## How it works

        Backend: `core/router.py` — `/core/roles` CRUD, `/core/employees` (StoreOps roster merged with app_users), `/core/users/assign`, `create-login`, `resend-invite` (rate-limited ~5/hr; returns 400 "already active" for an active login — use a password reset instead), `reveal-code` (super-admin OR own-tenant admin, audited as `code_revealed`; older invites where the plain code was never stored return `code_available:false` — use Resend), `bulk-assign`, `bulk-provision`, `employees/purge` (delete/deactivate). Login enforcement = `rbac_enabled` in auth-config.

        Role permission shape: `{ modules: {key:bool}, scope: all|market|store|self, home, reports: {area:bool}, data_grants, pages: {href:bool} per-page overrides, employee_widgets, settings: {area:bool} }`.

        **Key support facts:**
        - **A page missing from someone's sidebar = their role lacks that module key (or a per-page/report-area override hides it).** Grant it here and have them re-login. **Seeded role modules are FORWARD-ONLY:** when a new module ships in the seed, EXISTING roles never auto-gain it — a missing `modules.<key>` silently hides nav and redirects the page. (Real case: house market_manager lacked `closing` until manually granted 2026-07-21.)
        - **Manager sees empty data:** with scope=market, `app_users.market` must EXACTLY match `stores.market` (string equality). An "All Markets"-style label matches NOTHING — real all-market access = role scope `all` or org-tree root placement (/admin/org), never a fake market string.
        - **Report access defaults by scope:** company-wide (`all`) roles keep reports by default; market/store/self roles get none until explicitly ticked.
        - Assigning a role with no email fails with an explicit warning — email is the login key.
        - Access-code delivery: `delivery_status=sent` means emailed; `failed` means hand the on-screen code over manually.


**Account-linking privacy (hard rule):** NEVER disclose cross-tenant relationships. Do not confirm or deny that an email exists in another company, is invited elsewhere, or belongs to several tenants — not to admins, not to the user's manager, not in error messages. Invites are consent-based: the invited USER connects the company (with an access code) at their own login screen. If someone chose "Disable old login & start fresh", the old login can only be reinstated by a MetricsPro super-admin via support@metricspro.tech or the helpdesk.


        ## Symptom → diagnosis → fix

        - "I granted the module but the user still can't see the page" → user has not re-logged in (permissions load at login), OR a per-page override/report-area gate blocks it → check the role card's function list; re-login.
        - "New module exists for admins but not for role X" → forward-only seeding → tick the module on role X and save.
        - "Market manager dashboard is empty" → market string mismatch → set app_users.market to a value that exactly matches stores.market (pick from the dropdown), or use org-tree placement / scope=all.
        - "Create login says could NOT email the code" → Resend delivery failed → hand over the on-screen code; if all deliveries fail, escalate (Railway RESEND_API_KEY = platform operator).
        - "Resend invite errors with 'already active'" → the login is live; a resend would have silently reset their password (guarded on purpose) → use Security Settings "Set an employee's password" or a super-admin reset instead.
        - Role delete fails → role still assigned to someone → reassign those people first.

common_issues.symptom: Page/module missing from a user's sidebar
common_issues.diagnosis: Role lacks the module key — seeded modules are forward-only; existing roles never auto-gain newly shipped modules. Per-page overrides or report-area gates can also hide single items.
common_issues.fix: Roles tab → tick the module (and report area / page function if needed) → Save → user signs out and back in.
common_issues.escalate_when: Module is ticked, user re-logged in, page still 404s/redirects — possible deploy or entitlement issue for the platform operator.

common_issues.symptom: Manager with market scope sees no stores / empty reports
common_issues.diagnosis: app_users.market must EXACTLY equal stores.market. Labels like 'All Markets' match zero stores.
common_issues.fix: Pick a real market from the dropdown for the user, or give genuine all-market access via role scope 'all' or org-tree root placement at /admin/org.
common_issues.escalate_when: Market strings match byte-for-byte and data is still empty — data-side issue (store_mapping) for the module owner/operator.

common_issues.symptom: Employee row won't save a role
common_issues.diagnosis: No email on the row — a role assignment is keyed on email (it creates the login record).
common_issues.fix: Enter the work email in the Email column first, then Save.
common_issues.escalate_when: Email present and save still fails with a server error (check /failures Reference id).

common_issues.symptom: Access code was never received
common_issues.diagnosis: Email delivery failed or went to spam; the UI shows delivery status on create/resend.
common_issues.fix: Use Resend (fresh code, newest wins) or Reveal code (audited) and hand it over securely. Rate limit ~5 resends/hour.
common_issues.escalate_when: All code emails failing tenant-wide — Resend/env config is platform-operator territory.

common_issues.symptom: Turning ON login enforcement locked people out
common_issues.diagnosis: Users without a role + login are excluded once rbac_enabled is on.
common_issues.fix: Turn enforcement OFF (same switch), provision the missing logins (Provision all), then turn it back ON.
common_issues.escalate_when: The admin themself is locked out — super-admin resets via /admin/tenants.

pages.permissions_needed: Role with the 'admin' module (role management). Reveal code additionally requires super-admin or own-tenant admin (audited). Setting-area toggles govern which roles may edit which settings elsewhere.

pages.title: Security Settings
pages.user_md:
## Security Settings

Per-company security controls (read-only unless you hold edit rights):

- **Password policy:** min/max length and required character classes. Hard cap 128 chars regardless of settings. Applies to every password set in this company (self-serve, forced resets, admin-assigned).
- **Two-factor authentication:** off / optional / required (default OFF — no lockout). Allowed channels: email and/or WhatsApp. In "required" mode you may limit it to specific roles (none checked = everyone). Also sets the default country code applied to 10-digit phone numbers.
- **My two-factor phone (WhatsApp):** self-service — add/verify the phone that receives your own WhatsApp sign-in codes (send code → enter 6 digits).
- **Set an employee's password:** assign a specific password to anyone in the company; it must pass the policy; by default they're forced to change it at next login.

**When to ticket:** policy saves fail, or 2FA codes stop arriving company-wide.
pages.support_md:
## How it works

`GET/PUT /core/security-settings` (password_policy + twofa_policy; `can_edit` from the per-setting rights system). Self 2FA phone: `POST /core/me/phone` + `/core/me/phone/verify`. Admin password set: `POST /core/users/set-password` (policy-validated server-side, optional require_change). 2FA challenge at login: `/core/me/2fa/start|verify`, remember-device 30 days.

**Support facts:**
- 2FA is per-tenant policy, DEFAULT OFF. Email channel is confirmed working; WhatsApp shows "NOT yet live-verified" in the UI banner until confirmed — advise email as the reliable channel.
- Password policy is per tenant; the /account/password and login reset screens echo it client-side but the server is authoritative.
- Default country code fixes "WhatsApp code never arrives" cases caused by 10-digit numbers stored without +1.
- Editing rights come from roles.permissions.settings (SETTING_AREAS) — a user seeing "read-only access" needs the relevant settings grant on their role, not a bug fix.

## Symptom → diagnosis → fix

- Users complain new passwords rejected → policy tightened → show them the rules; this is expected.
- "Required" 2FA locking a role out → codes not arriving → temporarily set mode=optional, fix the channel (spam/phone enrollment/default CC), re-enable.
- WhatsApp 2FA codes not arriving → phone not enrolled/verified, wrong CC, or WhatsApp channel unverified platform-wide → enroll phone here; fall back to email.
- Save buttons missing → can_edit false → grant the settings area on the role at /admin/roles.

common_issues.symptom: Admin sees the page read-only
common_issues.diagnosis: Their role lacks the security settings edit grant (per-setting rights).
common_issues.fix: Grant the settings area to their role on /admin/roles (Role permissions → setting toggles).
common_issues.escalate_when: Company admin with scope 'all' still read-only — operator checks _can_edit_setting.

common_issues.symptom: Everyone hit with 2FA unexpectedly
common_issues.diagnosis: Mode set to 'required' with no role restriction (none checked = everyone).
common_issues.fix: Set mode back to optional/off, or check only the intended roles.
common_issues.escalate_when: The admin is locked out by their own 2FA policy with no working channel — super-admin/platform operator.

common_issues.symptom: WhatsApp sign-in codes never arrive
common_issues.diagnosis: Phone not enrolled/verified, missing country code, or platform WhatsApp channel unconfirmed (send-validity not live-verified).
common_issues.fix: Enroll + verify the phone in 'My two-factor phone'; set the default country code; use email channel meanwhile.
common_issues.escalate_when: Email works but WhatsApp fails for ALL users — WHATSAPP_* env / Meta template = platform operator.

pages.permissions_needed: Visible to admins; editing requires the security settings area grant (roles.permissions.settings). The 2FA phone card is self-service for the signed-in user.

pages.title: Support Console
pages.user_md:
**Support Console** — the house tech-support queue for escalated tickets from every tenant.

- Red SLA badge = overdue, amber = due soon.
- Open a case to reply (visible to the user) or leave an internal note (house-only).
- Resolving requires a resolution note.
pages.support_md:
Cross-tenant console (house-gated server-side via modules.support on a HOUSE membership or super_admin; tenant logins always 403).

WORKFLOW: queue → case → check the right-rail playbook + the tenant's Failure Log entries → reply (fans into the tenant helpdesk thread + email) or internal note → status new→in_progress→waiting_user→resolved(closed).

RULES: playbook first; empty ≠ broken under multi-tenant; config fixes are guidable, SQL/deploy/money-touching → platform operator; never disclose cross-tenant info.

common_issues.symptom: Console shows 403
common_issues.diagnosis: Login is not a house-org membership with the Tech Support module (or super-admin).
common_issues.fix: Grant the module at /admin/roles; log in with a house account.
common_issues.escalate_when: A house login with the module granted still 403s after re-login.

common_issues.symptom: Queue is empty
common_issues.diagnosis: No tickets escalated yet (normal), or migration 715 not run.
common_issues.fix: Escalate a test ticket from a helpdesk ticket page.
common_issues.escalate_when: Escalation succeeds but the case never appears.

common_issues.symptom: User never saw the support reply
common_issues.diagnosis: It was saved as an internal note, not a reply.
common_issues.fix: Re-send via the Reply box (visible-to-user).
common_issues.escalate_when: A visible reply exists on the case but is missing from the tenant ticket thread.

pages.title: Help Docs Editor
pages.user_md:
**Help Docs** — edit the per-page help shown by the "?" panel and the support playbooks.

- user_md = what everyone sees; support_md = console-only playbook.
- A doc keyed /commcalc answers for any /commcalc/... page without its own doc (longest prefix wins).
pages.support_md: Coverage view lists every page vs docs present (151 seeded). Docs are HOUSE-global with optional per-tenant overrides (tenant row wins for that tenant). Human-edited rows survive re-seeds (updated_by guard: seed only touches rows with updated_by NULL/'seed'). is_published=false hides a doc from the panel.

common_issues.symptom: Edited doc not showing in the "?" panel
common_issues.diagnosis: Doc unpublished, or a longer-prefix doc wins for that route.
common_issues.fix: Check is_published and whether a more specific page_key exists.
common_issues.escalate_when: A published exact-key doc still doesn't render.

pages.title: Company Setup (pay period & work-week)
pages.user_md:
## Company Setup — pay period & work-week

Defines your company's work-week and pay cycle ONCE; the schedule week, manager hours budget, and payroll all derive from it.

- Work week start day, pay cycle (weekly / every 2 weeks), payday day-of-week, and which payday after the period ends. Biweekly adds an anchor date for the 2-week grid.
- **Save & preview** recomputes the "Upcoming pay periods" table — tune the settings until the listed paydays match your real ones (e.g. Thu→Wed week paid the following Friday).
- Also hosts the **carrier picker** — selecting your carrier(s) shows only the app areas that apply.

Until saved once, the company runs on the default Monday week (a banner says "Not yet set").

**When to ticket:** the preview paydays can't be made to match your real cycle with any combination.
pages.support_md:
## How it works

`GET/PUT /core/tenant-settings` (mig 085): `work_week_start_dow` (0=Mon), `pay_period_type` weekly|biweekly, `payday_dow`, `payday_weeks_after`, `biweekly_anchor`. The response carries a computed `preview` of upcoming periods and `setup_complete`. Read-only without admin edit rights. The CarrierPicker writes the tenant's carrier set — carrier choice drives carrier-gated nav (see /admin/labels overrides) and commission behavior (non-Boost tenants pay ONLY from Commission Plans).

## Symptom → diagnosis → fix

- Payroll/schedule weeks look shifted → work-week start or payday settings wrong → adjust + Save, verify via the preview table.
- Biweekly periods off by one week → anchor date is on the wrong week of the 2-week grid → set anchor to a known real period start.
- Carrier pages missing/present unexpectedly → tenant carrier set vs nav capability overrides → check the carrier picker here and the per-item override at /admin/labels.
- Page read-only → user is not a company admin (expected).

common_issues.symptom: Payday in the preview is one week early/late
common_issues.diagnosis: payday_weeks_after off by one (first payday on/after period end vs the next one).
common_issues.fix: Change 'Which payday after the period ends' and Save; re-check the preview.
common_issues.escalate_when: No combination reproduces the real cycle — module owner may need a new placement rule.

common_issues.symptom: Commission pages absent after carrier change
common_issues.diagnosis: Carrier-gated nav follows the tenant carrier set; some pages are Boost-only by default.
common_issues.fix: Verify carriers here; use /admin/labels 'Always show/hide' override per item if needed.
common_issues.escalate_when: Override set and page still gated.

pages.permissions_needed: View: signed-in members. Edit: company admin (can_edit from the settings rights system).

pages.title: Companies (Tenants)
pages.user_md:
## Companies (Tenants) — super-admin only

Onboard companies onto MetricsPro and run platform-level account operations. Non-super-admins see an explanation card only.

- **Add a company:** creates the org, seeds its roles + modules, and provisions the first admin login (temp password shown once — hand it to the company admin; they reset it on first login).
- **Reset a user's password:** works for ANY tenant's user by email; sets a temp password and forces a change at next login.
- **Platform super-admins:** logins that bypass tenant isolation and see every tenant. Keep this list to internal operators. A row highlighted red holds platform access with a non-admin role — almost always a mistake to fix. Revoke removes the platform access only (the login itself stays).
- Per tenant: rename, activate/deactivate, and **Reset admin** (resets that company's admin login password; if the tenant has several admin logins you pick which).

**When to ticket:** a tenant reports every user locked out, or you need a disabled login reinstated (super-admin action, via support@metricspro.tech / helpdesk).
pages.support_md:
## How it works

        Endpoints (all `_require_super_admin`): `GET/POST /core/tenants`, `PATCH /core/tenants/{org_id}` (rename / is_active), `POST /core/tenants/{org_id}/reset-admin-password` (returns `needs_email` + admin list when >1 admin login), `POST /core/users/reset-password` (cross-tenant by email), `GET/POST/DELETE /core/super-admins`. Tenant creation provisions org + seeded roles/modules + first admin (must_reset on).

        The "Multi-tenant mode (this browser)" toggle only flips localStorage `mp_multi_tenant` for API-call scoping tests in that browser. Server-side isolation is `MULTI_TENANT_ENFORCE=1` on Railway — LIVE since 2026-07-04; the middleware rewrites org_id from the JWT; the super_admin column is the bypass. Manage super-admins HERE, not by SQL.


**Account-linking privacy (hard rule):** NEVER disclose cross-tenant relationships. Do not confirm or deny that an email exists in another company, is invited elsewhere, or belongs to several tenants — not to admins, not to the user's manager, not in error messages. Invites are consent-based: the invited USER connects the company (with an access code) at their own login screen. If someone chose "Disable old login & start fresh", the old login can only be reinstated by a MetricsPro super-admin via support@metricspro.tech or the helpdesk.


        ## Symptom → diagnosis → fix

        - Tenant admin forgot their password → Reset admin on the tenant row (or Reset a user's password by email). Temp password shown once, change forced at next login.
        - "Reset admin" asks which login → tenant has more than one admin login; pick the requester's.
        - Whole tenant can't sign in → check the tenant isn't Deactivated here; check their login enforcement + roles inside the tenant.
        - Someone can see other companies' data → check the super-admins list — revoke anyone who shouldn't bypass isolation; red-flagged rows (non-admin role with platform access) should be fixed immediately.
        - Deactivate vs delete: there is no tenant delete here — deactivate blocks access, reversible.

common_issues.symptom: Non-super-admin needs a company created or a cross-tenant reset
common_issues.diagnosis: Page and endpoints are super-admin gated.
common_issues.fix: Route the request to a platform super-admin (support@metricspro.tech / helpdesk).
common_issues.escalate_when: Always — these are super-admin actions by design.

common_issues.symptom: New tenant's admin can't log in with the temp password
common_issues.diagnosis: Temp password mistyped, or the auth user creation reported an error (auth_error note on the created card).
common_issues.fix: Run Reset admin for the tenant to mint a fresh temp password.
