common_issues.symptom: Checking 'Missing?' on a device doesn't seem to do anything here.
common_issues.diagnosis: It writes to a separate table (`commcalc.asset_investigation`, upserted by ESN/IMEI so it survives ledger re-uploads) and surfaces on the Missing Phones report — not visibly changed on this page.
common_issues.fix: Check the Missing Phones report for the flagged device.
common_issues.escalate_when: The device doesn't appear on Missing Phones after being checked here with no error shown. Escalate.

pages.permissions_needed: commcalc `asset` nav module, scopes `all`/`market`; nav-gated to Boost-carrier tenants only.
related_settings: 45/60-day bucket thresholds (hardcoded in router.py, not an admin setting yet)

pages.title: Aging · Rebate Received
pages.user_md:
## What this page shows
Devices still sitting in Inventory Aging (unsold, On-Inventory) but for which a Distributor rebate/reimbursement was already received — meaning they were effectively sold/activated and should be pulled out of inventory. Each is matched to a sale by IMEI. **REBATE, NO SALE** flags a rebate with no matching sale on record — the priority investigation queue. Filter by store (multi-select) and toggle "rebate-without-sale only".

## When to open a ticket
A device is flagged REBATE, NO SALE but you can confirm the sale actually happened.
pages.support_md:
## Data source
`commcalc.asset_ledger` (unsold On-Inventory rows with `reimbursement > 0`), joined to `commcalc.raw_payment_detail` by IMEI (rebate amount/date, summed across ALL periods) and to `commcalc.raw_sales` by `serial_1` (any matching sale). "Sale found" only checks that ANY sales-file row exists for that IMEI — it does not confirm the sale date lines up with the rebate date.

common_issues.symptom: A device shows REBATE, NO SALE but the sale definitely happened.
common_issues.diagnosis: The sales export (raw_sales) covering that sale's period may not have been uploaded, or the sale is recorded under a different IMEI/serial than what's on the asset ledger.
common_issues.fix: Confirm the correct Sales Transaction Details file (78-column, with Contract Type) has been uploaded for the period the sale actually happened, then reload this page.
common_issues.escalate_when: The sale is confirmed present in Sales data for that exact IMEI/date and this page still shows unmatched. Escalate.

common_issues.symptom: The rebate $ amount looks wrong.
common_issues.diagnosis: Rebate = sum of all matching commcalc.raw_payment_detail rows for that IMEI across every period, not just one month.
common_issues.fix: Confirm the ePay Payment Detail report has actually been ingested for this org.
common_issues.escalate_when: ePay data is loaded and the IMEI has genuine payment rows, but the total still looks wrong. Escalate.

pages.permissions_needed: commcalc `asset` nav module, scopes `all`/`market`; nav-gated to Boost-carrier tenants only.

pages.title: Inter-store Borrowed Money
pages.user_md:
## What this page shows
Tracks money one store borrowed from another to fund asset/device purchases — who owes whom, net position per store, and the full ledger of borrowings + paybacks. Record a new borrowing (pick a borrower store, lender store, amount, date, note — from dropdowns, never free text), then expand a borrowing to record or remove a payback. Filters: market, store, open/settled status.

## When to open a ticket
The store dropdown is empty when trying to record a new borrowing, or a delete needs to be undone.
pages.support_md:
## Data source
`commcalc.store_borrowings` + `commcalc.store_borrowing_payments` (both org-scoped). This is the ONE asset-domain page with **zero dependency on `asset_ledger` / the VIP financing program** — it is genuinely universal to every tenant regardless of whether they run Distributor consignment. Outstanding = amount − sum(payments). "Who owes whom" only lists pairs with outstanding > $0.005 (a floating-point-safe threshold). Deleting a borrowing cascades and removes its payments immediately.

## Store dropdown gap
The borrower/lender store dropdowns are populated from `GET /asset/filter-options`, which only returns stores that appear in `asset_ledger` — so a tenant with NO asset ledger data at all will see an empty store list here too, even though this feature has no real dependency on the ledger. This is a known gap, not a data bug.

common_issues.symptom: Can't select a store when recording a new borrowing.
common_issues.diagnosis: The store dropdowns come from asset_ledger's distinct stores (via /asset/filter-options) — a tenant with no asset ledger rows sees empty dropdowns here too.
common_issues.fix: None available today for a tenant with zero asset_ledger data.
common_issues.escalate_when: A tenant needs to use Borrowed Money but has no asset_ledger data (so no stores populate). Escalate as a feature gap, not a bug to work around.

common_issues.symptom: Deleted a borrowing by mistake and lost its payment history.
common_issues.diagnosis: Delete cascades payments immediately, behind a confirm dialog but with no undo.
common_issues.fix: Re-enter the borrowing and its payments manually from records.
common_issues.escalate_when: Never needed for this — it's expected behavior; just note it to the user for next time.

pages.permissions_needed: commcalc `asset` nav module, scopes `all`/`market`; NOT carrier-gated (available to every tenant).

pages.title: Charge Group Detail (Appeals & Denied Payments / Distributor Fees / Stock Balancing / Reconciliation Oddities)
pages.user_md:
## What this page shows
Line-item detail for one charge group reached from a Charges Dashboard tile (URL slugs: `appeals`, `vip-fees`, `stock-balance`, `recon`): Total Charges + Item Count tiles, a **By Category** breakdown (click a category to drill the line items below), a **By Store** breakdown, and the full line-item table (store, category, device, IMEI, date, owed, selling price, Distributor invoice #/date). The Appeals variant additionally shows a per-device **Reason** column and a red "Critical — money at stake" banner. Same period/market/store filter bar as the dashboard.

## When to open a ticket
An Appeals denial reason looks unhelpful/wrong, or the on-screen line items don't add up to the dashboard tile total.
pages.support_md:
## Two endpoints, one page
Reads `GET /asset/charges-summary` (group totals/breakdowns) and `GET /asset/charge-rows` (the actual line items — charges-summary is totals-only). `CHARGE_GROUPS` is the single source of truth for which `asset_ledger.category` values fall into each group.

## Appeals: there is no stored denial reason
The **Reason** text is derived at request time from the row's `category`, any "PN paid to ESN"/"Reimbursement on PN" fields captured in the raw uploaded row, and — when the ePay Payment Detail Report has been loaded for this org — the actual per-device Carrier payments joined by IMEI (`ePay paid $X (...)` or `ePay: no payment found for this device`), which is the true evidence of what was or wasn't paid. Without ePay Payment Detail loaded, only the category-based reason appears. The true detailed denial reason, if one is needed beyond this, lives in the Carrier's own Payment Detail report, not in this ledger.

## Line-item cap
The line-items table is capped at 2,000 rows per load for the current filter (the group summary/tile total is not capped — it comes from the RPC).

## VIP invoice join
Every line item is matched to its VIP invoice # + date via `vip_invoice_devices.SERIAL` (NOT `imei` — imei matches almost nothing; serial matches ~99.6% of asset IMEIs).

common_issues.symptom: Appeals 'Reason' column is generic and doesn't give the real denial reason.
common_issues.diagnosis: There is no true stored denial-reason column — this is a best-effort derived label. The actual detailed reason lives in the Carrier's Payment Detail Report (ePay), not this ledger.
common_issues.fix: Check whether ePay Payment Detail has been uploaded for this org (if not, the 'ePay paid/no payment found' evidence line won't appear). For a truly definitive reason, pull it from the Carrier's own portal/report.
common_issues.escalate_when: ePay Payment Detail IS loaded and the join is failing to surface any evidence for a device that should have payment history. Escalate (check IMEI formatting first).

common_issues.symptom: Line items shown don't sum to the dashboard tile total.
common_issues.diagnosis: The line-item table is capped at 2,000 rows per filter; the tile total comes from the uncapped Postgres RPC.
common_issues.fix: Narrow the filter (store/market/period) so the full set is under 2,000 items, or use Export to verify the full set.
common_issues.escalate_when: After narrowing filters below 2,000 items, the sum still disagrees with the tile total. Escalate.

common_issues.symptom: Distributor Invoice # is blank for a device known to be invoiced.
common_issues.diagnosis: The join key is `vip_invoice_devices.SERIAL`, not `imei` — about 0.4% of asset IMEIs don't match any VIP invoice.
common_issues.fix: Check the VIP Invoices page directly for that serial.
common_issues.escalate_when: A device is confirmed present on a VIP invoice (checked directly) but never shows an invoice # here. Escalate.

pages.permissions_needed: commcalc `asset` nav module, scopes `all`/`market`; the underlying charge groups only exist on the VIP/Boost financing ledger, so these pages are only meaningful for Boost-carrier tenants.

pages.title: RMA Reconciliation
pages.user_md:
## What this page shows
Returned devices (category = RMA) bucketed into **Not Reimbursed** (red, full loss), **Reimbursed Short** (orange, partial shortfall), **Reimbursed in Full** (green). A **Net Loss** headline = uncredited + shortfall. Filters: market, store, sold month/year. This RMA figure feeds directly into the Charges Dashboard's Total Loss.

## When to open a ticket
A specific device is bucketed incorrectly given its actual reimbursement status, or this page's Net Loss visibly disagrees with the Charges Dashboard's RMA figure.
pages.support_md:
## Per-device classification (`_classify_rma`) — this is the authoritative RMA number
`commcalc.asset_ledger` where `category = 'RMA'`. A device is:
- **none** — no reimbursement received (reimbursement ≤ 0 AND no reimbursement_date)
- **short** — reimbursed, but `reimbursement < owed_to_vip - $0.01`
- **full** — otherwise

Net Loss = `none.owed + (short.owed - short.reimb)`.

## Known discrepancy vs the Charges Dashboard
The Charges Dashboard's Total Loss RMA figure comes from a Postgres RPC that groups by `(category, store, market)` BEFORE bucketing — a coarser approximation flagged in migration 304's header. If a group mixes devices in different reimbursement states, the grouped figure can differ from this page's true per-device number. **Trust this page as authoritative for RMA** if the two visibly disagree, and flag the discrepancy rather than resolving it independently.

common_issues.symptom: A device shows 'Not Reimbursed' but a payment is known to have come in.
common_issues.diagnosis: Classification requires either `reimbursement` (amount) or `reimbursement_date` to be populated on the Asset_Lending upload for that device.
common_issues.fix: Confirm the source file has a reimbursement date/amount for that device; re-upload if missing.
common_issues.escalate_when: The source file clearly has reimbursement data for that device and it's still bucketed 'none' after a fresh upload. Escalate.

common_issues.symptom: RMA Net Loss here doesn't match the RMA figure on the Charges Dashboard.
common_issues.diagnosis: This page classifies per device; the dashboard's Total Loss uses a Postgres RPC that may group by (category, store, market) before bucketing — a known, documented approximation.
common_issues.fix: Trust this page's per-device number as authoritative for RMA.
common_issues.escalate_when: Any time this discrepancy is observed — flag to the platform operator so the RPC can be diffed against this page's logic; this is a known/tracked ambiguity, not something to resolve independently.

common_issues.symptom: A device sold/returned this month doesn't show under this month's filter.
common_issues.diagnosis: The month/year filter here is on `date_sold`, not `acquired_date` or `reimbursement_date`.
common_issues.fix: Check the device's `date_sold` matches the expected month.
common_issues.escalate_when: date_sold is correct for the filtered month and the device still doesn't appear. Escalate.

pages.permissions_needed: commcalc `asset` nav module, scopes `all`/`market`; nav-gated to Boost-carrier tenants only.

pages.title: Asset Charges Dashboard
pages.user_md:
## What this page shows
The top-level money-at-risk view: a **Total Loss** headline (denied Appeals + RMA net loss) plus 5 tiles — Appeals & Denied Payments, RMA Reconciliation, Distributor Fees, Stock Balancing/Returns, Reconciliation Oddities — each linking to its own detail report. A filter bar (All time / Month / Week-of-Friday, plus market/store) drives every tile. **Push Flags** manually re-syncs Appeals + RMA flags into Flags & Compliance. Exports respect the active filter.

## When to open a ticket
Any tile's figure looks wrong versus its own detail report, or numbers shifted unexpectedly after a system update.
pages.support_md:
## Powered by an RPC, not Python
Backed by the Postgres function `commcalc.asset_charges_summary` via `GET /asset/charges-summary` — aggregates in the database (never pulls all ~44k ledger rows into Python; that would take ~14s vs sub-second for the RPC).

## Charge groups (single source of truth = `CHARGE_GROUPS` in router.py)
- `vip_fees`: PROCESSING FEE, SHIPPING, SIM KIT
- `stock_balance`: Stock Balancing
- `appeals` (CRITICAL): Appeal Denied, Re-Escalation, Over 10 Days Missing Reimbursement, Missing 1st MRC, **Failed Activation**
- `recon_oddity`: PN paid to wrong ESN, No Elevate Data, Non-Promo coupon, Exchange/Return

## Total Loss ≠ sum of the 5 tiles (by design)
Total Loss = Appeals owed + RMA net loss ONLY. Distributor Fees / Stock Balancing / Reconciliation Oddities are shown for visibility but are never counted toward "loss".

## Period modes
All time / Month (`month`+`year`) / Week (a specific billing Friday via `week_friday` — the SAME `billing_friday` column used by Weekly Owed-to-Distributor).

## Migration 304 caveat
The RPC that powers this page (`asset_charges_summary`) previously existed ONLY in live Supabase with no checked-in migration; migration 304 is a reconstruction with an explicitly flagged ambiguity around RMA grouping granularity (grouped-then-bucketed vs true per-device classification). If Total Loss numbers ever shifted around when that migration ran, that's the place to look.

## Empty-ledger tenants
A tenant with no `asset_ledger` rows sees the shared `NoLedgerData` card instead of a misleading "$0.00 Total Loss" headline — intentional, not a bug.

common_issues.symptom: Total Loss doesn't equal the sum of the 5 tiles.
common_issues.diagnosis: By design — Total Loss = Appeals owed + RMA net loss only; the other 3 tiles are informational.
common_issues.fix: Explain the composition to the user; no change needed.
common_issues.escalate_when: The Appeals or RMA figures THEMSELVES look wrong (not just that the other tiles aren't summed in) — escalate via the specific tile's own issue path (Appeals detail page / RMA page).

common_issues.symptom: Charges Dashboard figures changed around when migration 304 was applied.
common_issues.diagnosis: Mig 304 is a reconstruction of a previously-uncommitted live RPC, with a flagged unconfirmed ambiguity in RMA grouping granularity.
common_issues.fix: None from support staff — requires comparing pg_get_functiondef output before/after against the migration file.
common_issues.escalate_when: Any time this is observed — escalate to the platform operator immediately; do not assume either the before or after number is correct without that comparison.

common_issues.symptom: 'Push Flags' doesn't seem to change anything on the Flags page.
common_issues.diagnosis: It re-syncs Appeal + RMA flags only (delete-first by source, then re-insert) — if underlying charge counts haven't changed, the flags list will look identical.
common_issues.fix: Check the Flags & Compliance page for a fresh updated timestamp on `asset_appeal`/`asset_rma` sourced entries.
common_issues.escalate_when: The sync reports success but Flags & Compliance shows stale or missing entries. Escalate.

pages.permissions_needed: commcalc `asset` nav module, scopes `all`/`market`; nav-gated to Boost-carrier tenants only.
related_settings: CHARGE_GROUPS category mapping (hardcoded in router.py, not yet an admin-configurable table)

pages.title: Hotsheet Recon — Expected vs Paid
pages.user_md:
## What this page shows
For every ACTIVATED device (unsold On-Inventory is excluded), compares the EXPECTED promo amount from the pricing hotsheet (by device model, effective as of the acquired date, on the promo column chosen by contract type: **Upgrade > AAL > Port-In > Non-Port**) against the ACTUAL Carrier reimbursement. Buckets: Matched / Underpaid / Overpaid / Not on hotsheet / Unmapped type. **Sync underpaid → Flags** writes a flag per currently-underpaid device. Data-quality panels list device models missing from the hotsheet and contract types with no promo mapping. Filters: market, store, acquired month/year, $ tolerance.

## When to open a ticket
A device's expected/actual comparison looks wrong even after you've checked the hotsheet data itself against a real current hotsheet document.
pages.support_md:
## Two UNCONFIRMED assumptions — flag before trusting the numbers
Per the module handoff, this reconciliation has never been verified against a real hotsheet on two points: (1) the contract_type → promo-column precedence (Upgrade > AAL > Port-In > Non-Port — the one business assumption in `_promo_type`), and (2) whether the $ amounts actually loaded into `commcalc.hotsheet` are correct. Treat any surprising Underpaid/Overpaid result as a data-verification question first, not necessarily a system bug.

## Matching logic
Joins `commcalc.asset_ledger` to `commcalc.hotsheet` by normalized `device_model` (`_norm_model` — exact match after case/whitespace normalization) + the latest hotsheet row effective on/before `acquired_date` (falls back to the earliest hotsheet row if the device predates all of them).

## Empty-ledger tenants
The "No hotsheet loaded" warning and the underpaid/overpaid math are both replaced by the shared `NoLedgerData` empty state for a tenant with zero `asset_ledger` rows — there's nothing to reconcile, not a broken hotsheet.

common_issues.symptom: A device is bucketed Underpaid/Overpaid but the promo amount looks wrong.
common_issues.diagnosis: This whole reconciliation rests on two unconfirmed assumptions (see Support notes) — the contract-type precedence and the hotsheet $ amounts themselves.
common_issues.fix: Verify the hotsheet's promo columns for that device model/effective date against a REAL current hotsheet document before assuming the reconciliation math is at fault.
common_issues.escalate_when: The hotsheet data and precedence both check out and the bucket still looks wrong for a specific device. Escalate with the device's contract_type + acquired_date + hotsheet row.

common_issues.symptom: 'Not on hotsheet' count is high.
common_issues.diagnosis: Matching is exact (case/whitespace-normalized) between asset_ledger.device_model and hotsheet.device_model — any spelling drift between the two sources yields zero matches for that model.
common_issues.fix: Check the 'Device models not on any hotsheet' data-quality panel at the bottom of the page and align naming between the two sources.
common_issues.escalate_when: Model names look identical between the two sources and still don't match. Escalate (may be trailing whitespace/hidden characters).

common_issues.symptom: 'Unmapped type' count is high.
common_issues.diagnosis: contract_type doesn't contain 'upgrade'/'add a line'/'aal'/'port' — check the 'Contract types with no promo mapping' panel.
common_issues.fix: Confirm with the user whether these represent a legitimate contract type that needs a new mapping added.
common_issues.escalate_when: A common, valid contract type is landing in unmapped. Escalate as a mapping gap.

common_issues.symptom: 'Sync underpaid → Flags' seems to have written nothing.
common_issues.diagnosis: It only syncs devices currently in the Underpaid bucket at the CURRENT $ tolerance — raising the tolerance moves borderline devices out of Underpaid into Matched.
common_issues.fix: Check the tolerance value and the on-screen Underpaid count before syncing.
common_issues.escalate_when: Underpaid count is clearly >0 and sync still reports 0 flags written. Escalate.

pages.permissions_needed: In the nav config this page is filed under module `commissions` (Pricing Hotsheet, alongside the Commissions area) rather than `asset`, but the underlying report permission area is still `assets`. Scopes `all`/`market`; nav-gated to Boost-carrier tenants only.
related_settings: commcalc.hotsheet (pricing hotsheet upload, on the Commissions page)

pages.title: On-Inventory ↔ b2bsoft Recon
pages.user_md:
## What this page shows
Compares Asset On-Inventory device counts (classified into iPhone/Android/Tablet/Watch/Hotspot) against a manually-uploaded b2bsoft "Inventory Aging" export, per store — each cell shows `asset / b2b` with mismatches highlighted. Upload a b2bsoft export (optionally with a $ value column) to refresh the snapshot; **Sync mismatches to Flags** writes per-store/category discrepancies into Flags & Compliance.

## When to open a ticket
Rows are being skipped on upload that shouldn't be, or the Balance Sheet inventory value still looks wrong after uploading a file with a $ column.
pages.support_md:
## Two independent things happen on one upload
**Asset side**: `commcalc.asset_ledger` (unsold On-Inventory), classified via keyword matching on `device_model` (e.g. "iphone" in the model name → iphone bucket; see `INV_BUCKETS`/`_inv_bucket`).
**b2bsoft side**: `commcalc.b2b_inventory`, populated ONLY via manual upload here — the automatic wsreports.b2bsoft.com portal sweep is NOT wired yet (`login()`/`fetch_inventory_aging()` in `commcalc/b2b_sweep.py` are still stubs, mod-commission-owned).

If the uploaded file ALSO has a $ value/cost column, this same upload writes to `commcalc.inventory_value` (org+store scoped, canonicalized through `store_mapping`) — which is what feeds the Balance Sheet's inventory line on the finance-owned Account module. This value-write is independent of category/qty matching (an unmatched category like "Accessory" still counts toward the store's $ value) and independent of whether `asset_ledger` has any VIP-financing rows at all — genuinely universal.

common_issues.symptom: Rows are reported skipped on upload.
common_issues.diagnosis: A row is skipped from the qty/category recon if it has no store, no recognized category, or a non-numeric qty — but if that same row HAS a $ value, the value is still written to inventory_value independently.
common_issues.fix: Check the skipped-row detail in the upload response; align the source export's category naming with a recognizable device-type keyword if it's a real device that should have counted.
common_issues.escalate_when: A clearly-a-phone row (e.g. 'iPhone 15') is being skipped and the category text looks normal. Escalate — likely a keyword-matching gap in the classifier.

common_issues.symptom: Balance Sheet inventory value still looks wrong/near-zero after uploading here.
common_issues.diagnosis: The $ value write only happens if the uploaded file HAD a value/cost column — a plain qty-only b2bsoft export writes zero dollars.
common_issues.fix: Re-export from b2bsoft/POS including a cost/retail column, then re-upload.
common_issues.escalate_when: A file WITH a value column was uploaded and the Balance Sheet still doesn't reflect it. Escalate to mod-finance/platform operator — the Balance Sheet page itself is finance-owned, outside this page's file ownership.

common_issues.symptom: 'Sync mismatches to Flags' button is disabled.
common_issues.diagnosis: It's disabled until a b2bsoft snapshot has been loaded.
common_issues.fix: Upload a b2bsoft Inventory Aging export first.
common_issues.escalate_when: A snapshot is loaded and the button is still disabled. Escalate.

pages.permissions_needed: commcalc `asset` nav module, scopes `all`/`market`; NOT carrier-gated (available to every tenant).

pages.title: Asset Lending (Distributor PayGo)
pages.user_md:
## What this page shows
The weekly lent-device billing ledger from the Distributor's PayGo consignment portal — Outstanding now (the current open/pending week), lifetime billed, by-year and by-month rollups, and the full weekly batch list. A funding-recon panel tracks HOW each week's bill was paid (own account vs a borrowed account) against the consignment distributor. Read-only report plus a small funding-entry form. Filter by year.

## When to open a ticket
The 'Outstanding now' figure looks like it's double-counting something you see on another asset/finance report.
pages.support_md:
## Backend is mod-commission-owned, page is asset-owned
Data comes from `commcalc.vip_paygo_payments` via the commcalc module's `GET /vip/paygo/summary` endpoint — this page's own asset router does NOT own this endpoint (cross-module read). Degrades to `configured:false` (not an error) if there are no PayGo batches for this org.

## Do not touch the PayGo-pending liability figure
The current outstanding/pending week is a **REAL liability** (~$121k company-wide historically) — it is NOT a double-count of `asset_ledger`'s own `owed_to_vip` totals or the VIP-invoices-AP figures shown elsewhere. A prior commit wrongly zeroed this figure out and it had to be restored. Never zero, net, or 'de-duplicate' it without the owner's explicit sign-off — these are three genuinely separate money views (weekly PayGo lending vs per-device financing vs invoiced AP).

## Funding recon
Recorded against whichever `commcalc.distributors` row is flagged `has_asset_lending` / matches 'VIP' — writes to `commcalc.distributor_payments`.

common_issues.symptom: 'Distributor PayGo lending isn't configured yet (no batches found)'.
common_issues.diagnosis: The correct empty state for a tenant that doesn't run the PayGo/consignment asset-lending program (also nav-gated to Boost-carrier tenants and behind the `asset_lending` capability flag).
common_issues.fix: No fix needed if this tenant doesn't run that program.
common_issues.escalate_when: A tenant known to run PayGo lending sees this empty state. Escalate.

common_issues.symptom: 'No consignment distributor found' banner in the funding-recon panel.
common_issues.diagnosis: No row in commcalc.distributors is flagged has_asset_lending / portal_provider='vip' / named 'VIP' for this org.
common_issues.fix: Add/configure the Distributor entry on the Distributors page (outside this page's own file ownership — commission/finance area).
common_issues.escalate_when: A distributor entry exists but still isn't being picked up. Escalate.

common_issues.symptom: 'Outstanding now' figure seems double-counted against another asset/finance number.
common_issues.diagnosis: It is explicitly NOT a duplicate of asset_ledger's owed_to_vip or the VIP-invoices figures — three genuinely separate money views.
common_issues.fix: Do not net these together or 'correct' this figure down.
common_issues.escalate_when: Never resolve this by editing the number yourself. If a genuine double-count is suspected, escalate to the owner/platform operator — this exact figure was wrongly zeroed once before and had to be restored.

pages.permissions_needed: commcalc `asset` nav module, scopes `all`/`market`, capability `asset_lending` must be enabled for the tenant; nav-gated to Boost-carrier tenants only.

pages.title: Marketplace Purchases
pages.user_md:
## What this page shows
Per-order purchase history from the VidaPay "MA - Marketplace Handset Fulfillment Orders" report — date ordered/filled/shipped, order #, status, order type, business/store, product, quantity, price, tracking #. Filters are dropdowns fed from the real data (business, status, order type — never free text) plus a date-ordered range.

This is the one asset-domain report that applies to non-VIP/non-Boost tenants (e.g. Total/VidaPay-processor dealers) — it has zero dependency on the VIP financing ledger, so a tenant with an empty Asset Ledger can still have real data here.

## When to open a ticket
'No marketplace orders yet' shows for an account known to have real marketplace orders, or two rows clearly represent the same store under different spellings.
pages.support_md:
## Data source
`commcalc.raw_ma_marketplace_orders` — a read view over `commcalc.raw_ma_fulfillment`, populated by mod-commission's VidaPay report-pull (migration 207). NOT `asset_ledger`. `business_address` is canonicalized to the tenant's real store name via the same `store_mapping` resolution the Asset Ledger's own market backfill uses, so differently-spelled raw addresses for the same store land under one bucket; an address absent from `store_mapping` is kept as-is rather than dropped or merged incorrectly.

Degrades to `available:false` (a friendly empty state, never a 500) if migration 207 hasn't been applied yet, or the VidaPay report pull has simply never populated this org.

common_issues.symptom: 'No marketplace orders yet' even though this tenant definitely places marketplace orders.
common_issues.diagnosis: This view is populated by mod-commission's VidaPay report-pull (a scheduled/manual ingest), not by anything on this page. An empty view usually means that pull hasn't run for this org yet.
common_issues.fix: Check with the operator whether the VidaPay MA Fulfillment Orders report pull has been run/scheduled for this tenant.
common_issues.escalate_when: The report pull HAS run (confirmed) and this page is still empty. Escalate — crosses into mod-commission's ingest code.

common_issues.symptom: Two rows appear for what's clearly the same store, under slightly different names.
common_issues.diagnosis: Canonicalization only works if the raw business_address has a matching entry in store_mapping — an address genuinely absent from store_mapping is kept as its own bucket rather than merged.
common_issues.fix: Add/confirm the store's address in store_mapping so future loads canonicalize correctly.
common_issues.escalate_when: The address IS confirmed present in store_mapping and still isn't canonicalizing. Escalate.

common_issues.symptom: Filter dropdowns (business/status/order type) are empty.
common_issues.diagnosis: These come from GET /asset/marketplace-purchases/filter-options, which returns available:false under the exact same condition as the main data endpoint (view missing / not yet populated for this org).
common_issues.fix: Same as the 'no orders' case above — check whether the VidaPay pull has run.
common_issues.escalate_when: Same escalation path as the 'no orders' issue above.

pages.permissions_needed: commcalc `asset` nav module, scopes `all`/`market`; nav-gated to non-Boost/VidaPay-processor (`total`) tenants specifically — carrier-neutral, the opposite gating direction from the rest of this domain.
related_settings: migration 207 / VidaPay MA Fulfillment Orders report-pull schedule (mod-commission-owned)

pages.title: Missing Phones
pages.user_md:
## What this page shows
The investigation worklist for devices checked "physically missing" on the Inventory Aging page — device detail plus the $ owed-to-Distributor exposure at risk. Filter by store (multi-select).

## When to open a ticket
A device flagged missing on Aging doesn't show up here, or shows with no store/detail when it clearly should.
pages.support_md:
## Data source
`commcalc.asset_investigation` (rows where `physically_missing = true`) joined to `commcalc.asset_ledger` by `esn_imei`. A device flagged missing that later drops off the ledger (e.g. removed on a later Asset_Lending re-upload) still appears here with `not_in_ledger:true` and blank store/market/owed fields — this is intentional so an old flag can never silently vanish. There is no write action on this page itself; it is purely a read of what was set on the Aging page's checkbox.

common_issues.symptom: Checked a device as missing on Aging but it never shows up here.
common_issues.diagnosis: The Aging page's save is best-effort — a failed write is swallowed client-side with no error shown.
common_issues.fix: Re-check the box on Inventory Aging and confirm no error appears, then refresh this page.
common_issues.escalate_when: The checkbox visibly saves with no error, but the device still never appears here. Escalate.

common_issues.symptom: A row shows 'not in ledger' with no store/owed value.
common_issues.diagnosis: Expected — the device was flagged missing on a prior ledger and later dropped off (sold, or excluded on a later Asset_Lending re-upload). The flag intentionally isn't lost.
common_issues.fix: No fix needed; investigate the device outside this report if it's still relevant.
common_issues.escalate_when: Many devices show 'not in ledger' immediately after a normal upload — suggests the upload dropped rows unexpectedly. Escalate.

pages.permissions_needed: commcalc `asset` nav module, scopes `all`/`market`; nav-gated to Boost-carrier tenants only.

pages.title: On-Inventory by Store
pages.user_md:
## What this page shows
A per-store rollup of unsold On-Inventory device counts and $ owed to the Distributor, split into the SAME aging buckets as Inventory Aging (<45 / 45–60 WARN / >60 MISSED). Sortable columns, filters for market/store/acquired month-year, and the same stale-data banner as Aging. These totals should reconcile exactly with the /aging report.

## When to open a ticket
This report's totals disagree with /aging for the identical filters — that should never happen.
pages.support_md:
## Query
Same underlying source and bucket rules as `/aging` (`commcalc.asset_ledger`, unsold On-Inventory, buckets computed live from `acquired_date` vs today), just aggregated per store instead of per device. Because both are computed live, comparing them at different moments (even minutes apart, near a bucket boundary) can show tiny drift — but with identical filters loaded together, the totals must match.

common_issues.symptom: Totals here don't match /aging for the same filters.
common_issues.diagnosis: This is NOT expected — both reports share identical bucket rules and source rows. A mismatch usually means the filters (market/store/month-year) aren't actually set the same way on both pages, or the pages were loaded at very different moments (buckets are computed live from today's date).
common_issues.fix: Confirm identical filters on both pages and reload both together before comparing.
common_issues.escalate_when: Filters are confirmed identical and reloaded together, and totals still disagree. Escalate — this indicates a real bug in one of the two aggregations.

common_issues.symptom: Stale-data banner shows despite a recent upload.
common_issues.diagnosis: Same FileDate-based staleness check as /aging — reads the vendor file's own internal date stamp, not the upload time.
common_issues.fix: Confirm the uploaded file is a genuinely fresh Distributor export.
common_issues.escalate_when: A confirmed-fresh file still shows stale. Escalate.

pages.permissions_needed: commcalc `asset` nav module, scopes `all`/`market`; nav-gated to Boost-carrier tenants only.

pages.title: Weekly Owed to Distributor
pages.user_md:
## What this page shows
What the Distributor collects on a chosen **billing Friday** — split into **Sold Phones** (billed the Friday after the device sold) and **Aged > 60 Days** (never sold, billed once past due). Includes a by-store breakdown, an upcoming-Fridays forecast (click a row to jump there), and the full device list for the selected Friday. Use Prev/Next/This week to navigate, and the market/store multi-select filters to narrow.

## When to open a ticket
Only if a Friday's total disagrees with the **actual VIP invoice** for that exact date after you've reconciled the invoice yourself — see Support notes, this computation is locked.
pages.support_md:
## The Friday billing rule — DO NOT CHANGE THIS
VIP (the Distributor) bills every **Friday**. The trigger for a device is the **first Friday on/after `payg_date`** (falling back to `due_date` if `payg_date` is blank); the `billing_friday` column, computed by the parser at upload time, encodes this. **This has been verified to match VIP invoices to the penny.** It has been challenged before on an emotional user complaint and was confirmed correct both times. If a number looks wrong, reconcile against a REAL VIP invoice first — do not touch the trigger logic on a complaint alone.

The API query parameter is literally named `thursday` even though it always carries a Friday date — this is a historical/backward-compat naming quirk (existing saved notify subscriptions reference it), not a bug.

`bill_path` = `"aging"` when the device has no `payg_date` (billed via `due_date` instead, i.e. it aged out unsold) vs the default (has a `payg_date`, i.e. it sold and PayGo was added).

## Empty page = correct isolation
A tenant with no Boost/VIP asset-financing program has an empty `asset_ledger`, so every Friday shows "Nothing bills on this Friday" — expected, not broken. This page is also nav-gated to Boost-carrier tenants only.

common_issues.symptom: A Friday's total doesn't match the real VIP invoice for that date.
common_issues.diagnosis: First confirm you're comparing the exact same Friday date, with all store/market filters cleared, against the real invoice PDF — not an adjacent date or a filtered subset.
common_issues.fix: None by default — this computation is verified-correct and locked. Do not alter the Friday-trigger logic.
common_issues.escalate_when: A REAL VIP invoice, reconciled line-by-line, still disagrees with this report for the exact same Friday. Escalate to the platform operator/mod-asset with the invoice attached — this is the one rule in the whole module that must never be changed casually.

common_issues.symptom: A device I expected to bill this Friday is missing from the list.
common_issues.diagnosis: The device has no `payg_date` AND no `due_date` — `billing_friday` is null, so it never appears on any Friday view.
common_issues.fix: Check the source Asset_Lending.xlsx has the 'ESN Added Pay as You Go' / 'Due Date' columns populated for that device; re-upload if the vendor export was missing that data.
common_issues.escalate_when: Both dates are present in the source file but billing_friday still didn't populate after a fresh upload. Escalate — likely a parser issue.

common_issues.symptom: Every week shows 'Nothing bills on this Friday'.
common_issues.diagnosis: This tenant may simply not run the VIP/Boost asset-financing consignment program (empty asset_ledger).
common_issues.fix: Check the Asset Ledger landing page for 'No asset data loaded' — if so, this is expected.
common_issues.escalate_when: The tenant DOES run VIP asset financing and has uploaded Asset_Lending.xlsx, yet this page stays empty. Escalate.

pages.permissions_needed: commcalc `asset` nav module, scopes `all`/`market`; nav-gated to Boost-carrier tenants only (NAV_CARRIERS).
related_settings: asset_ledger.billing_friday (computed by the parser at upload, not user-editable)

pages.title: Carrier Commission File -> Table
pages.user_md:
### What this page shows
A tool to extract a carrier's commission PDF/file into a structured table you can review and use.

### How to use it
Upload the carrier file; run extract; review the extracted table.

### Top gotchas
1. Extraction quality depends on the file layout - verify the output.
pages.support_md:
### Data sources
`api /commcalc/carrier-comm-file/extract`. Parses a carrier commission document to rows.

### Symptom -> diagnosis -> fix
- **Extraction garbled** -> unusual PDF layout; may need a different export or manual mapping.

### Escalation
Format issues = support-guidable; extractor failing on a standard file = escalate.

### Related settings
/commcalc/commission-import, /commcalc/payout-schedules.

common_issues.symptom: The extracted table is missing rows or misaligned.
common_issues.diagnosis: The carrier file layout isn't cleanly parseable.
common_issues.fix: Try the source's standard export, or use the Commission Import wizard with explicit mapping.
common_issues.escalate_when: A standard carrier file consistently fails extraction -> escalate to platform operator.

pages.title: Carrier Mapping (Comp Report -> 4 Components)
pages.user_md:
### What this page shows
Rules that classify a carrier's comp-report categories into the 4 canonical components (residual/commission/spiff/reimbursement) used by Total Compensation and the ledger. Shows unmapped categories to be mapped.

### How to use it
Pick a carrier; for each raw category pattern choose a match type + component. Unmapped categories are listed. Category/subtype inputs are typeaheads over the org's real comp categories (pick, or "use as new pattern").

### Top gotchas
1. Unmapped comp categories don't roll into any component - Total Compensation will look short until they're mapped.
2. Match type matters (exact vs contains vs prefix vs regex).
pages.support_md:
### Data sources
`GET/POST /commcalc/carrier-category-map`; options from `/carrier-category-options` (distinct `raw_comp_report.compensation_type` for the org). Migration 038.

### Symptom -> diagnosis -> fix
- **Categories in the Unmapped panel** -> add a rule mapping them to a component.
- **Rule matches nothing** -> wrong match type/pattern; the typeahead shows the real category strings.

### Escalation
Mapping = support-guidable. Mapped categories still not flowing to Total Comp = escalate.

### Related settings
/commcalc/comp-trend, /commcalc/commission-category-map, /commcalc/commission-ledger.

common_issues.symptom: Total Compensation is missing some comp dollars.
common_issues.diagnosis: Those comp categories are unmapped in Carrier Mapping.
common_issues.fix: Map each unmapped category (shown in the panel) to a component with the right match type.
common_issues.escalate_when: All categories mapped and the report still under-totals -> escalate to platform operator.

pages.title: Chargebacks & Fraud
pages.user_md:
### What this page shows
Chargeback review and fraud scan: suspected clawbacks assigned to a rep -> employee, with a fraud scan tool. Captures customer/email for the case.

### How to use it
Run the fraud scan; review chargeback items; assign to the responsible rep/employee.

### Top gotchas
1. Assign-first workflow: a chargeback must be assigned to a rep before it lands on an employee.
2. Recalculating commissions preserves existing chargeback assignments.
pages.support_md:
### Data sources
`chargeback_review` -> `chargeback_items` (mig 036). `POST /commcalc/chargeback-review/scan-fraud`; employees from `storeops/employees`.

### Symptom -> diagnosis -> fix
- **Chargeback not hitting an employee's pay** -> not yet assigned to the rep. Assign it.
- **Missing customer info** -> source sales file lacked Customer #/email. Re-upload full 78-col file.

### Escalation
Assignment/data = support-guidable. A recompute that drops assignments = escalate to platform operator (money-touching).

### Related settings
/commcalc/sales-analyzer, /commcalc/rep-aliases.

common_issues.symptom: A known chargeback isn't reducing anyone's commission.
common_issues.diagnosis: It hasn't been assigned to a rep (assign-first design).
common_issues.fix: Assign the chargeback_review row to the correct rep on this page.
common_issues.escalate_when: It's assigned and still not deducted after recompute -> escalate to platform operator.

pages.title: Rep Coaching
pages.user_md:
### What this page shows
Coaching view per rep for the period - where reps are under target and suggested focus areas.

### How to use it
Pick period; review per-rep coaching cues and export if needed.

### Top gotchas
1. 'all'/'market' scopes only.
2. Relies on targets being configured - no targets means thin coaching output.
pages.support_md:
### Data sources
Combines the commission/sales snapshot with the targets engine actuals-vs-target. Read-only.

### Symptom -> diagnosis -> fix
- **No coaching signal** -> targets not set for the store/rep. Configure targets (/commcalc/targets/settings).

### Escalation
Config = support-guidable; wrong computed gaps = escalate.

### Related settings
/commcalc/targets, /commcalc/targets/settings.

common_issues.symptom: Coaching page shows little/no actionable data.
common_issues.diagnosis: Targets not configured, so there is no target to compare actuals against.
common_issues.fix: Set targets on /commcalc/targets/settings; ensure sales data exists for the period.
common_issues.escalate_when: Targets + data present but coaching still blank -> escalate to platform operator.

pages.title: Column Mapping
pages.user_md:
### What this page shows
Maps a carrier/report's file columns to MetricsPro's expected fields, with auto-detect and target-field help.

### How to use it
Pick the carrier/report; detect columns; map each source column to the target field.

### Top gotchas
1. A wrong/missing column map is the usual cause of "uploaded but nothing ingested / dollars are 0".
2. Detection is a starting point - verify each mapping.
pages.support_md:
### Data sources
`GET/POST /commcalc/column-mapping`, `/column-mapping/detect`, `/column-mapping/targets`; carriers.

### Symptom -> diagnosis -> fix
- **Uploaded data ingests as 0 / missing** -> key columns (Ext Price, GP, Contract Type) unmapped. Fix the mapping.
- **Detection off** -> non-standard export; map manually.

### Escalation
Mapping = support-guidable; a correct map still mis-ingesting = escalate.

### Related settings
/commcalc/upload, /commcalc/implementation, /commcalc/target-fields.

common_issues.symptom: An uploaded file's dollar fields all come through as 0.
common_issues.diagnosis: Ext Price/GP (or Contract Type) columns aren't mapped to the right target fields.
common_issues.fix: Map those columns correctly here, then re-upload/re-ingest.
common_issues.escalate_when: Columns mapped correctly and values still ingest as 0 -> escalate to platform operator.

pages.title: Category -> Bucket Map (Commission Ledger)
pages.user_md:
### What this page shows
Maps the observed commission types in a source report to the 5 canonical ledger buckets, per template, with a priority (lower wins).

### How to use it
Pick a source report/template; for each observed type set a bucket + priority. Unmapped types stay out of the ledger buckets.

### Top gotchas
1. Drives the Commission Ledger, not what reps are paid.
2. Priority ordering resolves overlapping rules - lower number wins.
pages.support_md:
### Data sources
`GET/POST /commcalc/commission-category-map`; observed types from `/commission-ledger/observed-types`; templates from `/commission-ledger/templates`.

### Symptom -> diagnosis -> fix
- **Ledger rows unmapped** -> add a mapping for the observed type.
- **Wrong bucket** -> a higher-priority rule wins; adjust priority.

### Escalation
Mapping = support-guidable; ledger totals wrong after full mapping = escalate.

### Related settings
/commcalc/commission-ledger, /commcalc/carrier-mapping.

common_issues.symptom: Commission Ledger rows land as unmapped.
common_issues.diagnosis: Their observed type has no Category -> Bucket rule for the template.
common_issues.fix: Map the observed types (listed on the page) to buckets with appropriate priority.
common_issues.escalate_when: All observed types mapped and rows still unbucketed -> escalate to platform operator.

pages.title: Commission Explain (how was this calculated?)
pages.user_md:
### What this page shows
A per-rep "why is my number this?" narration: which plan attached, per-IMEI M1-M6 gate status, held reasons, and $0-explanations. Also reachable via the drill-in on the Rep Commission Report. Includes an IMEI search.

### How to use it
Pick a rep/period (or drill in from the Rep Commission Report); read the plan-attach and per-line explanation. Search an IMEI to see its gate status.

### Top gotchas
1. Best first stop when a rep disputes their pay - it usually names the cause (no plan, unmet gate, no matching rule).
2. Reads the saved snapshot; a stale snapshot reflects the last Calculate.
pages.support_md:
### Data sources
Read-only over the commission engine's diagnose path (`_resolve_plan_for`/diagnose) + the sale-installment gate status. Boost vs plan resolved by carrier mode.

### Common $0 explanations it surfaces
- No Commission Plan assigned (non-Boost) -> assign on Commission Plans.
- Rule matched nothing (e.g. rule uses `equals` where the data needs `contains`).
- Multi-month installment withheld because the dealer-paid residual gate isn't met (MA/residual data).

### Symptom -> diagnosis -> fix
- **"No plan attached"** -> assign the rep to a plan (/commcalc/commission-plans).
- **"Withheld - dealer unpaid"** -> the residual gate; check the MA/residual file is ingested for the gate month.
- **Stale narration** -> needs a recompute (money-touching; operator/owner).

### Escalation
Config causes = support-guidable. A gate/plan that is correctly configured but still explained as $0 = escalate to platform operator.

### Related settings
/commcalc/commission-plans, /commcalc/plan-installments, /commcalc/rep-aliases.

common_issues.symptom: A rep asks why they were paid $0 or an unexpected amount.
common_issues.diagnosis: Commission Explain names the cause: no plan, no matching rule, or an unmet multi-month gate.
common_issues.fix: Act on the stated cause: assign a plan, fix the rule operator (equals->contains) on Commission Plans, or ingest the residual/MA file for the gate month; then the operator recomputes.
common_issues.escalate_when: The explanation shows correct plan+rules+gate met but the number is still wrong -> escalate to platform operator (engine bug).

pages.title: Commission Import Wizard
pages.user_md:
### What this page shows
A guided upload for a carrier commission file: analyze the file, then commit it into the commission data.

### How to use it
Pick the carrier, upload the file, review the analyze step, then commit.

### Top gotchas

2. Importing here doesn't pay reps; a Calculate is still needed for pay.

common_issues.diagnosis: File layout doesn't match the detector; likely a reduced/alternate export.
common_issues.fix: Correct the column mapping in the analyze step or supply the full expected export.
common_issues.escalate_when: Correct file + mapping still imports wrong values -> escalate to platform operator.

pages.title: Commission Ledger (canonical, SAP-style) - incl. /setup
pages.user_md:
### What this page shows
The canonical, carrier-agnostic commission ledger: 5 buckets, rule-mapped per template, with per-rep and per-row drill-down. You can import a carrier commission file into it. The **/setup** sub-page walks first-time template + column mapping.

### How to use it
- Pick a template + period; view summary / by-rep / rows.
- Import a carrier file (analyze -> map columns -> import). First time, use **/setup**.

### Top gotchas
1. This sits ALONGSIDE the legacy Boost calc - it does not change what reps are paid; it's a normalized ledger view.
2. Negative amounts = payout (SAP sign convention).
3. Rows land in buckets only if the Category -> Bucket Map covers their types.
pages.support_md:
### Data sources
- `GET /commission-ledger/summary|by-rep|rows|templates`; import via `POST /commission-ledger/import` (analyze on /setup).
- 5 canonical buckets (mig 071); Boost template seeded (mig 072). Mapping rules per template map raw types -> buckets.

### Symptom -> diagnosis -> fix
- **Rows show as "unmapped"** -> the raw type has no Category -> Bucket rule. Map on /commcalc/commission-category-map.
- **Import fails** -> column mapping wrong; redo via /setup analyze step.
- **Empty ledger** -> no template selected or no file imported for the org/period.

### Escalation
Mapping/import = support-guidable. Ledger totals disagreeing with a fully-mapped source = escalate.

### Related settings
/commcalc/commission-category-map, /commcalc/commission-ledger/setup, /commcalc/carrier-mapping.

common_issues.symptom: Imported commission rows show up as unmapped / not in any bucket.
common_issues.diagnosis: Their source type isn't covered by the template's Category -> Bucket map.
common_issues.fix: Add the mapping on /commcalc/commission-category-map (observed types are listed there), re-view.
common_issues.escalate_when: All observed types mapped and rows still unbucketed -> escalate to platform operator.

pages.title: Commission Plans
pages.user_md:
### What this page shows
The user-defined commission rules that pay non-Boost carriers: each plan has rules (field + match + payout) producing the 5 payout kinds and tiers, plus which reps/stores are assigned to it.

### How to use it
Create/edit plans, add rules (e.g. "contract_type contains Activation -> $X"), and ASSIGN reps to the plan. Then Calculate the period.

### Top gotchas
1. A rep pays $0 because they have no plan assignment - the #1 non-Boost "bug" that isn't one.
2. Rule operator matters: `equals "Accessory"` misses "Accessories"; use `contains "Accessor"`.
3. Editing a plan does NOT recompute - someone must Calculate afterward (money-touching).
pages.support_md:
### Data sources
`GET/POST /api/v1/commcalc/commission-plans`; fields from `sales-fields`; reps from `storeops/employees`; stores from `storeops/stores`. Engine = `commission_engine.py` (migs 057/059/060: commission_plan/rule/tier/assignment).

### How pay is produced
For each assigned rep, sales lines are matched against the plan's rules -> payout kinds (+ tiers). Only carriers in `carrier_mode='plan'` use this; Boost uses the KPI-tier calculator.

### Symptom -> diagnosis -> fix
- **$0 rep** -> no assignment, or a rule using `equals`/wrong field that matches nothing. Assign + fix the rule operator, then Calculate.
- **Overpay/underpay** -> rule amount or tier config. Money-touching - propose the change and get owner sign-off before editing.

### Escalation
Assignment + rule-operator fixes are config the support user can guide. ANY change to a rate/amount/tier that moves pay = propose-first, owner approval, escalate to platform operator to apply + recompute.

### Related settings
/commcalc/payout-schedules, /commcalc/plan-installments, /commcalc/rep-aliases, /commcalc/commission-explain.

common_issues.symptom: A whole carrier/tenant's reps pay $0 and there are no KPI tiers.
common_issues.diagnosis: Non-Boost carrier (carrier_mode='plan') with missing plans and/or no rep assignments - the plan engine has nothing to apply.
common_issues.fix: Create the plan + rules and assign every selling rep, then have the operator Calculate. Verify with Commission Explain.
common_issues.escalate_when: Plans + assignments + rules are all correct and reps still pay $0 -> escalate to platform operator.

common_issues.symptom: An accessory rule pays some transactions but not others.
common_issues.diagnosis: Rule uses equals or the wrong token (e.g. 'Accessory' misses 'Accessories').
common_issues.fix: Change the rule to contains 'Accessor'. This alters pay - propose it and get owner sign-off before saving + recomputing.
common_issues.escalate_when: Any rate/amount/tier change (moves money) -> escalate to platform operator for owner approval + recompute.

pages.title: Total Compensation (trend)
pages.user_md:
### What this page shows
Total compensation trend across periods - residual + commission + spiff + reimbursement, mapped into canonical buckets.

### How to use it
Pick range; review the trend. Export as needed.

### Top gotchas
1. Bucketing depends on Carrier Mapping (Comp Report -> components). Unmapped comp categories fall out of the buckets.
2. "Total Compensation" is NOT residual alone - it's the sum of all comp buckets.
pages.support_md:
### Data sources
Reads `raw_comp_report` (total compensation) classified via `carrier_category_map` (migration 038). Residual = MI + ATU; comprehensive comp = total, not residual.

### Symptom -> diagnosis -> fix
- **Categories missing from buckets** -> unmapped comp categories. Map them on /commcalc/carrier-mapping.
- **Trend gap for a month** -> comp report for that month not ingested.

### Escalation
Mapping/ingestion = support-guidable; wrong bucket math after mapping = escalate.

### Related settings
/commcalc/carrier-mapping, /commcalc/commission-category-map.

common_issues.symptom: Some compensation dollars don't appear in any bucket.
common_issues.diagnosis: Their comp category isn't mapped to a component in Carrier Mapping.
common_issues.fix: Add the category -> component rule on /commcalc/carrier-mapping.
common_issues.escalate_when: All categories mapped and totals still wrong -> escalate to platform operator.

pages.title: Connectors
pages.user_md:
### What this page shows
Configured data connectors / report definitions for the tenant - the sources MetricsPro pulls from and their run settings.

### How to use it
Add/edit connectors and report definitions; set 2FA method and run-now dispatch.

### Top gotchas
1. A connector's org_id decides which tenant its data lands in - a mis-filed connector routes another tenant's data into the wrong org.
2. report_definitions `auto` for report_key='sales' gates feed -> raw_sales promotion.
pages.support_md:
### Data sources
`GET /commcalc/connectors`, `/report-definitions`. Feeds the sweeps (email/ftp/portal).

### Symptom -> diagnosis -> fix
- **Data landing in the wrong tenant** -> connector row filed under the wrong org_id. Correct the org.
- **Sales not promoting** -> report_definitions auto for 'sales' is off.

### Escalation
Config = support-guidable; a wrong-org data leak = escalate immediately to platform operator (multi-tenant).

### Related settings
/commcalc/email-imports, /commcalc/ftp-imports, /commcalc/report-mappings.

common_issues.symptom: A tenant is seeing another tenant's imported data.
common_issues.diagnosis: A connector/mailbox row was filed under the wrong org_id, routing data into the wrong tenant.
common_issues.fix: Correct the connector's org; this is a multi-tenant issue - flag it.
common_issues.escalate_when: Any cross-tenant data routing -> escalate immediately to platform operator.

pages.title: Custom Report (builder)
pages.user_md:
### What this page shows
A build-your-own report over every commcalc dataset (sales lines, commissions, targets actuals, DLAR KPIs, expenses, chargebacks, flags, MA commission/tenure). Pick datasets + columns, apply the standard filters, group by anything, then export/send. You can SAVE a named configuration to recall it.

### How to use it
- Choose a dataset, tick columns, set filters/group-by, run.
- Save the config with a name to reload later.
- Export Excel/PDF or Send by email/WhatsApp.

### Top gotchas
1. Money columns are permission-gated - a user without the grant simply won't see them (not a bug).
2. An empty result on a non-house tenant is often correct isolation (that dataset has no rows for the org).
3. Saved configs are per-org; a removed column drops out of an old saved config.
pages.support_md:
### Data sources
- Config-driven registry `commcalc.custom_report.DATASETS` merged with config rows (mig 211): code default -> house row -> org override.
- Resolvers REUSE existing reads (no duplicate query logic): `_sales_rows_union`, the `rep_commissions` snapshot + chargeback deduction, `_compute_feed_actuals_py`, `raw_dlar_store`, `store_expenses`, `chargeback_items`, `flags`, `raw_ma_commission`, `raw_ma_daily_tx`.
- Read-only; never touches the calc path or fires a recompute.

### Symptom -> diagnosis -> fix
- **A dataset shows nothing** -> no data for org/period (correct isolation) or the backing table isn't ingested. Confirm on the source page first.
- **A money column is missing for a user** -> role lacks the per-column grant. Fix via /admin/roles.
- **Saved report won't load a column** -> column renamed/disabled in the registry; re-pick it.

### Escalation
New dataset/column requests or registry changes need mig/config work = escalate to platform operator. Data-presence and permission issues are support-guidable.

### Related settings
/admin/roles (column grants), the source pages for each dataset, mig 211 registry (operator).

common_issues.symptom: Report comes back empty for a dataset the user expected data in.
common_issues.diagnosis: No org-scoped rows for that period, or the backing table isn't imported. Under multi-tenant, empty is often correct isolation.
common_issues.fix: Confirm the data exists on the dataset's native page (Sales Report, KPI, etc.) with the same period/filters before treating it as a fault.
common_issues.escalate_when: Data confirmed present on the native page but the Custom Report shows none with identical filters -> escalate to platform operator.

pages.title: Device History Lookup
pages.user_md:
### What this page shows
Look up one IMEI/phone number and see its full story: activation/tenure history, per-period commission & rebate, plus aging (days on inventory, aging bucket) and the device purchase price. Also embedded on the employee portal.

### How to use it
Type or paste an IMEI (or phone number) and search. Export the result (Excel/PDF).

### Top gotchas
1. The per-period commission & rebate $ is a gated (admin-only until granted) column - reps see history/tenure/aging/price but not the money unless granted.
2. For MA-fed (Total/VidaPay) tenants, money/tenure come from the MA files - if those aren't ingested you'll see $0 / "no residual history".
pages.support_md:
### Data sources
- `GET /api/v1/commcalc/device-history`. Carrier-aware: Boost -> `raw_mi` + `raw_payment_detail`; MA/Total -> `raw_ma_commission` (spiffs/rebate/margins) + `raw_ma_daily_tx` (tenure). Dispatch via `_resolve_carrier_mode`.
- Aging + purchase price from `commcalc.asset_ledger` (matched on esn_imei/phone_number).

### How money is shown
Negative MA amounts = payout to dealer; multiple rows per IMEI/period (base + adjustment) are normal. Period spelling is 'June 2026' style - reads go through `_pvariants`.

### Symptom -> diagnosis -> fix
- **$0 / "No residual history" on a Total tenant** -> MA file for the period not ingested, or the IMEI truly has none. Confirm the MA file was uploaded for the sale month (manual-upload tenants must re-upload the refreshed month).
- **Reps can't see commission $** -> default-closed gate; grant `device_commission` via /admin/roles.
- **No aging/price** -> device not in asset_ledger (honest "no inventory record" line).

### Escalation
Missing MA ingestion / grant = support-guidable. A carrier-mode misdispatch (Boost money on an MA tenant or vice-versa) = escalate to platform operator.

### Related settings
/admin/roles (device_commission grant), /commcalc/ma-upload, /commcalc/email-imports.

common_issues.symptom: Total/VidaPay tenant device shows Commission $0 / Rebate $0 / no residual.
common_issues.diagnosis: MA commission file for the sale month not ingested (money/tenure for MA tenants come from raw_ma_*, not raw_mi).
common_issues.fix: Confirm/ingest the MA commission file for that period (Manual upload or the VidaPay email/portal pull). Re-search.
common_issues.escalate_when: MA rows confirmed present for the IMEI+period and it still renders $0 -> escalate to platform operator.

common_issues.symptom: A rep says they can't see the commission/rebate dollars.
common_issues.diagnosis: device_commission is a default-closed sensitive-data grant, separate from module access.
common_issues.fix: Grant it on the user's role at /admin/roles (admin action).
common_issues.escalate_when: Grant set and money still hidden -> escalate to platform operator.

pages.title: Pay Discrepancy
pages.user_md:
### What this page shows
Expected-vs-paid commission discrepancy: where the carrier paid differently than the system expected, per rep/deal.

### How to use it
Pick period; run the discrepancy; review mismatches; export.

### Top gotchas
1. Needs both an "expected" basis (your calc) and an "actual" (carrier comp file) - if one side is missing, everything looks like a discrepancy.
2. Period-spelling mismatches ('June 2026' vs '2026-06') can make one side return zero rows.
pages.support_md:
### Data sources
`POST /commcalc/discrepancy/run` -> `discrepancy_engine.run_discrepancy`. Compares the commission snapshot against carrier comp/MI data. Reads go through `_pvariants` for period spelling.

### Symptom -> diagnosis -> fix
- **Everything flagged as discrepant** -> one side missing (no comp file ingested, or commissions not calculated). Ensure the calc ran and the carrier comp file is ingested for the same period.
- **Zero rows on one side** -> period spelled differently in the two tables. Usually resolves once both use the same month's data.

### Escalation
Missing-data/period = support-guidable. A genuine expected-vs-paid gap that isn't a data issue = a real recovery/appeal case (see Appeal Recovery) or escalate.

### Related settings
/commcalc/recovery, /commcalc/carrier-mapping, /commcalc/epay/sweep.

common_issues.symptom: Almost every line shows a discrepancy.
common_issues.diagnosis: One input is missing - either commissions weren't calculated or the carrier comp/MI file isn't ingested for the period.
common_issues.fix: Confirm a Calculate ran and the carrier comp file is imported for the same month; re-run discrepancy.
common_issues.escalate_when: Both sides present + same period and the engine still flags known-good pay -> escalate to platform operator.

pages.title: Distributors
pages.user_md:
### What this page shows
The tenant's distributors/vendors and their payment ledger - terms, funding (own vs borrowed), asset-lending capability.

### How to use it
Add/edit distributors and their arrangement; review the payment ledger.

### Top gotchas
1. `has_asset_lending` on a distributor drives whether Asset-Lending/PayGo surfaces appear.
2. Needs migration 058 - a "run migration 058" note means it isn't enabled yet.
pages.support_md:
### Data sources
`GET/POST /commcalc/distributors` and `/distributor-payments` (mig 058). Carriers from `/commcalc/carriers`.

### Symptom -> diagnosis -> fix
- **"Run migration 058" note** -> the distributors tables aren't installed. The operator runs the SQL.
- **PayGo pages hidden** -> the distributor's asset-lending capability is off.

### Escalation
Config = support-guidable; the migration note = escalate to platform operator to run SQL.

### Related settings
/commcalc/vip, /commcalc/vip/paygo.

common_issues.symptom: Page shows a 'Run migration 058' message.
common_issues.diagnosis: The distributors/distributor_payments tables aren't installed for the environment.
common_issues.fix: Support can't run SQL - escalate to the platform operator to apply migration 058.
common_issues.escalate_when: Always for the migration note - it needs an operator to run SQL.

pages.title: Metrics Rep/Store Sync (DLAR)
pages.user_md:
### What this page shows
The DLAR auto-sweep that scrapes boostelevatego.com daily for rep/store metrics (replaces the manual DLAR upload). Status + controls.

### How to use it
Review sweep status; run if permitted. It also auto-recalcs Boost commissions once a day.

### Top gotchas
1. This is the ONLY automatic recompute in the system (Boost-only, once daily) - everything else waits for Calculate.
2. KPI Metrics reads the snapshot this sweep refreshes.
pages.support_md:
### Data sources
`dlar_sweep` -> `raw_dlar_store` (unique key = address). `_do_dlar_sweep` auto-recalcs Boost after each run.

### Symptom -> diagnosis -> fix
- **KPI/DLAR data stale** -> sweep hasn't run today; run it or wait.
- **Store missing** -> address not matched; add a store alias.

### Escalation
Freshness/mapping = support-guidable. Scrape login failures = escalate to platform operator.

### Related settings
/commcalc/kpi, /commcalc/store-match.

common_issues.symptom: KPI/DLAR numbers are a day behind.
common_issues.diagnosis: DLAR sweep runs once daily; the snapshot reflects the last run.
common_issues.fix: Run the sweep (if permitted) or wait for the daily run; KPI Metrics refreshes with it.
common_issues.escalate_when: The sweep fails to log into boostelevatego -> escalate to platform operator.

pages.title: Email & Portal Logins (2FA) - Email Auto-Import
pages.user_md:
### What this page shows
Email auto-import (IMAP mailboxes that receive carrier/B2B report emails) plus portal logins including 2FA / proxy settings (e.g. VidaPay pull). Configure mailboxes, data sources, test, and see processed emails.

### How to use it
Add a mailbox/data source, configure 2FA/proxy, test it, and review processed emails.

### Top gotchas
1. A mailbox's org_id decides which tenant its emails land in - a mis-filed mailbox routes another tenant's data into the wrong org.
2. Portal 2FA/residential-proxy logins are configured HERE, not on Connectors.
3. b2bsoft/portal logins can be IP-blocked from datacenter IPs - a login failure post-2FA is often that.
pages.support_md:
### Data sources
`email-sweep/accounts|config|processed|test`, `data-sources`, `data-source/test-proxy`, `custom-import-types`, `distributors`, `carriers`. The daily B2B feed flows via IMAP into `daily_sales_feed`.

### Symptom -> diagnosis -> fix
- **Feed empty / not flowing** -> mailbox not configured or IMAP creds wrong; test the account.
- **Wrong tenant getting emails** -> mailbox filed under the wrong org_id (a real repeated failure mode). Fix the org.
- **Portal 2FA pull fails post-login** -> residential-proxy/2FA setup or datacenter-IP block; use the proxy path (test-proxy).

### Escalation
Mailbox/creds config = support-guidable. Cross-tenant mis-routing = escalate immediately. Portal IP blocks / proxy = escalate to platform operator (egress).

### Related settings
/commcalc/connectors, /commcalc/report-mappings, /commcalc/ma-upload, /commcalc/sales-recon.

common_issues.symptom: The daily B2B sales feed stopped flowing.
common_issues.diagnosis: IMAP mailbox misconfigured/creds changed, or emails not arriving.
common_issues.fix: Test the email-sweep account here; confirm the mailbox receives the report emails.
common_issues.escalate_when: Mailbox tests OK, emails arrive, but nothing ingests -> escalate to platform operator.

common_issues.symptom: VidaPay/portal pull fails right after the 2FA step.
common_issues.diagnosis: Portal login is IP-blocked from the datacenter, or the residential proxy/2FA config is off.
common_issues.fix: Configure/test the proxy (test-proxy) and 2FA method here; if still blocked it needs operator egress.
common_issues.escalate_when: Proxy + 2FA configured and login still blocked -> escalate to platform operator.

pages.title: Payment Processor Sync (ePay MI + ATU)
pages.user_md:
### What this page shows
The ePay sync that pulls MI + ATU (residual) data into MetricsPro. Status + controls.

### How to use it
Review sync status; run if permitted.

### Top gotchas
1. Boost residual = MI + ATU comes from ePay; Total residual comes from VidaPay (a different path).
2. A comp value of 0 can just mean the carrier hasn't posted comp yet for the current month.
pages.support_md:
### Data sources
`epay_sweep` -> `raw_mi` / `raw_payment_detail` / `raw_comp_report`. Headless portal pull.

### Symptom -> diagnosis -> fix
- **Comp 0 for the current month** -> carrier comp not posted yet, or a current-month period gap. Not a bug.
- **Sweep fails** -> portal auth/IP (WAF) issue.

### Escalation
Timing/period = support-guidable. Portal auth/WAF failures = escalate to platform operator.

### Related settings
/commcalc/email-imports, /commcalc/carrier-mapping, /commcalc/discrepancy.

common_issues.symptom: ePay comp/residual shows 0 for the current month.
common_issues.diagnosis: The carrier hasn't posted comp yet, or the current-month period isn't fully populated - a timing gap, not a fault.
common_issues.fix: Wait for the carrier to post; recheck after the next sweep. Confirm the period.
common_issues.escalate_when: Comp is posted (visible in the ePay portal) but never syncs -> escalate to platform operator.

pages.title: Owner Overview
pages.user_md:
### What this page shows
A period-level executive summary of commissions/sales/payout for leadership. Scoped to company-wide or market managers.

### How to use it
Pick the period; review the roll-up tiles and tables. Filters and exports follow the standard bar.

### Top gotchas
1. Visible only to 'all'/'market' scope roles - store/self roles won't see it (by design).
2. Numbers derive from the same sales aggregation as the Sales Report; disagreement is a classification/mapping issue upstream.
pages.support_md:
### Data sources
Aggregates the commission snapshot + `_sales_rows_union` for the org/period. Read-only.

### Symptom -> diagnosis -> fix
- **Doesn't match Sales Report** -> the Sales Report is the owner-declared truth; reconcile classification config and confirm same period/filters.
- **Empty** -> no data, or role scope excludes markets (correct).

### Escalation
Aggregation mismatches after config is confirmed = escalate to platform operator.

### Related settings
Classification, /admin/roles (scopes).

common_issues.symptom: Owner Overview numbers differ from the Sales Report.
common_issues.diagnosis: Upstream classification/mapping differences or stale snapshot; the Sales Report is the source of truth.
common_issues.fix: Reconcile classification (Classification panel) and re-run with the same period/filters.
common_issues.escalate_when: Config identical and figures still diverge -> escalate to platform operator.

pages.title: Executive MTD
pages.user_md:
### What this page shows
Month-to-date executive metrics with the standard store/market/rep filter bar and configurable metric tiles.

### How to use it
Pick period + filters; tiles and tables update; exports follow filters.

### Top gotchas
1. Cumulative figures are DERIVED from the same aggregation as the Sales Report - the Sales Report is the source of truth.
2. Blank contract_type transactions under-count activations here too - fix in Classification.
3. A store shown twice = a spelling variant between sales and targets/roster rows (e.g. "957 Pennsylvania Ave" vs "...Avenue") - add a store alias.
pages.support_md:
### Data sources
- `_exec_mtd` over `_sales_rows_union`; tile config from `GET /api/v1/commcalc/exec-metric-config`.
- Activation classification uses the tenant's config tokens; blank-ct rules matter here.

### Symptom -> diagnosis -> fix
- **Undercount** -> blank contract_type lines. Add classification / blank-ct activation rules. A bare "Port" value not counting needs a contract-type map entry ("Port" -> premium/upgrade).
- **Store double-listed** -> sales vs targets/roster spelling. Add a store alias on /commcalc/store-match.
- **Differs from Sales Report** -> should be byte-equal by design; if not, escalate.

### Escalation
Classification/alias = support-guidable. Divergence from the Sales Report after config = escalate to platform operator.

### Related settings
Classification, /commcalc/store-match, exec-metric-config (on-page gear).

common_issues.symptom: Activation counts lower than the store's own tally.
common_issues.diagnosis: Blank/unmapped contract_type transactions, or a bare 'Port' value with no map entry.
common_issues.fix: Add contract-type map / blank-ct activation rules in Classification (per-org config).
common_issues.escalate_when: Rules configured and counts still wrong, or MTD disagrees with a correct Sales Report -> escalate to platform operator.

common_issues.symptom: A store appears twice in the MTD breakdown.
common_issues.diagnosis: Same store spelled differently in sales vs targets/roster (Ave/Avenue).
common_issues.fix: Add a store alias on /commcalc/store-match so the spellings collapse to one canonical store.
common_issues.escalate_when: Alias added and the duplicate persists -> escalate to platform operator.

pages.title: Store Expenses
pages.user_md:
### What this page shows
Per-store expense entry/summary used in store P&L and net calculations.

### How to use it
Pick store + period; enter/review expenses.

### Top gotchas
1. Stores come from the org's real store roster (pick, don't type).
2. 'all'/'market' scopes only.
pages.support_md:
### Data sources
`store_expenses` table; stores from `storeops/stores`.

### Symptom -> diagnosis -> fix
- **Store missing from picker** -> not in the store roster; add/confirm the store.
- **Expense not in P&L** -> period/store mismatch; confirm.

### Escalation
Roster/entry = support-guidable; P&L integration issues = finance module/operator.

### Related settings
/commcalc/store-match, Finance P&L pages.

common_issues.symptom: A store isn't selectable for expense entry.
common_issues.diagnosis: The store isn't in the org's store roster.
common_issues.fix: Add/confirm the store in the roster (storeops) and check store aliases.
common_issues.escalate_when: Store exists in roster but still unselectable -> escalate to platform operator.

pages.title: Flags & Compliance
pages.user_md:
### What this page shows
Compliance/commission flags for the period (e.g. port-out risk, missing data, appeal-related) - a worklist of exceptions to review.

### How to use it
Pick period; work through flags; export.

### Top gotchas
1. Flags are computed from current data - new uploads change them.
2. Some flags come from the asset module's sync (appeals/RMA) - managed there.
pages.support_md:
### Data sources
`commcalc.flags` populated by `calc_flags` / `portout_flags` and asset flag syncs (`_sync_appeal_flags`, `_sync_rma_flags`, delete-first by source then insert). Read here.

### Symptom -> diagnosis -> fix
- **A flag looks wrong/stale** -> underlying data changed; re-run the relevant calc/sync.
- **Empty** -> no exceptions, or correct isolation.

### Escalation
Data/sync = support-guidable; a flag rule producing clearly-wrong results = escalate.

### Related settings
/commcalc/accessory-flags, asset flag syncs (asset module).

common_issues.symptom: A flag persists after the underlying issue was fixed.
common_issues.diagnosis: Flags are re-derived on calc/sync; the display predates the fix.
common_issues.fix: Re-run the relevant calculation/sync (or wait for the daily sweep) and reload.
common_issues.escalate_when: Data corrected and re-synced but the flag rule still misfires -> escalate to platform operator.

pages.title: FTP Auto-Import
pages.user_md:
### What this page shows
Configuration + status for pulling files automatically over FTP, including test and run-now.

### How to use it
Set the FTP config, test it, and review processed files.

### Top gotchas
1. A failing test is usually credentials/host/path, not a MetricsPro bug.
2. Custom import types define how each file is treated.
pages.support_md:
### Data sources
`GET /commcalc/ftp-sweep/config|processed`, `POST /ftp-sweep/test|run-now`; `custom-import-types`.

### Symptom -> diagnosis -> fix
- **Test fails** -> wrong host/creds/path. Fix the config.
- **Files pulled but not ingested** -> import type/mapping mismatch.

### Escalation
Config = support-guidable; a correct config that still won't connect = escalate (may be egress/IP).

### Related settings
/commcalc/connectors, /commcalc/email-imports, /commcalc/report-mappings.

common_issues.symptom: FTP test connection fails.
common_issues.diagnosis: Host/credentials/path incorrect, or the server blocks the backend IP.
common_issues.fix: Verify and re-enter the FTP config; test again.
