common_issues.escalate_when: Config confirmed correct and it still can't connect -> escalate to platform operator (egress/IP).

pages.title: Gross Profit Report
pages.user_md:
### What this page shows
Gross profit by store/category from the sales file's GP columns, grouped by GP category.

### How to use it
Pick period + filters; review GP by category/store; export.

### Top gotchas
1. GP $0 on a whole month usually = wrong sales export (no GP/Ext Price columns).
2. Accessory GP $0 on specific "* BYOD" items is a POS catalog issue (Unit Cost = Unit Price), not a MetricsPro bug.
pages.support_md:
### Data sources
`gp_report.calc_gp_report` over the sales union; category mapping via `/commcalc/gp-category-map`. GP comes straight from the source file's GP column.

### Symptom -> diagnosis -> fix
- **All GP $0** -> reduced export missing GP/Ext Price. Re-upload the 78-col file.
- **Specific items GP $0** -> source catalog has Unit Cost = Unit Price ("* BYOD" items). The fix is in the POS catalog; there is no MetricsPro cost-override.
- **Category "Other"** -> GP category not mapped; map on /commcalc/gp-category-map.

### Escalation
Upload/mapping = support-guidable. Source-catalog cost issues = a business/POS fix (tell the user), not a code bug. Wrong GP math on good data = escalate.

### Related settings
/commcalc/gp-category-map, /commcalc/upload.

common_issues.symptom: Gross Profit shows $0 for a whole month.
common_issues.diagnosis: The uploaded sales file lacks GP/Ext Price columns (reduced/legacy export).
common_issues.fix: Re-upload the 78-column Sales Transaction Details file with GP + Ext Price present.
common_issues.escalate_when: Full file confirmed and GP still $0 -> escalate to platform operator.

common_issues.symptom: Certain accessory items show GP $0.
common_issues.diagnosis: The POS catalog has Unit Cost equal to Unit Price for those '* BYOD' items - GP is genuinely 0 in the source.
common_issues.fix: Explain it's a POS catalog data issue; the cost must be corrected in the POS, not in MetricsPro.
common_issues.escalate_when: Advise correcting the POS catalog; escalate only if the user believes a cost-override should exist in MetricsPro.

pages.title: GP Category Map
pages.user_md:
### What this page shows
Maps sales departments/categories to GP report categories (so the Gross Profit report groups correctly).

### How to use it
Assign each department to a GP category.

### Top gotchas
1. Unmapped departments fall into a catch-all/Other on the GP report.
pages.support_md:
### Data sources
`GET/POST /commcalc/gp-category-map`; departments from `/commcalc/gp-departments`.

### Symptom -> diagnosis -> fix
- **GP grouped as Other** -> department not mapped. Map it.

### Escalation
Mapping = support-guidable; mapped-but-wrong grouping = escalate.

### Related settings
/commcalc/gp, /commcalc/item-mapping.

common_issues.symptom: Gross Profit lumps sales into 'Other'.
common_issues.diagnosis: Those departments aren't mapped to GP categories.
common_issues.fix: Map each department to its GP category here.
common_issues.escalate_when: Mapped and still grouped wrong -> escalate to platform operator.

pages.title: Implementation Wizard
pages.user_md:
### What this page shows
A hands-on wizard to detect a file's columns, map them, and upload mapped data for a carrier - the practical "get a file in" flow during implementation.

### How to use it
Upload a file, let it detect columns, confirm the mapping, then upload-mapped.

### Top gotchas
1. Column detection depends on the file; verify before uploading.
2. This is for setup - routine imports use the sweeps or Data Imports.
pages.support_md:
### Data sources
`apiUpload /commcalc/column-mapping/detect` + `/upload-mapped`; carriers + report-definitions + column-mapping.

### Symptom -> diagnosis -> fix
- **Detection wrong** -> non-standard export; correct the mapping.
- **Upload lands no data** -> wrong period/store spelling or empty mapping; verify (dates must be real date cells, not Excel serials).

### Escalation
Mapping/format = support-guidable; upload accepted but data missing = escalate.

### Related settings
/commcalc/column-mapping, /commcalc/onboarding, /commcalc/upload.

common_issues.symptom: Upload succeeds but no rows appear.
common_issues.diagnosis: Column mapping incomplete, or period/store spelling doesn't match how the app reads it, or dates were Excel serials.
common_issues.fix: Recheck the column mapping and that dates are real date cells; re-upload.
common_issues.escalate_when: Mapping correct, dates valid, still no rows -> escalate to platform operator.

pages.title: Item / Model Mapping
pages.user_md:
### What this page shows
Maps raw catalog items to device models/categories (single or bulk), with a seed-from-catalog helper.

### How to use it
Map items to models/categories; use bulk + seed-from-catalog to speed it up.

### Top gotchas
1. Unmapped items may miss device-based classification (activation/accessory).
2. Seed-from-catalog is a starting point - review the results.
pages.support_md:
### Data sources
`GET/POST /commcalc/item-mapping` (+ `/bulk`, `/facets`, `/seed-from-catalog`); `device-models`, `item-categories`.

### Symptom -> diagnosis -> fix
- **Items unclassified** -> not mapped to a model/category. Map or seed.

### Escalation
Mapping = support-guidable; mapped-but-misclassified = escalate.

### Related settings
/commcalc/gp-category-map, /commcalc/device-history.

common_issues.symptom: Some items aren't being classified as device vs accessory.
common_issues.diagnosis: The item isn't mapped to a model/category.
common_issues.fix: Map it (or bulk/seed-from-catalog) here.
common_issues.escalate_when: Mapped correctly and still misclassified -> escalate to platform operator.

pages.title: KPI Metrics
pages.user_md:
### What this page shows
Per-store / per-rep KPI numbers (the counts that drive Boost tier qualification) with store and rep filters.

### How to use it
Pick period + filters; review KPI attainment by store/rep.

### Top gotchas
1. Reads a snapshot, not live data - it refreshes after the daily DLAR sweep (Boost) or a Calculate, so brand-new data may lag.
2. KPI tiers only apply to Boost tenants; non-Boost tenants pay via plans.
pages.support_md:
### Data sources
Reads the `rep_commissions` / DLAR KPI snapshot (`raw_dlar_store`). `_do_dlar_sweep` (Boost, once daily) auto-recalcs and refreshes it. Unique store key = `raw_dlar_store.address`.

### Symptom -> diagnosis -> fix
- **Stale KPI numbers** -> snapshot not yet refreshed; wait for the daily DLAR sweep or a Calculate.
- **Store missing** -> store address not matched (store alias) or no DLAR rows.
- **Empty for non-Boost tenant** -> correct isolation; the KPI-tier model is Boost-only.

### Escalation
Data-freshness and mapping = support-guidable. Persistent wrong KPI after a fresh sweep = escalate to platform operator.

### Related settings
/commcalc/dlar/sweep, /commcalc/store-match.

common_issues.symptom: KPI numbers look out of date.
common_issues.diagnosis: The page reads a snapshot refreshed by the once-daily DLAR sweep, not live boostelevatego data.
common_issues.fix: Wait for the next daily sweep, or have the operator run the DLAR sweep / a Calculate.
common_issues.escalate_when: Snapshot is fresh (sweep ran today) but KPI still wrong -> escalate to platform operator.

pages.title: Total Processor Commissions (MA)
pages.user_md:
### What this page shows
Master-agent / processor commission detail for Total (VidaPay) tenants: per-subscriber MRC and M1-M6 spiffs from the MA Commission Details files.

### How to use it
Pick period; review MA commission rows by rep/sub.

### Top gotchas
1. Total's MI/ATU come from VidaPay MA reports, NOT ePay - a different data path from Boost.
2. Zeros here usually mean the MA file isn't ingested or product MRC prices are missing.
pages.support_md:
### Data sources
`raw_ma_commission` / `raw_ma_daily_tx` (mig 083). Ingested via Manual upload (carrier=Total) or the VidaPay email/portal pull. Period spelling 'June 2026' - reads via `_pvariants`.

### How the numbers work
Per-sub MRC + M1-M6 spiffs; negative = payout to dealer; multiple rows per IMEI/period (base + adjustment) are normal; don't key on line_status alone.

### Symptom -> diagnosis -> fix
- **Empty / $0** -> MA file not ingested for the period, or wrong org_id on the mailbox (another tenant's data mis-routed). Confirm the MA upload.
- **MRC shows $0** -> product_mrc price sheet not imported (pct_mrc -> $0). Import prices on /commcalc/payout-schedules.

### Escalation
Ingestion/pricing = support-guidable. Correct MA data rendering wrong = escalate to platform operator.

### Related settings
/commcalc/ma-upload, /commcalc/email-imports, /commcalc/payout-schedules (product MRC import).

common_issues.symptom: Total Processor page is empty for a Total tenant with known activations.
common_issues.diagnosis: MA Commission Details file not ingested for that period (Total data doesn't come through ePay/raw_mi).
common_issues.fix: Ingest the MA file via /commcalc/ma-upload (carrier=Total) or the VidaPay pull on /commcalc/email-imports.
common_issues.escalate_when: MA rows confirmed in the period and page still empty -> escalate to platform operator.

pages.title: Manual Report Upload (MA / carrier)
pages.user_md:
### What this page shows
A manual upload for a carrier/MA report when the automatic sweep can't get it - detect columns, map, and ingest (e.g. Total MA Commission Details).

### How to use it
Pick the carrier (e.g. Total), upload the file, confirm the detected mapping, ingest.

### Top gotchas
1. For Total tenants this is how MA commission data gets in when the VidaPay pull isn't available.
2. Ingesting here doesn't pay reps - a Calculate is still needed.
pages.support_md:
### Data sources
`apiUpload /commcalc/manual-upload/detect` + `/ingest`, mapping via `/manual-upload/mapping`. Lands in `raw_ma_commission` / related tables (carrier=Total).

### Symptom -> diagnosis -> fix
- **MA pages still empty after ingest** -> wrong carrier selected or wrong period spelling; verify.
- **Detection wrong** -> adjust the mapping.

### Escalation
Mapping/format = support-guidable; correct ingest not showing = escalate.

### Related settings
/commcalc/ma-commission, /commcalc/email-imports, /commcalc/device-history.

common_issues.symptom: After a manual MA upload, Total Processor / Device History still show $0.
common_issues.diagnosis: Wrong carrier tag on ingest, wrong period, or a downstream read that needs the MA data - confirm carrier=Total and the 'June 2026'-style period.
common_issues.fix: Re-ingest with the correct carrier + period; verify on /commcalc/ma-commission.
common_issues.escalate_when: MA rows present for the period and downstream pages still read $0 -> escalate to platform operator.

pages.title: All Mappings (hub)
pages.user_md:
### What this page shows
A hub linking to every mapping surface (store, column, GP category, item/model, rep aliases, custom target fields).

### How to use it
Use it to jump to the specific mapping you need.

### Top gotchas
1. It's navigation - the actual config lives on the linked pages.
pages.support_md:
### Data sources
Aggregates the mapping pages; no data of its own.

### Symptom -> diagnosis -> fix
- **A link 404s** -> confirm the specific mapping page loads directly.

### Escalation
Rare; a broken hub link = escalate.

### Related settings
store-match, column-mapping, gp-category-map, item-mapping, rep-aliases, target-fields.

common_issues.symptom: User can't find where to fix a mapping.
common_issues.diagnosis: Mapping config is spread across dedicated pages; the hub links them all.
common_issues.fix: Direct them from here to the right mapping page (store/column/GP/item/rep/target-field).
common_issues.escalate_when: A hub link leads to a broken page -> escalate to platform operator.

pages.title: Carrier / Company Onboarding Wizard
pages.user_md:
### What this page shows
A guided setup for onboarding a new carrier/company: carriers, KPI metrics, column mappings, connectors, distributors, an initial upload, and store matching.

### How to use it
Walk the steps to stand up a new tenant/carrier's commission setup.

### Top gotchas
1. It's a convenience wrapper over the individual config pages - each step maps to a standalone page.
2. Store-unmatched at the end means store aliases still need setting.
pages.support_md:
### Data sources
Orchestrates `/commcalc/carriers`, `/carrier-kpi-metrics`, `/column-mapping`, `/connectors`, `/distributors`, `/upload-mapped`, `/store-unmatched`.

### Symptom -> diagnosis -> fix
- **A step won't complete** -> the underlying config is incomplete; jump to the standalone page for that step.
- **Unmatched stores remain** -> add aliases on /commcalc/store-match.

### Escalation
Config = support-guidable; step endpoints erroring = escalate.

### Related settings
/commcalc/implementation, /commcalc/store-match, /commcalc/column-mapping.

common_issues.symptom: Onboarding wizard stalls on a step.
common_issues.diagnosis: That step's underlying config (carrier/mapping/connector) is incomplete.
common_issues.fix: Complete it on the dedicated page for that area, then resume.
common_issues.escalate_when: A step endpoint errors despite valid input -> escalate to platform operator.

pages.title: Device Forecasting & Vendor Payables
pages.user_md:
## Device Forecasting & Vendor Payables

Tracks, per IMEI, what is **owed to the vendor** vs the **rebate received**, reconciled against whether the device sold — plus phones-only stock **forecasting**. Four tabs:
- **Payables (per IMEI)** — owed, rebate, net owed, due date, status (discrepancy / due / offset / open). Click a row for the offset drill-down (what offsets what, incl. ePay cross-check).
- **Forecast (phones)** — sales velocity over a look-back window -> recommended order for the next N days, per carrier.
- **Daily Owed** — devices + $ owed grouped by due date.
- **Phone Mapping** — map each raw model name (as it appears in sales/inventory) to a canonical model + carrier so the forecast lines sales up with stock.

### What you can do
- **Rebuild ledger** — rebuilds the per-IMEI payable ledger from the per-carrier config.
- **Settings** — require clock-in acknowledgment of priority phones; set the priority window %.
- **Filter** by store / status; **export** the active tab.

### When to open a ticket
- Many rows show **unconfigured** or the forecast shows unmapped models.
- A device shows a rebate mismatch (ePay cross-check disagrees).
pages.support_md:
### Data sources & construction
- Router: `/api/v1/payables/*` (mounted at `/api/v1/payables`). Backend: `backend/app/modules/payables/**` (finance-owned backend; the frontend page lives under commcalc and is mod-commission's — coordinate on frontend changes).
- **Config-driven engine** (`payables/engine.py`, module 095): builds `commcalc.device_payable_ledger` from `commcalc.payable_source_map` (per-carrier). A NEW carrier is a **config row**, not code. The IMEI is the universal tally key joining device -> sales (sold?) and reimbursement (rebate received?).
- **Read-only** over `asset_ledger` (+ vip_invoices / raw_payment_detail). For Boost the DUE report equals /asset/owed-weekly because it COPIES billing_friday/bill_path/owed_to_vip verbatim — it never recomputes Friday billing.
- Phone mapping: `payable_source_map` + carrier `carrier` table; candidates are the unmapped raw models seen in sales/inventory.

### MUST-KNOW facts
- **Empty/unconfigured = correct isolation** until a `payable_source_map` row exists for the carrier. A tenant with no source map correctly shows nothing — universal, config-driven.
- Everything is org-scoped (multi-tenant); org_id is a query param.
- Rebate mismatch (ePay cross-check) flags where the primary rebate disagrees with the ePay lines — a recon signal, not necessarily an error.
- Payables/AP is distinct from the accounting-side Distributor liabilities (owed_vip / vip_ap on the Balance Sheet); this module is the per-IMEI vendor ledger + forecast.

### symptom -> diagnosis -> fix
- Rows show 'unconfigured' -> no payable_source_map for that carrier -> add a source-map row (carrier_id + source_table + imei_field) on the source-maps config.
- Forecast shows unmapped models -> raw model names not mapped -> map the highest-frequency ones on the Phone Mapping tab.
- Rebate mismatch warning -> ePay cross-check disagrees with the primary rebate -> open the row drill to compare; reconcile the source.
- Ledger looks stale after new data -> not rebuilt -> click Rebuild ledger.

### Escalation
Support: add source-map rows + phone mappings + settings in-UI, and Rebuild. Frontend changes touch a commcalc-owned page (coordinate with mod-commission); anything needing SQL/migrations -> platform operator.

common_issues.symptom: Payables rows show status 'unconfigured' for a carrier.
common_issues.diagnosis: No payable_source_map row exists for that carrier, so the engine can't build its ledger.
common_issues.fix: Add a source-map row (carrier_id + source_table + imei_field) via the payables source-maps config, then Rebuild ledger.
common_issues.escalate_when: The source table/field mapping is unclear or needs schema work — escalate to the platform operator.

common_issues.symptom: Forecast flags unmapped models / phones don't line up with stock.
common_issues.diagnosis: Raw model names in sales/inventory aren't mapped to a canonical model + carrier.
common_issues.fix: On the Phone Mapping tab, map the highest-frequency raw models to a canonical name + carrier, then Rebuild.
common_issues.escalate_when: Carrier records themselves are missing (no carrier to map to) — escalate.

common_issues.symptom: A device shows a rebate mismatch (⚠) on the ePay cross-check.
common_issues.diagnosis: The primary rebate amount disagrees with the ePay payment-detail lines for that IMEI.
common_issues.fix: Open the row drill-down to compare owed vs primary rebate vs ePay lines; reconcile against the source data.
common_issues.escalate_when: The discrepancy is a data-integrity issue in the source feeds — escalate.

common_issues.symptom: Forecasting/payables numbers look stale or empty.
common_issues.diagnosis: Underlying asset ledger / distributor data isn't up to date.
common_issues.fix: Ensure the asset ledger and distributor records are current (asset module upload).
common_issues.escalate_when: Data is current but the forecast is wrong -> escalate to platform operator.

pages.permissions_needed: Commcalc/Payables module access (org-scoped). Rebuild + config edits are per-tenant actions; frontend lives on a commcalc-owned page.

pages.title: Commission Payout Plans (Overview)
pages.user_md:
### What this page shows
An overview of how the tenant is set up to pay: which engine (Boost KPI tiers vs Commission Plans), plan coverage, and links to the config pages.

### How to use it
Use it as the hub for payout configuration - jump to Commission Plans, Schedules, Boost Rates, etc.

### Top gotchas
1. Non-Boost tenants pay ENTIRELY from Commission Plans - if reps show $0, start here to check plan coverage.
pages.support_md:
### Data sources
`GET /api/v1/commcalc/payout-plans/overview`. Summarizes commission_plan/assignment coverage and carrier mode.

### Symptom -> diagnosis -> fix
- **Reps unpaid** -> gaps in plan assignment; drill into Commission Plans.
- **Wrong engine** -> carrier mode is derived from the carrier, not editable here; confirm the tenant's carrier.

### Escalation
Coverage gaps = support-guidable. Carrier-mode misresolution = escalate.

### Related settings
/commcalc/commission-plans, /commcalc/payout-schedules, /commcalc/settings.

common_issues.symptom: Overview shows reps/stores with no plan coverage on a non-Boost tenant.
common_issues.diagnosis: Those reps have no Commission Plan assignment -> they will pay $0.
common_issues.fix: Assign plans on /commcalc/commission-plans, then have the operator Calculate.
common_issues.escalate_when: Coverage is complete but the engine still resolves the wrong way -> escalate to platform operator.

pages.title: Multi-Month Payout Schedules & Product MRC
pages.user_md:
### What this page shows
Carrier payout schedules (the M1-M6 template a carrier pays) and the product MRC price sheet that turns %-of-MRC spiffs into dollars. You can clone a carrier template and import a product-MRC price file.

### How to use it
Pick a carrier; edit its payout schedule or clone from a source; import the product MRC price sheet.

### Top gotchas
1. If product MRC prices are missing, %-based spiffs compute to $0 (pct_mrc -> $0).
2. Cloning a template is a starting point - verify the amounts match the carrier's real PDF.
pages.support_md:
### Data sources
`GET /commcalc/payout-schedule`, `carrier-template/sources|clone`, `product-mrc` (+ import). Seeded from carrier PDFs (e.g. Total Wireless mig 078).

### Symptom -> diagnosis -> fix
- **Spiffs $0** -> product MRC prices not imported. Import the price sheet here.
- **Schedule doesn't match carrier statement** -> wrong template/amounts; re-clone or edit (money-touching -> owner sign-off).

### Escalation
Price-sheet import = support-guidable. Schedule amount changes move pay = escalate to platform operator for owner approval.

### Related settings
/commcalc/plan-installments, /commcalc/ma-commission, /commcalc/carrier-mapping.

common_issues.symptom: Percentage-based spiffs are paying $0.
common_issues.diagnosis: product_mrc price sheet not imported, so %-of-MRC has no dollar base.
common_issues.fix: Import the product MRC price file on this page for the carrier.
common_issues.escalate_when: Prices imported and spiffs still $0 -> escalate to platform operator.

pages.title: Multi-Month Installments (sale-triggered)
pages.user_md:
### What this page shows
Sale-triggered multi-month commission schedules (M1-M6): a sale pays out across months, optionally gated on the carrier actually paying the dealer (residual received / line active). Includes edit + audit history.

### How to use it
Create/edit a schedule (trigger + month lines + gate mode). Edits are audited; nothing changes pay until the operator recomputes.

### Top gotchas
1. Gated installments stay "withheld" until the dealer-paid residual is seen - for MA/Total tenants this reads the MA files, not raw_mi.
2. Editing a schedule is money-touching; it only takes effect on the next Calculate.
pages.support_md:
### Data sources
`sale_installment_engine.py` (mig 201) + schedule edit/audit (mig 210). Gate evidence source is config-driven (mig 223): Boost -> raw_mi, MA -> raw_ma_commission.

### Symptom -> diagnosis -> fix
- **All M1-M6 withheld for an MA tenant** -> historically the gate read raw_mi only (fixed); now needs the MA residual file ingested for the gate month. Confirm MA ingestion.
- **Wrong month count paid** -> schedule line config; propose-first before editing.

### Escalation
Any schedule/gate change moves pay = propose-first + owner approval + operator recompute. Before the first Calculate after a gate change the operator takes an L3 snapshot; there's an `INSTALLMENT_GATE_LEGACY=1` kill switch - all operator territory.

### Related settings
/commcalc/commission-plans, /commcalc/payout-schedules, /commcalc/ma-upload.

common_issues.symptom: An MA/Total tenant's multi-month spiffs are all 'withheld - dealer unpaid'.
common_issues.diagnosis: The residual gate needs dealer-paid evidence; for MA tenants that's raw_ma_commission, which must be ingested for the gate month.
common_issues.fix: Confirm the MA commission file is ingested for the sale/gate month; then the operator recomputes.
common_issues.escalate_when: MA residual rows are present (negative = paid) and installments still withhold -> escalate to platform operator.

pages.title: Productivity & Reviews
pages.user_md:
### What this page shows
Per-rep productivity metrics and performance-review roll-ups for the period (leadership view).

### How to use it
Pick period + filters; review rep productivity and review status.

### Top gotchas
1. Visible to 'all'/'market' scopes only.
2. Numbers derive from the same sales/commission snapshot - refresh depends on the last Calculate/sweep.
pages.support_md:
### Data sources
Aggregates the rep commission snapshot + sales actuals. Read-only.

### Symptom -> diagnosis -> fix
- **Empty/stale** -> snapshot not refreshed or role scope excludes the market. Confirm scope + last recompute.

### Escalation
Data-freshness/scope = support-guidable; computed-value disputes = escalate.

### Related settings
/admin/roles, /commcalc/coaching.

common_issues.symptom: Page is empty for a market manager.
common_issues.diagnosis: Either no data for the period or the manager's market span is empty/mis-set.
common_issues.fix: Verify the user's scope/market assignment on /admin/roles and that the period has data.
common_issues.escalate_when: Scope correct, data present, still empty -> escalate to platform operator.

pages.title: Appeal Recovery (commission claw-back)
pages.user_md:
### What this page shows
Recoverable commission claw-backs / appeals - money the carrier clawed back that may be recoverable, tracked as claims.

### How to use it
Review claims; configure recovery rules on the config panel; export.

### Top gotchas
1. 'all'/'market' scopes only.
2. Claims derive from discrepancy/appeal data - thin input means thin claims.
pages.support_md:
### Data sources
`GET /api/v1/recovery/claims`, `GET /api/v1/recovery/config`. Fed by discrepancy + appeal/asset denial data.

### Symptom -> diagnosis -> fix
- **No claims** -> no discrepancies/appeals ingested, or config thresholds exclude them.
- **Claim amount looks wrong** -> underlying appeal denial detail; cross-check ePay Payment Detail.

### Escalation
Config/data = support-guidable; recovery math errors = escalate.

### Related settings
/commcalc/discrepancy, recovery config (on-page).

common_issues.symptom: Recovery shows no claims despite known clawbacks.
common_issues.diagnosis: Discrepancy/appeal data not ingested or config thresholds filter them out.
common_issues.fix: Run discrepancy for the period and check the recovery config thresholds.
common_issues.escalate_when: Clawbacks are in the data and still produce no claims -> escalate to platform operator.

pages.title: Rep Aliases
pages.user_md:
### What this page shows
Maps alternate rep name spellings (e.g. "Last, First" vs "First Last") to one canonical rep so their sales, commissions and targets don't split.

### How to use it
Add an alias linking each variant spelling to the real rep.

### Top gotchas
1. This is the fix when a rep's sales exist but they show $0/missing on commissions - the name didn't match.
2. Names display First Last; disambiguate same-name people by email.
pages.support_md:
### Data sources
`GET/POST /commcalc/rep-aliases`. The engine's name-matcher bridges "Last,First" <-> "First Last".

### Symptom -> diagnosis -> fix
- **Rep missing/$0 despite sales** -> name mismatch. Add an alias, then recompute.
- **One rep split into two** -> alias one spelling to the other (or merge on rep-map).

### Escalation
Aliasing = support-guidable. A recompute is money-touching (operator).

### Related settings
/commcalc/targets/rep-map, /commcalc/commission-plans, /commcalc/reports.

common_issues.symptom: A rep with clear sales shows $0 or is missing from commissions.
common_issues.diagnosis: Their sales-file name spelling doesn't match the roster/plan name.
common_issues.fix: Add a rep alias linking the spellings, then have the operator recompute.
common_issues.escalate_when: Alias added, name matches, and the rep still pays $0 after recompute -> escalate to platform operator.

pages.title: Report-Pull Mapping
pages.user_md:
### What this page shows
Maps each pulled report to how it's processed/ingested - the routing between an incoming report and its target table. Includes a reseed action.

### How to use it
Review/edit report-pull mappings; reseed defaults if needed.

### Top gotchas
1. An advanced integration config - most tenants use the seeded defaults.
2. A wrong mapping can send a report to the wrong ingest path.
pages.support_md:
### Data sources
`GET/POST /commcalc/report-pull-map`, `/report-pull-map/reseed`.

### Symptom -> diagnosis -> fix
- **A pulled report ingests wrong/nowhere** -> the report-pull mapping is off. Fix or reseed.

### Escalation
Mapping = support-guidable; reseed not resolving = escalate.

### Related settings
/commcalc/connectors, /commcalc/email-imports, /commcalc/column-mapping.

common_issues.symptom: A pulled report isn't landing in the right table.
common_issues.diagnosis: Its report-pull mapping is missing or wrong.
common_issues.fix: Correct the mapping (or reseed defaults) on this page.
common_issues.escalate_when: Mapping correct and the report still mis-ingests -> escalate to platform operator.

pages.title: Rep Commission Report
pages.user_md:
### What this page shows
The per-rep commission breakdown for the period - the detailed, exportable version of the dashboard, with a per-rep drill-in (magnifier) that opens the Commission Explain view.

### How to use it
Pick period + filters; review each rep's components. Use the drill-in to see how a rep's number was built. Export/Send as needed.

### Top gotchas
1. Reads the saved `rep_commissions` snapshot - stale-looking numbers need a recompute (money-touching).
2. $0 reps on non-Boost tenants are usually unassigned to a plan (not a bug).
pages.support_md:
### Data sources
Reads the `rep_commissions` snapshot for the period (same as the dashboard). Drill-in calls the Commission Explain endpoints.

### Symptom -> diagnosis -> fix
- **Stale numbers** -> snapshot predates the latest upload/name-matcher. A recompute fixes it, but Calculate is money-touching - confirm with operator/owner before firing.
- **$0 rep** -> non-Boost + no plan assignment, or the rep name didn't match (rep-alias). Assign plan / add rep alias.

### Escalation
Firing a recompute or diagnosing a wrong-but-configured payout = escalate to platform operator (money-touching).

### Related settings
/commcalc/commission-plans, /commcalc/rep-aliases, /commcalc/commission-explain.

common_issues.symptom: A rep is missing or shows $0 while their sales exist.
common_issues.diagnosis: Name mismatch between sales rows and roster (needs a rep alias) OR non-Boost tenant with no plan assignment.
common_issues.fix: Add a rep alias on /commcalc/rep-aliases and/or assign a Commission Plan, then have the operator recompute.
common_issues.escalate_when: Alias + plan confirmed correct and the rep still pays $0 -> escalate to platform operator.

pages.title: Sales Analyzer (3-Month Retention)
pages.user_md:
### What this page shows
3-month retention / churn drill-down: which activations stayed active vs churned, with drill-down to the accounts. Feeds chargeback review.

### How to use it
Pick period; drill from summary into churned accounts. Send suspected fraud to chargeback review.

### Top gotchas
1. The Analyzer's 3-month retention is NOT the same figure as DLAR's 3MR - they're computed differently.
2. Empty for a tenant with no history is normal.
pages.support_md:
### Data sources
Retention over `raw_sales`/feed activations across months; `GET/POST /api/v1/commcalc/chargeback-review` routes churned/fraud cases.

### Symptom -> diagnosis -> fix
- **3MR differs from DLAR** -> expected; different definitions/sources. Not a bug.
- **No churn data** -> not enough months ingested, or correct isolation.

### Escalation
Data-window questions = support-guidable; computation disputes = escalate.

### Related settings
/commcalc/chargebacks.

common_issues.symptom: Analyzer 3-month number doesn't match DLAR's 3MR.
common_issues.diagnosis: They are two different metrics from different sources - not reconcilable one-to-one.
common_issues.fix: Explain the distinction; use each in its own context. No action needed.
common_issues.escalate_when: A single metric is internally inconsistent (totals don't add up) -> escalate to platform operator.

pages.title: Sales Feed Recon
pages.user_md:
### What this page shows
Reconciles the daily B2B email sales feed against the authoritative monthly sales basis - what's in the feed vs what promoted into raw_sales.

### How to use it
Pick period; review rows present in one source but not the other.

### Top gotchas
1. A "missing in monthly" gap is usually a stale monthly upload, not lost sales.
2. The feed is authoritative for the CURRENT month; raw_sales for CLOSED months.
pages.support_md:
### Data sources
`sales_recon` over `daily_sales_feed` vs `raw_sales`. `_promote_feed_to_raw_sales` turns feed -> raw (gated on the tenant's report_definitions.auto for report_key='sales'). `_open_month_source` picks feed (current) vs raw_sales (closed).

### Symptom -> diagnosis -> fix
- **Large "missing in monthly"** -> monthly raw_sales upload is stale; the feed has newer data. Re-upload the current monthly file or let promotion run.
- **Feed empty** -> the B2B email feed isn't flowing (IMAP/mailbox). Check /commcalc/email-imports.

### Escalation
Upload/feed config = support-guidable. Promotion duplicating/compounding rows = escalate to platform operator (money-adjacent).

### Related settings
/commcalc/email-imports, /commcalc/upload, report_definitions auto (sales).

common_issues.symptom: Recon shows a big block of sales 'missing in monthly'.
common_issues.diagnosis: The monthly raw_sales file is stale; the hourly feed already has the newer transactions.
common_issues.fix: Re-upload the up-to-date monthly Sales Transaction Details file (or let feed -> raw promotion run for an open month).
common_issues.escalate_when: Feed and monthly are both current and still diverge, or promotion is duplicating rows -> escalate to platform operator.

pages.title: Sales Report
pages.user_md:
### What this page shows
Every sales line for the period from the POS/B2B data, grouped (default: by store, collapsed): activations, accessories, GP, swaps, and a pinned TOTAL row. The owner treats this as the source of truth for sales counts.

### How to use it
- Use the standard filter bar (period / stores / market / reps) - what you see is what exports.
- Expand a store group for line detail; export via Excel / PDF / Print / Send.
- The **classification (gear icon)** button configures how raw transactions map to activation/accessory buckets.

### Top gotchas
1. A "N transactions unclassified" banner means blank/unknown Contract Type lines aren't counted - fix in Classification, don't file a bug.
2. Low/zero numbers usually mean the wrong sales export was uploaded (needs the 78-column file).
3. A store appearing twice is usually a spelling variant (e.g. "Ave" vs "Avenue") - a mapping fix, not data loss.
pages.support_md:
### Data sources
- `_sales_rows_union` over `daily_sales_feed` (current month) + `raw_sales` (closed month), classified by `classify_contract_type` + the tenant's `accessory_config`.
- `GET /api/v1/commcalc/accessory-config` powers the Classification panel (contract-type map, box departments, set-up fee, blank-ct `activation_rules`).

### How the numbers are computed
Activations = DISTINCT trans_id per bucket; accessories via the accessory classifier; GP from the source file's GP columns. Store rows group by a canonical store key so spelling variants collapse.

### Symptom -> diagnosis -> fix
- **Unclassified banner / low activations** -> blank contract_type lines (a real Luxelink case ~77% one month). Fix in Classification: add contract-type map entries and/or blank-ct activation rules (dept/category/product -> premium/upgrade/byod). Config-driven, no code.
- **All $0 / missing GP+accessories** -> reduced/legacy export. Re-upload the 78-col Sales Transaction Details with Contract Type + Department + Category + Ext Price + GP; dates must be real date cells, not Excel serials.
- **Store listed twice** -> spelling drift between sales and targets/roster. Add a store alias on /commcalc/store-match.
- **Empty for a non-house tenant** -> often correct multi-tenant isolation (no sales uploaded yet), not a bug.

### Escalation
Classification/mapping/upload = support-guidable via config UI. A correctly-classified file that still miscounts, or the report disagreeing line-for-line with the raw file = escalate to platform operator.

### Related settings
Classification (accessory_config), /commcalc/store-match, /commcalc/gp-category-map, /commcalc/upload.

common_issues.symptom: Banner says 'N transactions unclassified - map in Classification'.
common_issues.diagnosis: Those lines have blank/unrecognized contract_type, so activations under-count. A configuration gap, not a bug.
common_issues.fix: Open Classification, add contract-type map entries or blank-ct activation rules (per-org config) so the lines classify.
common_issues.escalate_when: Rules are configured to match the lines and they still show unclassified -> escalate to platform operator.

common_issues.symptom: Sales totals are far lower than the store expects (or $0).
common_issues.diagnosis: Wrong sales file uploaded (reduced/legacy export missing key columns) or dates stored as Excel serials.
common_issues.fix: Re-upload the 78-column Sales Transaction Details export with real date cells; recheck.
common_issues.escalate_when: Correct file confirmed and totals still wrong -> escalate to platform operator.

pages.title: Boost Rates (KPI-tier) - Commission Settings
pages.user_md:
### What this page shows
The Boost/house KPI-tier rate settings: the 8 hardcoded components and the KPI-count tiers (100/75/50%) the legacy Boost engine pays from.

### How to use it
Adjust Boost rates/tiers here (Boost tenant only). Changes are money-touching and take effect on the next Calculate.

### Top gotchas
1. These rates are carrier-gated - they only apply to Boost tenants. A non-Boost tenant editing them changes nothing (it pays via Commission Plans).
2. Any rate/tier edit moves pay - propose-first.
pages.support_md:
### Data sources
Boost rate config consumed by `calculator.py`. Only used when `carrier_mode='boost'`.

### Symptom -> diagnosis -> fix
- **Edited rates didn't change a non-Boost tenant** -> correct; that tenant uses Commission Plans.
- **Boost payouts wrong after edit** -> recompute needed; verify the edit and Calculate.

### Escalation
Rate/tier changes are money-touching = propose-first + owner approval + operator recompute.

### Related settings
/commcalc/commission-plans (non-Boost), /commcalc/payout-plans.

common_issues.symptom: A non-Boost tenant changed Boost Rates and nothing happened.
common_issues.diagnosis: Boost Rates are carrier-gated to carrier_mode='boost'; non-Boost tenants pay via Commission Plans, so these settings are inert for them.
common_issues.fix: Point the user to /commcalc/commission-plans instead.
common_issues.escalate_when: A Boost tenant edits rates and payouts don't reflect it after Calculate -> escalate to platform operator.

pages.title: Store Matching (aliases)
pages.user_md:
### What this page shows
Store aliases that collapse different spellings/codes of the same store into one canonical store (fixes double-listed stores and unmatched sales).

### How to use it
Map each raw store spelling to its canonical store. Pick from the real store roster.

### Top gotchas
1. Fixes the classic "same store listed twice" (e.g. "Ave" vs "Avenue") and sales landing under an unknown store.
2. Store IDs/keys are stored, not free-text names.
pages.support_md:
### Data sources
`GET/POST /commcalc/store-aliases`. Canonical stores from `store_mapping` / the store roster. Used by the sales union's canonical store grouping.

### Symptom -> diagnosis -> fix
- **Store double-listed on reports** -> add an alias mapping the variant to the canonical store.
- **Sales under an unknown store** -> the raw store string isn't aliased; map it.

### Escalation
Aliasing = support-guidable; an alias that doesn't take effect = escalate.

### Related settings
/commcalc/mapping, /commcalc/targets/rep-map, Sales Report/Exec MTD.

common_issues.symptom: The same physical store appears as two rows on reports.
common_issues.diagnosis: Its name is spelled two ways across sales vs targets/roster and isn't aliased.
common_issues.fix: Add a store alias here mapping both spellings to one canonical store.
common_issues.escalate_when: Alias added and the duplicate persists across reports -> escalate to platform operator.

pages.title: Custom Target Fields
pages.user_md:
### What this page shows
Define custom fields (per report_key) that targets and mappings can reference - extends the standard field set for a tenant's data.

### How to use it
Add custom fields tied to a report_key; they become available in mapping/targets.

### Top gotchas
1. Advanced config - only needed when a tenant's data has fields beyond the standard set.
pages.support_md:
### Data sources
`GET/POST /commcalc/target-fields` (by report_key).

### Symptom -> diagnosis -> fix
- **A field isn't available to map** -> not defined here for the report_key. Add it.

### Escalation
Config = support-guidable; a defined field not appearing = escalate.

### Related settings
/commcalc/column-mapping, /commcalc/targets/settings.

common_issues.symptom: A needed field isn't offered in column mapping/targets.
common_issues.diagnosis: The custom field isn't defined for that report_key.
common_issues.fix: Define it here, then it appears in mapping/targets.
common_issues.escalate_when: Defined and still not selectable -> escalate to platform operator.

pages.title: Daily Targets
pages.user_md:
### What this page shows
Daily sales targets by store/rep and actual-vs-target progress, with a projection engine that spreads the month's goal across open days (catch-up rule for missed days).

### How to use it
Pick period + filters; review target vs actual per store/rep/day.

### Top gotchas
1. Targets need to be configured first (Target Settings) - no config, no targets.
2. Actuals derive from the same sales aggregation as the Sales Report; blank contract_type undercounts here too.
pages.support_md:
### Data sources
`targets_engine.py` (projects future open days from the weekly pattern) + `_compute_feed_actuals_py` over the sales union. Target types are defined in Target Settings.

### Symptom -> diagnosis -> fix
- **No targets** -> not set up. Fix on /commcalc/targets/settings.
- **Actuals look low** -> blank contract_type / wrong sales file - same fix as Sales Report (Classification / re-upload).

### Escalation
Config/data = support-guidable; projection math errors = escalate.

### Related settings
/commcalc/targets/settings, /commcalc/targets/rep-map, Classification.

common_issues.symptom: A store shows targets of 0 or no target at all.
common_issues.diagnosis: Targets not configured for the store, or the rep -> store map is missing.
common_issues.fix: Set targets on /commcalc/targets/settings and confirm the rep -> store map (/commcalc/targets/rep-map).
common_issues.escalate_when: Targets configured and actuals still wrong after classification is correct -> escalate to platform operator.

pages.title: Accessory Sales Targets
pages.user_md:
### What this page shows
Accessory-specific sales targets and attainment (accessory $ per day), including the device set-up fee counting toward the accessory target.

### How to use it
Pick period + filters; review accessory target vs actual.

### Top gotchas
1. Set-up fee counts toward the accessory TARGET but is reported as a separate pay item - don't fold it into accessory commission basis.
2. Accessory numbers use the accessory classifier (intentionally divergent across surfaces).
pages.support_md:
### Data sources
Targets engine + accessory actuals via `accessory_config`. Set-up-fee handling per mig 217.

### Symptom -> diagnosis -> fix
- **Accessory actual $0** -> wrong sales export (no accessory columns) or classifier config.
- **Set-up fee double-counted** -> it's target-only, a separate pay item; verify config.

### Escalation
Config/data = support-guidable; classifier changes are owner-gated.

### Related settings
Classification (accessory_config), /commcalc/targets/settings.

common_issues.symptom: Accessory attainment shows $0 despite accessory sales.
common_issues.diagnosis: Reduced sales export missing Department/Category, or the accessory classifier config.
common_issues.fix: Re-upload the full 78-col file and/or adjust Classification.
common_issues.escalate_when: Full file + correct classifier and still $0 -> escalate to platform operator.

pages.title: Daily Action Plan
pages.user_md:
### What this page shows
The daily action plan derived from targets: what each store/rep needs to sell today to stay on pace, including catch-up for missed days.

### How to use it
Pick period + filters; read the per-store/rep daily plan.

### Top gotchas
1. Depends entirely on targets being set.
2. If a store was closed on a day, catch-up redistributes to open days.
pages.support_md:
### Data sources
`targets_engine.py` projection (open-day pattern) + actuals. Read-only.

### Symptom -> diagnosis -> fix
- **Blank plan** -> no targets configured.
- **Plan looks too aggressive** -> catch-up from missed days redistributed the remaining goal; expected.

### Escalation
Config = support-guidable; projection errors = escalate.

### Related settings
/commcalc/targets/settings, /commcalc/targets.

common_issues.symptom: Action plan is empty.
common_issues.diagnosis: No targets set, so nothing to plan against.
common_issues.fix: Configure targets on /commcalc/targets/settings.
common_issues.escalate_when: Targets set and plan still blank/wrong -> escalate to platform operator.

pages.title: My Targets
pages.user_md:
### What this page shows
The logged-in rep's own targets and progress - the self-service view for a salesperson.

### How to use it
A rep opens it to see their target vs actual for the period.

### Top gotchas
1. If a rep sees nothing, their identity may not be mapped to their sales rows (rep alias / rep -> store map).
pages.support_md:
### Data sources
Self-scoped targets/actuals for the caller's rep identity.

### Symptom -> diagnosis -> fix
- **Rep sees no targets** -> their user isn't linked to a rep record / store, or no targets set. Fix: rep alias + rep -> store map + Target Settings.

### Escalation
Identity/config = support-guidable; correct mapping but empty = escalate.

### Related settings
/commcalc/rep-aliases, /commcalc/targets/rep-map, /commcalc/targets/settings.

common_issues.symptom: A rep's My Targets page is blank.
common_issues.diagnosis: Their login isn't linked to their rep/sales identity, or no targets were set for their store.
common_issues.fix: Link the rep (rep-aliases / rep-map) and confirm targets exist in Target Settings.
common_issues.escalate_when: Mapping + targets confirmed and still blank -> escalate to platform operator.

pages.title: Rep -> Store Map / Merge Duplicate Reps
pages.user_md:
### What this page shows
Maps reps to stores for targeting, and merges duplicate rep records that came in under slightly different names.

### How to use it
Assign reps to stores; merge duplicates so one person's numbers don't split.

### Top gotchas
1. Duplicate reps split a person's targets/actuals - merge them here.
2. Names are shown First Last; disambiguate same-name people by email.
pages.support_md:
### Data sources
Rep -> store assignment used by the targets engine; rep identity relates to `rep-aliases`.

### Symptom -> diagnosis -> fix
- **A rep's numbers are split across two rows** -> duplicate rep records. Merge here (and/or add a rep alias).
- **Rep on the wrong store's targets** -> reassign.

### Escalation
Mapping = support-guidable; a merge that mis-combines two different people = escalate.

### Related settings
/commcalc/rep-aliases, /commcalc/targets.

common_issues.symptom: One salesperson appears twice with split targets/actuals.
common_issues.diagnosis: Duplicate rep records from name spelling drift.
common_issues.fix: Merge the duplicates here (or add a rep alias on /commcalc/rep-aliases).
common_issues.escalate_when: A merge combined two genuinely different people -> escalate to platform operator to unwind.

pages.title: Target Settings
pages.user_md:
### What this page shows
Where targets are configured: target types, values, and the catch-up/projection behavior for each store/rep.

### How to use it
Define target types and values here before expecting anything on the Targets pages.

### Top gotchas
1. This is the prerequisite for every targets page.
2. Target types are defined here (the engine has a fixed set of type kinds).
pages.support_md:
### Data sources
Writes the targets config consumed by `targets_engine.py`.

### Symptom -> diagnosis -> fix
- **Targets pages empty** -> nothing configured here yet.
- **Wrong projection** -> check catch-up settings.

### Escalation
Config = support-guidable; engine projecting wrong from correct config = escalate.

### Related settings
/commcalc/targets, /commcalc/target-fields.

common_issues.symptom: All targets pages are empty for a store.
common_issues.diagnosis: Targets have not been configured in Target Settings.
common_issues.fix: Configure the target types/values here for the store/rep.
common_issues.escalate_when: Configured correctly but targets pages still show nothing -> escalate to platform operator.

pages.title: Tax Collected
pages.user_md:
### What this page shows
Sales tax collected, summarized by store/period from the sales data.

### How to use it
Pick period + filters; review tax collected; export.

### Top gotchas
1. Depends on the tax field being present in the sales export.
2. 'all'/'market' scopes only.
pages.support_md:
### Data sources
Derived from the sales union tax fields for the org/period.

### Symptom -> diagnosis -> fix
- **No tax figures** -> sales export lacks the tax column, or wrong file. Re-upload the full export.

### Escalation
Upload = support-guidable; wrong tax math on good data = escalate.

### Related settings
/commcalc/upload.

common_issues.symptom: Tax Collected is empty or zero.
common_issues.diagnosis: The uploaded sales file doesn't carry the tax field, or the wrong file/period.
common_issues.fix: Re-upload the full 78-col Sales Transaction Details export for the period.
common_issues.escalate_when: Correct file with tax present and still empty -> escalate to platform operator.

pages.title: Data Imports (Upload Files)
pages.user_md:
### What this page shows
The unified Data Imports page: upload the sales file and other monthly files, with per-month "Uploaded" badges + upload history so you can see exactly which file each month got.

### How to use it
Pick the file type + month and upload. Check the badge/history to confirm the right file went in.

### Top gotchas
1. Use the 78-column "Sales Transaction Details" export (has Contract Type, Department, Category, Ext Price, GP). A reduced/legacy export ingests every dollar as 0 -> $0 commissions and $0 accessories.
2. Dates must be real date-formatted cells, not Excel serial numbers.
3. Uploading does NOT recompute - a Calculate is still required for pay to change.
pages.support_md:
### Data sources
Ingests into `raw_sales` (monthly basis) and related tables. The daily B2B email feed (`daily_sales_feed`) is the primary source; manual upload is the fallback. Upload-history badges surface which file each month received.

### Symptom -> diagnosis -> fix
- **$0 month after upload** -> wrong/reduced export. Re-upload the full 78-col Sales Transaction Details file, then Calculate. The upload-history badge is how you catch a dead legacy file being uploaded.
- **Dollars ingest as 0** -> dates were Excel serials or the file lacked Ext Price/GP. Re-export with real dates + full columns.
- **Upload didn't change pay** -> uploads don't recalc; run Calculate.

### Escalation
File-format/upload = support-guidable. An ingest that accepts a correct 78-col file but stores zeros = escalate to platform operator.

### Related settings
/commcalc/upload/wizard, /commcalc/column-mapping, /commcalc/store-match, dashboard Calculate.

common_issues.symptom: After uploading, the month shows $0 commissions and $0 accessories.
common_issues.diagnosis: The reduced/legacy export was uploaded (missing Contract Type/Department/Category/Ext Price/GP), so every dollar ingested as 0. The upload-history badge reveals the dead legacy file.
common_issues.fix: Re-upload the 78-column 'Sales Transaction Details' export with real date cells, then run Calculate from the dashboard.
common_issues.escalate_when: The correct 78-col file is confirmed uploaded and it still stores zeros -> escalate to platform operator.

common_issues.symptom: User uploaded a new file but payouts didn't change.
common_issues.diagnosis: Ingest never triggers a recompute.
common_issues.fix: Have them press Calculate for that period (poll; don't re-fire on a 502).
common_issues.escalate_when: Calculate runs clean but numbers ignore the new file -> escalate to platform operator.

pages.title: Upload Wizard
pages.user_md:
### What this page shows
A step-by-step guided upload (choose connector/type, map, confirm) - a friendlier path than the raw Data Imports page.

### How to use it
Follow the steps; it uses your configured connectors.

### Top gotchas
1. Same file rules as Data Imports (78-col sales file, real dates).
2. Uploading doesn't recompute.
pages.support_md:
### Data sources
Uses `/commcalc/connectors` + the mapped-upload path. Same ingest targets as Data Imports.

### Symptom -> diagnosis -> fix
- Same as Data Imports: wrong export -> $0; real dates required; Calculate after.

### Escalation
Same as Data Imports.

### Related settings
/commcalc/upload, /commcalc/connectors, /commcalc/column-mapping.

common_issues.symptom: Wizard upload results in a $0 month.
common_issues.diagnosis: Reduced/legacy sales export or Excel-serial dates.
common_issues.fix: Re-upload the full 78-col file with real date cells; Calculate.
common_issues.escalate_when: Correct file and still zeros -> escalate to platform operator.

pages.title: Distributor Invoices (VIP)
pages.user_md:
### What this page shows
Distributor (VIP) invoices - uploaded/scraped invoices, summaries, and per-invoice detail used to reconcile what's owed.

### How to use it
Upload or review invoices; open an invoice for line detail.

### Top gotchas
1. Distributor invoices join to assets by SERIAL (not IMEI) - a mismatch can look like a missing device.
2. 'all' scope for sweep actions.
pages.support_md:
### Data sources
VIP invoice tables + `vip_invoice_devices` (join key = SERIAL). Loader/scraper feeds it.

### Symptom -> diagnosis -> fix
- **Invoice device won't match an asset** -> join is by SERIAL; check the serial, not IMEI.
- **No invoices** -> none uploaded/swept for the org.

### Escalation
Upload/join = support-guidable; scraper failures = escalate.

### Related settings
/commcalc/vip/sweep, /commcalc/vip/paygo, /commcalc/distributors.

common_issues.symptom: An invoiced device doesn't tie to an asset record.
common_issues.diagnosis: VIP invoice <-> asset join is on SERIAL, not IMEI.
common_issues.fix: Match on the device serial; confirm the serial is present on both sides.
common_issues.escalate_when: Serials match and still no join -> escalate to platform operator.

pages.title: Distributor Asset Lending (PayGo)
pages.user_md:
### What this page shows
PayGo / asset-lending weekly billing for a distributor - devices lent out and the weekly liability owed.

### How to use it
Review lent devices and the weekly owed amounts.

### Top gotchas
1. Only appears when the distributor has asset-lending enabled.
2. PayGo-pending owed is a REAL liability - do not treat it as a double-count.
pages.support_md:
### Data sources
PayGo weekly billing over lent assets; gated behind the distributor's asset-lending capability (sweep behind a toggle).

### Symptom -> diagnosis -> fix
- **Page hidden** -> distributor asset-lending is off (enable on /commcalc/distributors).
- **Owed looks doubled** -> PayGo-pending owed is a standalone real liability, not a duplicate.

### Escalation
Capability config = support-guidable; billing math disputes = escalate (verified-correct behavior - don't reverse on an appeal).

### Related settings
/commcalc/distributors, /commcalc/vip/sweep.

common_issues.symptom: Someone says the PayGo owed amount is double-counted.
common_issues.diagnosis: PayGo-pending owed is a real, standalone liability (it was wrongly zeroed once and restored). It is NOT a double-count.
common_issues.fix: Explain it's a verified-correct liability; do not remove it.
common_issues.escalate_when: There is a specific, evidenced reconciliation error (not just a hunch) -> escalate to platform operator.

pages.title: Distributor Auto-Sweep
pages.user_md:
### What this page shows
The auto-sweep that pulls distributor invoices/data (e.g. the VIP portal). Status and run controls.

### How to use it
Review sweep status; trigger a run if permitted.

### Top gotchas
1. Portal scrapers can be blocked by device-trust/2FA - a failed sweep is often an auth/portal issue.
2. 'all' scope only.
pages.support_md:
### Data sources
Runs the distributor/VIP scraper into the invoice tables. Creds configured per the scraper.

### Symptom -> diagnosis -> fix
- **Sweep fails at login** -> portal 2FA/device-trust or IP block; may require the operator's trusted egress or manual upload.

### Escalation
Auth/portal failures = escalate to platform operator (creds/egress). Support can advise manual invoice upload meanwhile.

### Related settings
/commcalc/vip, /commcalc/email-imports.

common_issues.symptom: Distributor sweep fails to pull invoices.
common_issues.diagnosis: Portal login blocked (2FA / biometric device-trust / IP block) - a known scraper limitation.
common_issues.fix: Advise manual invoice upload on /commcalc/vip meanwhile; the sweep needs operator-side auth/egress.
common_issues.escalate_when: Sweep repeatedly fails at login -> escalate to platform operator.

pages.title: What-If / Scenario Analysis
pages.user_md:
### What this page shows
Carrier-agnostic scenario tools: model commission outcomes, carrier income (what the carrier/master-agent pays the company), and BYOD-residual analysis for any carrier the tenant has. Pick a carrier at the top; every tab follows it.

### How to use it
Pick a carrier, adjust the scenario inputs, read the modeled result. Read-only - it never changes real pay.

### Top gotchas
1. Analysis only - nothing here writes pay or fires a recompute.
2. For MA/Total carriers the inputs come from the MA files; verify the source file before trusting decisions.
pages.support_md:
### Data sources
- `whatif.py`, carrier resolved via `_resolve_carrier_mode` ('boost' vs 'plan').
- Source selection is CONFIG (`commcalc.whatif_source_config`, mig 209): per-(org,carrier) or mode-default, with two seeded house rows every tenant inherits. Boost -> raw_mi MI+ATU; plan/MA -> raw_ma_commission + tenure.

### Symptom -> diagnosis -> fix
- **Zeros for a Total carrier** -> MA source not ingested or the whatif_source_config points at the wrong table. Config-tunable on the page (Sources gear).
- **Wrong carrier behaviour** -> wrong carrier picked, or carrier row misconfigured.

### Escalation
Source-config = support-guidable (Sources gear). A resolver returning wrong money for a correctly-configured source = escalate to platform operator.

### Related settings
Sources (whatif_source_config), /commcalc/carrier-mapping, /commcalc/ma-upload.

common_issues.symptom: What-If shows $0 income/residual for an MA/Total carrier.
common_issues.diagnosis: The MA source file isn't ingested for the period, or the source config points at an empty/wrong table.
common_issues.fix: Confirm MA data is ingested; adjust the Sources config on the page to the correct source. Read-only, safe to retune.
common_issues.escalate_when: Source confirmed correct + populated and it still models $0 -> escalate to platform operator.

pages.title: Configurations hub
pages.user_md:
## Configurations

Every settings/configuration screen in one place — a hub of cards grouped by area (Company & Setup, Access & Roles, Communications, Commissions & Pay, Targets, Data Imports & Connectors, StoreOps & Closing, People, Helpdesk, Platform). Each card links to the page that owns that config; those pages keep their own routes too.

Recommended onboarding order: start with **Company Setup** (pay period + carriers), then Org Structure, Roles & Access, then module configs.

Platform cards (Companies, Billing) appear only for super-admins.
pages.support_md:
## How it works

Static hub — a hardcoded card list in the page filtered by `adminOnly` (super-admin). No data of its own; every issue on a linked page belongs to that page's doc. If a linked page 404s or redirects for a user, that's the ROLE lacking the target module key (seeded modules are forward-only — grant at /admin/roles), not a hub bug.

## Symptom → diagnosis → fix

- A card's target page redirects/shows nothing → role lacks the target module → grant at /admin/roles, re-login.
- "Companies/Billing cards missing" → user is not a super-admin (expected).

common_issues.symptom: Card visible but target page inaccessible
common_issues.diagnosis: The hub does not gate per-card on module keys; the target page enforces its own RBAC.
common_issues.fix: Grant the needed module/page on the user's role.
common_issues.escalate_when: Access granted + re-login and the target still fails.

pages.permissions_needed: Any signed-in user; super-admin cards for super-admins only. Target pages enforce their own permissions.
related_settings: Everything — this page indexes all config surfaces

pages.title: Employee Dashboard
pages.user_md:
**What it's for:** an individual's own performance/schedule/pay/flags dashboard — defaults to the
signed-in employee's own record; a manager/admin can switch to any employee they're allowed to see
via the picker. Includes "My Chargebacks" (always the CALLER's own, never the viewed employee's) and
"My Reports."

**When to open a ticket:** the dashboard is blank/errors for a specific period, or the employee
picker is missing people who should be visible to a manager.
pages.support_md:
**Data sources:** `GET /storeops/employees/visible` (role-scoped picker list),
`GET /core/employee-dashboard?org_id&employee_id&period`, plus commission coaching/targets calls
keyed off the **sales rep name** (not the short display name) — a mismatch there silently scopes
coaching/targets to nobody.

**Symptom → diagnosis → fix**
- *Dashboard blank for a valid period*: check the employee actually has data for that period (sales/
  hours/commission) — an employee with no activity that month legitimately shows blank widgets.
- *Employee picker missing someone a manager should see*: `/storeops/employees/visible` is
  role/scope-gated (self → just them; store → their store; market/DM → their stores; admin →
  everyone) — same org-tree/span root cause as My Team/Time Off empty views.
- *Coaching/targets widgets blank while the main dashboard has data*: these key off the employee's
  **rep_name** used in sales data (e.g. "ali, mohammad khalid"), not their short display name — if
  that mapping is off, coaching/targets return nothing even though hours/pay show fine.

**Escalate when:** the picker's scope is confirmed correct (org tree/role checked) and a specific
employee is STILL invisible to a manager who should see them — escalate to platform operator.

common_issues.symptom: Coaching/targets sections are blank but hours and pay show correctly
common_issues.diagnosis: These key off the employee's sales rep_name mapping, not their short display name — likely a name-mapping gap between StoreOps and the sales data.
common_issues.fix: Check the employee's rep_name mapping (ePay salesperson field on StoreOps Employees) matches how they appear in sales data.
common_issues.escalate_when: Mapping looks correct and coaching/targets are still empty — escalate to mod-commission.

common_issues.symptom: A manager can't find a specific employee in the picker
common_issues.diagnosis: Same org-tree/span root cause as other empty-manager-view issues — check org placement.
common_issues.fix: Correct the manager's org-tree unit assignment.
common_issues.escalate_when: Org placement is correct and the employee is still missing from the picker.

pages.permissions_needed: Any logged-in employee (own record) + manager/admin (others per scope)
related_settings: Org hierarchy / role scope (drives who's visible in the picker)

pages.title: Failure Logs
pages.user_md:
## Failure Logs

A system log of things the app couldn't complete (e.g. a valid rep rejected by kiosk face-match) — each entry carries a **how-to-fix** note. Admin-only by default; grant the /failures page to a role at Roles & Access to share it.

- Filter by status (open/resolved/ignored), type, date range, stores, and employees; export Excel/PDF from the bar.
- Click "how to fix" on a row to expand the remediation + technical detail.
- Resolve / Ignore / Reopen per row.
- **Clock-in face sensitivity:** the slider controls how close a live face must match (default 0.60; higher = easier match). If many valid reps get rejected, nudge toward 0.65. You can also untick failure types to stop logging them.

**If a user reports "system error Reference:<id>"** — this page is the first stop: search the reference id here and follow the entry's how-to-fix.
pages.support_md:
## How it works

Backed by `core.failure_log` (mig 112) — endpoints `GET/POST/PATCH /core/failures`, `GET /core/failure-types`, `GET/PUT /core/failures/config` (face threshold + disabled categories; `can_configure` gates edits). Kiosk face rejects auto-log `face_mismatch`. The face threshold is tenant-configurable and takes effect on the next clock-in immediately after save.

**Support flow for "system error Reference:<id>":** open /failures → clear the status filter (All statuses) → find the entry whose detail carries the reference id → the row's remediation says what to do. If the category is one support can act on (role/config/data), do it via the admin UIs; if the remediation calls for SQL, env vars, or a deploy, escalate to the platform operator with the reference id and the row's detail JSON.

## Symptom → diagnosis → fix

- Error mentions migration 112 → failure_log table missing in this environment → platform operator runs 112_failure_log.sql.
- Valid reps rejected at kiosk clock-in → face threshold too strict → raise slider toward 0.65, Save (immediate).
- A known-noisy failure type flooding the list → untick it under "Log these failure types" (stops NEW logging; existing rows can be Ignored).
- Config slider disabled → user lacks configure rights → admin role or settings grant needed.

common_issues.symptom: User got 'system error Reference:<id>'
common_issues.diagnosis: The app logged a structured failure with that reference.
common_issues.fix: Search the id here (all statuses), read the how-to-fix, apply it via admin UIs.
common_issues.escalate_when: Remediation requires SQL/env/deploy, no matching entry exists, or the same reference recurs after the fix — platform operator with the id + detail JSON.

common_issues.symptom: Kiosk rejects a legitimate employee's face
common_issues.diagnosis: face_mismatch entries; threshold (default 0.60) too strict for conditions/enrollment photo.
common_issues.fix: Raise the sensitivity slider slightly (e.g. 0.62–0.65) and Save; consider re-enrolling the employee's photo.
common_issues.escalate_when: Rejections persist at lenient settings — module owner reviews the enrollment/matching pipeline.

common_issues.symptom: Page not in a manager's nav
common_issues.diagnosis: Admin-gated by default; role lacks the /failures page grant.
common_issues.fix: Grant the page/module to the role at /admin/roles (forward-only seeding applies).
common_issues.escalate_when: Granted + re-login and still hidden.

pages.permissions_needed: Admin by default; shareable by granting the /failures page to a role. Config edits gated separately (can_configure).

pages.title: Helpdesk inbox
pages.user_md:
## Helpdesk

The ticket inbox. What you see depends on your role: agents (any scope above "self") see ALL org tickets with All / Assigned to me / Unassigned views; regular users see only their own tickets.

- Filter by status, priority, subject search, date range, and requester; export the visible list to Excel/PDF.
- Click a ticket to open it; "Raise a ticket" starts a new one.
- Agents also get Dashboard and (admins) Settings shortcuts, plus the AI Assistant when granted.

This is also the escalation channel of record: account problems that support can't fix in the admin UIs (e.g. reinstating a disabled login) should be raised here or to support@metricspro.tech.
pages.support_md:
## How it works

`GET /helpdesk/tickets` with agent/requester/view/status/priority/search params — agent view is decided client-side by `permissions.scope !== 'self'` and enforced by passing the requester email for self-scope users. Config (statuses/priorities) from `/helpdesk/config/bootstrap`. The helpdesk module must be enabled for the org (a disabled module returns an error from every endpoint) and granted on the role for nav to show.

## Symptom → diagnosis → fix

- User sees no tickets though some exist → they are self-scope and not the requester of any → expected; agents need scope above self.
- Helpdesk absent from nav → role lacks the helpdesk module key (forward-only seeding) → grant at /admin/roles.
- Every helpdesk call errors → module not enabled for the org → platform operator/entitlements.
- New-ticket emails not arriving → per-category alert emails / shared list not set → /helpdesk/settings.

common_issues.symptom: Manager can't see team tickets
common_issues.diagnosis: Their role scope is 'self' — agent features require a broader scope.
common_issues.fix: Adjust the role's data scope at /admin/roles (or use a proper agent role).
common_issues.escalate_when: Scope is market/store/all and the agent view still shows nothing.

pages.permissions_needed: Helpdesk module on the role. Agent capabilities = scope above 'self'. Settings link shows for admin module or scope 'all'.

pages.title: Ticket detail
pages.user_md:
## Ticket detail

The full conversation for one ticket: description, comments, attachments, and (for agents) the control rail — status, priority, category, and assignee (picked from the org user roster).

- Comment to reply; agents can mark a comment **internal** (requesters never see internal notes).
- Attach files; click an attachment to open it (temporary signed link).
- Requesters see their own ticket and public comments only.
pages.support_md:
## How it works

`GET/PATCH /helpdesk/tickets/{id}` (+`agent` flag: requester view hides internal comments), `POST .../comments` (is_internal), attachments upload + signed-URL open. Assignee picker: org app_users roster; the value stored is the display NAME string (data-compat) — an off-roster legacy assignee stays selectable but no new free-text assignee can be typed. Only agents fetch the roster (self-scope users never pull the org user list).

## Symptom → diagnosis → fix

- Requester claims a reply is missing → probably an internal note (invisible to them) → agent re-posts publicly.
- Attachment won't open → signed URL expired → click again (a fresh URL is minted per open).
- Assignee missing from the picker → person has no app_users login row → create their login/role at /admin/roles.
- Status/priority lists look wrong → tenant config at /helpdesk/settings.

common_issues.symptom: Can't assign a ticket to a teammate
common_issues.diagnosis: Picker is the org login roster; teammate has no login, or the viewer isn't an agent.
common_issues.fix: Provision the teammate's login at /admin/roles; confirm the viewer's scope is above 'self'.
common_issues.escalate_when: Roster loads but assignment PATCH fails.

pages.permissions_needed: Helpdesk module. Agent actions (assign, status, internal notes) require scope above 'self'.

pages.title: Helpdesk dashboard
pages.user_md:
## Helpdesk Dashboard

Aggregate tiles for the org's tickets: total, open, resolved/closed, average resolution hours, plus breakdowns by lifecycle stage and open-ticket aging. The date-range filter re-queries the aggregates for that window.
pages.support_md:
## How it works

`GET /helpdesk/stats/dashboard?date_from&date_to` — server-side aggregate over tickets (stage mapping comes from the tenant's status config: each status has a lifecycle stage). No store/market/rep dimension by design.

## Symptom → diagnosis → fix

- Numbers don't match the inbox → the inbox has extra filters applied; dashboard is org-wide for the date range.
- Stage buckets look wrong → statuses mapped to the wrong stage in /helpdesk/settings → fix the status's stage.
pages.permissions_needed: Helpdesk module; intended for agents (linked from the inbox for agents).

pages.title: Raise a ticket
pages.user_md:
## Raise a ticket

Describe the issue and submit — a manager/agent picks it up.

- Subject and description are required. Include steps, error messages, and any "Reference:<id>" the app showed you (that id lets support look the failure up directly).
- Category and priority are dropdowns your company configured; store is an optional picker (search by store code).
- Extra fields may appear if your company added custom ones.

You land on the ticket page after submitting; add comments/attachments there.
pages.support_md:
## How it works

`POST /helpdesk/tickets` with category/priority ids from config bootstrap, optional store_code (picked from the storeops roster — pick-don't-type), and custom_fields keyed by field_key. Requester identity comes from the signed-in user. New-ticket notifications go to the category's alert emails or the shared list (/helpdesk/settings).

## Symptom → diagnosis → fix

- Form fails to load ("Failed to load form") → config bootstrap failed → helpdesk module disabled for the org or backend down → escalate.
- Store search finds nothing → storeops store roster empty/unloaded → check /storeops/admin stores exist.
- Submit fails → required custom fields empty or server error → check message; persistent errors go to /failures.

common_issues.symptom: User can't find their store in the picker
common_issues.diagnosis: Store picker lists storeops stores by store_code; the store may be missing from the roster.
common_issues.fix: Leave store blank (optional) and mention it in the description; admin adds the store at /storeops/admin.
common_issues.escalate_when: Roster is populated but the picker stays empty.

pages.permissions_needed: Helpdesk module on the role (any scope — requesters included).

pages.title: Helpdesk settings
pages.user_md:
## Helpdesk Settings

Configure this organization's helpdesk — changes are data, not code, and apply immediately:

- **Categories:** names + per-category **alert emails** (route new-ticket emails, e.g. IT → IT lead). Blank = the shared list on the settings tab.
- **Priorities / Statuses:** keys, labels, colors (statuses also carry a lifecycle stage used by the dashboard).
- **Custom fields:** extra fields on the new-ticket form (text/textarea/select/checkbox/number/date, required flag).
- **Teams:** group agents; add/remove members.
- **Settings:** the shared new-ticket notification email list and other org-level toggles.
pages.support_md:
## How it works

CRUD over `helpdesk/config/*` tables (categories, priorities, statuses, custom-fields, teams, settings), all org-scoped; defaults are seeded per org on first use. Deleting config in use can orphan display values on old tickets (they keep the stored strings). New-ticket notifications resolve: category notify_emails → else shared list.

## Symptom → diagnosis → fix

- New-ticket emails going to nobody → category has no alert emails AND the shared list is empty → set one of them.
- Deleted a status/priority and old tickets look odd → old tickets keep their stored value → recreate the entry or update the tickets.
- Edits blocked → page is intended for admins (inbox links it for admin module / scope all) → adjust role.

common_issues.symptom: IT tickets alert HR (or vice versa)
common_issues.diagnosis: Per-category alert emails misconfigured or falling through to the shared list.
common_issues.fix: Set the correct emails on each category row (comma-separated) — blank falls back to the shared list.
common_issues.escalate_when: Emails configured but never sent (then treat as a notify/email delivery issue).

pages.permissions_needed: Helpdesk module + admin (inbox surfaces the link for admin module or scope 'all').

pages.title: HR
pages.user_md:
**What it's for:** a permission-gated consolidated VIEW of Total Compensation, Employees & Pay,
Payroll, and Time Off — scoped to the signed-in manager's area. **Pay rate is edited here** (moved
off StoreOps Admin) and flows automatically to payroll, total comp, and the employee dashboard.
Bulk pay-rate upload/download supported.

**When to open a ticket:** the `hr` module/nav item is missing for someone who should have it, or
Total Compensation numbers don't match what Payroll shows for the same person/period.
pages.support_md:
**Data sources:** `GET /hr/compensation?org_id&period`, `/storeops/employees`,
`GET /storeops/payroll?month`, `/storeops/time-off`. `PATCH /storeops/employees/{id}` for pay_rate.
**Total comp = base salary (hours × pay_rate) + commission − chargebacks; annualized = total comp ×
12** (formula stated on-page). Commission data here is a READ from the commission engine
(mod-commission owns that calculation).

**Symptom → diagnosis → fix**
- *"HR" module missing from someone's nav*: `hr` is a permission gated OFF by default for managers —
  check/grant the `hr` module key for their role at `/admin/roles`.
- *Total comp doesn't match Payroll Report's actual pay for the same employee/period*: Total Comp
  ADDS commission and SUBTRACTS chargebacks on top of the base wage number — a difference is
  expected unless the employee has $0 commission/chargebacks. Compare **base salary** here to
  **actual pay** on `/storeops/payroll` instead — those two should match.
- *Bulk pay-rate upload updated some rows but not others*: rows need BOTH a matchable
  `employee_id`/`name` AND a non-blank `pay_rate` — check the response message's "skipped" count and
  reasons.
- *"No compensation data for {period}"*: check the period selector (top nav / Period picker) —
  period format must resolve to a real month; an unrecognized/oddly-spelled period yields no rows.

**Escalate when:** base salary here disagrees with actual pay on `/storeops/payroll` for the exact
same employee+month (should be identical) — money-adjacent, escalate to platform operator.

common_issues.symptom: A manager can't see the HR tab/page at all
common_issues.diagnosis: hr is a permission module, OFF by default for managers.
common_issues.fix: Grant the hr module key to their role at /admin/roles.
common_issues.escalate_when: Module is granted and the page still 403s or nav-hides.

common_issues.symptom: Total Compensation numbers don't match Payroll Report for the same person
common_issues.diagnosis: Total Comp includes commission and chargebacks on top of base wages — compare 'base salary' here to 'actual pay' on Payroll instead.
common_issues.fix: Explain the formula difference; if base salary itself disagrees with Payroll's actual pay, that's a real bug.
common_issues.escalate_when: Base salary (not total comp) disagrees with the Payroll Report's actual pay for the identical employee + period.

pages.permissions_needed: Module permission `hr` (off by default for managers) + role scope determines visible area

pages.title: Compliance Document Repository
pages.user_md:
